jobs.title: General coordinator (head of mission) (F/M) - Pakistan
jobs.description:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Pakistan**

MdM France has been operating in Pakistan since 1996, mainly in Punjab and KPK provinces. In Punjab, over the past 30 years, MdM has been implementing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) including family planning and gender based violence projects. Present since 2009 in KP, MdM has been working with the Afghan refugees and internally displaced persons providing essential primary healthcare services including mental health and psychological support. In KP, across the course of the years, we have covered many districts and have built strong acceptance among the local communities and authorities. We have also responded to multiples emergencies including the 2022 and 2025 floods.

For the 2027–2029 period, MdM will continue to focus on advancing on SRHR as the central pillar of all programming in Pakistan. All interventions will be firmly grounded in a comprehensive, integrated, and rights-based SRHR strategy with particular focus on access to family planning services and cervical cancer awareness and screening. Developing specific initiatives focused on cervical cancer would be critical to the mission. Additionally, MdM is monitoring the situation related to humanitarian needs of Afghan refugees in KP and will intend to develop new actions to ensure humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable.

Currently the mission has a portfolio of around 500K€/year, with 20 staffs and 2 offices (coordination in Islamabad and one field office in Mardan/KP). A variety of institutional donors used to support the mission, but the funding environment is currently shrinking, and MdM is covering the mission with core funds. One of the main stakes of 2027 will be to secure new institutional fundings and ensure sustainability of MdM in the country.

**About the role**

As general coordinator, you will supervise the proper implementation of MdM strategy and operations in the country.

One of your main responsibilities is to drive a strategic restructuring of the Pakistan mission, ensuring the transition to a strengthened and autonomous national team.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the desk manager, you are responsible for the overall management of the Pakistan mission.

Your main responsibilities are the following:

- Recruit, manage, train and motivate the mission’s team
- Define the operational and advocacy strategy together with the coordination team, the desk manager and the volunteer board delegates of the mission
- Plan and monitor activities, implement corrective action when necessary, providing technical support to the team
- Represent MdM with authorities, local actors, partners, donors and the media
- Monitor partnership agreements with partners, authorities and donors, seek out and develop new partnerships, and ensure or supervise fundraising
- Ensure the financial coverage of the mission by leading fundraising and budget management
- Draft, adapt and monitor safety regulations and procedures and coordinate crisis management in the region
- Implement and monitor the application of MdM’s programmatic and support services framework, policies and procedures
- Supervise reporting to MdM and donors

**Who you’ll work with**

You will report directly to the Desk Manager based at HQ.

As General Coordinator, you will be the head of the country coordination team and you will manage directly a team composed of: Deputy Coordinator programs, Deputy Coordinator in charge of support services, Medical Advisor, Humanitarian Access and Risks Advisor and Field Coordinator/KP.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have 5+ years' experience in the humanitarian sector, including coordination and expatriate roles
- Have led teams and operations in complex or insecure environments
- Are confident representing an organisation with donors, authorities and humanitarian actors
- Can negotiate effectively, manage risks and oversee security matters
- Bring strong strategic thinking and sound operational judgment
- Have experience with programme, budget and support function management, ideally in health and SRHR
- Enjoy coaching teams, building capacity and developing talent
- Communicate with diplomacy, adapt quickly and lead through uncertainty
- Are comfortable with Microsoft Office and mapping tools
- Are fluent in English

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer stable environments with limited operational or security challenges
- Are uncomfortable making difficult decisions, negotiating or representing an organisation externally
- Prefer specialist or technical roles over broad leadership and management responsibilities
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 664 €
- Fixed-term contract of 6 months starting on January 2027
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in Islamabad with frequent travels to field locations (office in Mardan/KP)

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Individual guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Position Title**: Project Coordinator

**Duty Station**: Nairobi, with missions in Kiambu, Mombasa, Kilifi.

**Gross Salary Range:** KES 130,000 – 150,000 gross per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

**Type of Appointment**: Fixed term, one year with possibility of extension

**Estimated Start Date**: December - January 2026

**The Organisation:**

CEFA – The European Committee for Training and Agriculture is an Italian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 1972, active in several countries across Africa, Latin America, and Eastern Europe. CEFA promotes sustainable and inclusive development through long-term initiatives in agriculture, environment, education, gender equality, and human rights, implemented in partnership with local communities and institutions.

Its work is guided by the values of participation, equality, and social justice, aiming to empower people, especially women and youth, and strengthen their capacity for self-reliance.

**Project Summary**

The project **“TB Free-HIW: To Be Free – Health Inside the Walls”** will be implemented in six correctional institutions across four counties in Kenya (Nairobi, Kiambu, Kilifi, and Mombasa).

The overall objective of the project is to contribute to ending the TB and HIV epidemics by promoting equitable access to integrated prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and support services for people in detention. Specifically, the project aims to:

1. remove systemic, gender-related and human rights-based barriers to healthcare through awareness-raising, advocacy and institutional engagement; and
2. strengthen integrated TB and HIV services, psychosocial support and rehabilitation, including family, community and socioeconomic reintegration during detention and after release.

Under the supervision of the Regional Manager, the **Project Coordinator** will be responsible for coordinating and monitoring CEFA's activities related to awareness-raising and sensitisation to Kenya Prisons Service (KPS) staff, psychosocial support, vocational training and social reintegration. The Coordinator will supervise 2 Social Workers implementing activities within target correctional facilities, coordinate consultants and service providers, and ensure effective collaboration with the KPS, relevant health authorities and project partners.

The Coordinator will ensure timely implementation, quality reporting and compliance with donor requirements and CEFA's internal procedures.

**General Objectives and Responsibilities:**

The Project Coordinator, under the overall supervision of the Regional Manager, is responsible for the planning, coordination, quality assurance and monitoring of the assigned project activities addressing TB and HIV in the Kenyan prison system. The position focuses on removing systemic, gender-related and human-rights-based barriers to healthcare, strengthening awareness among KPS personnel and people in detention, and improving psychosocial support and social reintegration during detention and after release.

The Project Coordinator ensures that the activities are implemented in accordance with approved work plans, project objectives, applicable standards and donor requirements, in coordination with relevant institutional stakeholders, service providers and implementing partners.

**Main Duties**

**1. Coordination, planning and implementation**

- Prepare, update and follow up detailed implementation plans, activity schedules and budget forecasts for the assigned Result 1 and Result 2 activities, in consultation with the Regional Manager and relevant teams.
- Coordinate and oversee the implementation of project activities in target correctional facilities across 4 counties, ensuring quality, timeliness and alignment with project objectives.
- Coordinate awareness-raising initiatives for KPS personnel, relevant authorities and people in detention on TB, HIV, the right to health, prevention, risk reduction and human rights protection.
- Oversee the development of operational protocols and the delivery of training for KPS personnel on psychosocial support and social reintegration of people affected by TB and HIV.
- Coordinate the provision and strengthening of psychosocial support services, including individual and group psychological assistance for people in detention.
- Oversee educational, vocational and income-generating initiatives aimed at strengthening the skills and socioeconomic reintegration prospects of people in detention.
- Coordinate interventions supporting family, healthcare and socioeconomic reintegration, including during the post-release period.
- Coordinate and supervise the work of 2 Social Workers responsible for supporting the implementation of project activities within target correctional facilities, ensuring effective planning, consistent delivery and regular reporting.
- Supervise and coordinate consultants, trainers, service providers and implementing partners, ensuring the quality and timely delivery of assigned activities.
- Prepare monthly activity updates and forecasts of resources needed for implementation, and support timely submission of relevant financial justifications in line with project procedures.

**2. Monitoring and reporting**

- Monitor progress of assigned activities against approved work plans, targets and budgets; identify delays, gaps and risks and propose corrective measures.
- Coordinate collection and verification of activity-level evidence, including attendance records, training outputs, service delivery documentation and follow-up information, with appropriate confidentiality safeguards.
- Monitor the implementation and uptake of operational protocols, KPS training, psychosocial support and reintegration activities, documenting achievements and practical challenges.
- Contribute to periodic internal and donor reports with accurate narrative updates, results, challenges, lessons learned and supporting documentation.
- Participate in field monitoring visits and coordination meetings, and follow up agreed action points.

**3. Technical assistance and quality assurance**

- Support development and adaptation of awareness-raising and training materials on the right to health, TB and HIV, prevention, gender and human rights, psychosocial support and reintegration.
- Provide coordination and technical follow-up for the preparation of psychosocial support and reintegration protocols, ensuring appropriate review by competent specialists and institutional counterparts.
- Promote person-centred, non-discriminatory, gender-responsive and rights-based approaches across activities, with due attention to confidentiality, informed participation and protection from stigma.
- Facilitate exchanges of experience and lessons learned among KPS personnel, service providers, partners and project teams to improve continuity of support during detention and after release.
- Identify capacity-building needs and support follow-up coaching or refresher sessions where required.

**4. Synergies and representation**

- Maintain regular operational coordination with KPS, relevant prison and health departments at county level, and other institutional actors involved in the assigned activities.
- Support advocacy and stakeholder dialogue at county and national levels on barriers to equitable TB and HIV services in the prison system, within the project mandate and in coordination with the Regional Manager.
- Promote linkages between prison-based services, psychosocial support, healthcare referrals, family support and post-release community reintegration mechanisms.
- Participate in relevant technical meetings and coordination forums as delegated, ensuring consistent communication and follow-up.
- Perform other duties related to the assigned project objectives as requested by the Regional Manager.

**Requirements**

- Minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in project coordination or management, preferably in projects related to public health, human rights, psychosocial support, or social inclusion.
- Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Public Health, Social Work, Psychology, International Development, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience in coordinating field activities, supervising staff, and managing relationships with implementing partners, service providers, institutional stakeholders.
- Previous experience working with the KPS, correctional institutions, or other related public authorities.
- Strong understanding of human rights-based and gender-sensitive approaches to healthcare, particularly in correctional settings.
- Good knowledge of TB and HIV-related challenges, particularly among vulnerable and marginalized populations will be considered a strong asset.
- Experience in psychosocial support, community reintegration, vocational training, or livelihood interventions for vulnerable populations will be considered an asset.
- Excellent command of spoken and written English and Kiswahili.
- Thorough knowledge of the Kenyan context, particularly in the target counties (Nairobi, Kiambu, Kilifi, and Mombasa).
- Strong organizational, interpersonal, and networking skills, with the ability to establish and maintain constructive relationships with government institutions, correctional authorities, and other stakeholders.
- Previous experience working on internationally funded development projects, preferably with Italian Cooperation or other institutional donors, will be considered an asset.
- Valid driving licence (Category B or equivalent), with demonstrated driving experience, is mandatory.

jobs.title: Operations Director – Afghanistan
jobs.description:
**Job Title: Operations Director**

**Reports to: Country Director**

**Terms:** This is a 24-month, replacement role with non-accompanied terms.

**Location:** Taloqan, Afghanistan

**Salary:** GB7 €51,861 - €57,623

**Requirements:** The role is based in Taloqan, Afghanistan with frequent travel between Kabul, Taloqan, Kunduz and Badakhshan.

**Role Purpose:** You will be responsible for the overall management of Concern Afghanistan support functions, which comprise administration, HR, and logistics including procurement, warehousing and fleet management. You will ensure appropriate systems are in place to meet programme needs, while ensuring the effective and efficient use of Concern’s resources. As a member of the Country Management Team, you will provide strategic direction to Concern Afghanistan. You will also supervise security management in country.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic leadership - as part of the Country Management team**

- Contribute actively to the Country Management Team (CMT), the Country Strategic Plan and other country-level strategies, including emergency readiness and security planning. Translate country priorities and programme needs into coherent operational plans, systems and resourcing decisions.
- Advise the Country Director and CMT on operational risk, organisational capacity, compliance, access, cost and value for money.
- Represent the operations of Concern in Afghanistan with authorities at provincial and when needed at central (Kabul) level.
- Represent Concern in relevant operational coordination forums and build constructive relationships with peers and external stakeholders. Ensure support functions are prepared to scale and adapt for emergency response and participate actively in responses when required.

**External engagement, legal compliance and inclusive operations**

- Lead and coordinate engagement and representation with provincial and national authorities, including relevant authorities in Kabul, on operational, legal, access and administrative matters.
- Ensure timely organisational registration, licenses, permits, visas, work and travel authorisations, and compliance with applicable national legal and administrative requirements.
- Oversee legal advice and, with the Country Director, the management of legal matters affecting Concern’s operations.
- Negotiate, maintain and monitor appropriate arrangements that enable female staff to access offices and participate safely and meaningfully in Concern’s work.
- Identify and proactively manage constraints affecting female staff access and operations, escalating significant risks and decisions through the appropriate management and security channels.
- Ensure government authorisations and related commitments are tracked, implemented and renewed in a timely manner.

**Security, access, risk and assurance**

- Lead security and operational access management as Concern Afghanistan’s National Security Focal Point, working with field focal points and programme teams.
- Ensure the Security Management Plan and relevant procedures remain current, context-appropriate, understood and implemented, and that offices and international staff residences meet required security, health and safety standards.
- Participate in relevant security and access forums, maintain appropriate information flows and support timely decisions when conditions change.
- Ensure risk management, governance and internal controls operate effectively, audits are completed as required, and agreed recommendations are implemented.
- Assure compliance with Concern and donor requirements across support functions, and escalate material risks to the Country Director and CMT.

**People Management**

- Lead, develop and hold accountable the managers and teams responsible for HR, administration, logistics, procurement, fleet, facilities, assets and IT, ensuring clear priorities and effective collaboration with programme and finance colleagues. Ensuring Concern is fully compliant with national employment legislation and requirements and global HR policies and procedures and identify strategic training development.
- Ensuring staff are trained on Safeguarding and that mechanisms to report and reduce potential for abuse are functioning effectively,
- Promote an inclusive staffing structure including gender, ethnicities etc.
- Ensuring an effective performance development review (PDR) system is in place and ongoing training is provided to line managers and staff.

**Operational delivery and resource stewardship**

- Ensure reliable, efficient and accountable support services for all programme locations, including administration, facilities, travel, transport, fleet, procurement, contracting, warehousing, assets, communications and IT.
- Oversee procurement planning, tendering and contracting so that goods and services are delivered transparently, competitively, on time and with value for money.
- Ensure stores, assets, vehicles, offices and accommodation are safe, fit for purpose, properly controlled and managed in line with Concern and donor requirements.
- Lead planning and monitoring of support-function budgets and national staff costs, address significant variances and identify responsible efficiencies.
- Use management information to monitor operational performance, service quality and emerging constraints, and agree corrective action with relevant managers.

**Accountability**

- Promote and ensure compliance with Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) commitments and quality criteria
- Ensure that all staff are familiar with the principles underpinning accountability, safeguarding and Concern's Complaints and Response Mechanism (CRM) and ensure that information about Concern's commitments on accountability and safeguarding are disseminated among programme participants and communities
- Ensure that the CRM is functional, effectively implemented and accessible in all programme locations, enabling safe reporting of both programmatic and sensitive complaints, including safeguarding concerns
- Ensure that complaints are welcomed, managed and responded to in a timely, fair and appropriate manner; ensure that sensitive complaints, including safeguarding concerns, are handled with utmost confidentiality and that the safety of the complainants and those affected is prioritised at all stages.

**Other**

- Any other related duties as assigned by the Country Director
- Adhere fully to the commitments and rules of Concern’s Code of Conduct and its Associated policies, including the respect of confidentiality.

**Role Holder Requirements:**

- Relevant degree or equivalent professional experience in operations, management, supply chain, HR, administration or a related field.
- Substantial senior operational leadership experience in an INGO, humanitarian organisation or comparable complex international setting, including leadership through managers and multidisciplinary teams.
- Depth of expertise in at least one operational function, with sufficient breadth to lead HR, administration, logistics, procurement, fleet, facilities, assets and IT through specialist teams.
- Demonstrated ability to design, strengthen and assure operational systems that enable programme delivery and meet organisational, legal and donor requirements.
- Experience engaging and negotiating with government authorities and other external stakeholders on sensitive operational, legal, access or administrative matters.
- Experience managing security and operational access in an insecure, volatile or highly constrained context.
- Strong risk, internal control, compliance, resource-planning and budget-management capability.
- Proven leadership, communication, negotiation, judgement and prioritisation skills, including the ability to make timely decisions under pressure.
- Fluent written and spoken English.
- Willingness and ability to be based in Taloqan and travel frequently between Kabul, Taloqan, Kunduz and Badakhshan
- Commitment to safeguarding, equality, accountability, Concern’s values and inclusive ways of working.
- Empathy with Concern’s vision, mission, goal and objectives and commitment to capacity building, protection and participation.

**Desirable**

- Previous experience in a context with comparable regulatory, access and security constraints to Afghanistan
- Experience working with Concern Worldwide and knowledge of its policies and procedures.

jobs.title: CLINICAL TRIAL PROJECT MANAGEMENT CONSULTANT
jobs.description:
**Location: Latin América Countries**

**Objective of the assignment**

The Consultant will provide specialized clinical project management services in support of specifically assigned Phase II/III clinical trial activities within the CL program, with responsibility for the agreed deliverables described in this ToR and autonomy regarding the organization and execution of the services.

Working across multidisciplinary teams, the Project Manager will take ownership of assigned activities, proactively manage risks and timelines, and facilitate collaboration among internal functions, CROs, investigators, and external partners. The individual will also support the Head of Disease in selected scientific and programmatic activities, ensuring alignment with the overall priorities of the CL program

**Tasks and responsibilities**

***1st area - Clinical trial planning and coordination***

- Provide specialized project management services related to the planning, implementation and follow-up of the Phase II/III clinical trials specifically assigned under this consultancy, including the preparation and maintenance of agreed project management deliverables. Monitor trial progress against milestones and proactively identify potential delays or risks.
- Develop and maintain study timelines, project plans, trackers, and key deliverables to ensure timely follow-up and escalation where appropriate.
- Ensure trial activities comply with ICH-GCP and relevant regional and international regulatory requirements, including EMA/FDA requirements.
- Support study governance and contribute to effective project execution.

***2nd area - Cross-functional project management***

- Provide specialized technical input and coordinate activities with relevant DNDi functions and external partners in relation to the specific clinical trial deliverables covered by this assignment, without exercising line-management or hierarchical authority over DNDi personnel. Facilitate alignment of study objectives, timelines, deliverables, and dependencies across teams.
- Organize project team meetings, governance meetings, and study-related workshops, including agendas, minutes, and follow-up actions.

***3rd area - Study documentation***

- Lead the development and maintenance of key clinical study documents, including, but not limited to:
- Clinical study protocols
- Informed consent forms
- Monitoring plans
- Manuals of operations
- Risk management plans
- Clinical study reports.

***4th area - Vendor, CRO coordination***

- Provide technical and project coordination services in relation to CROs, vendors and external service providers involved in the assigned clinical studies, monitoring agreed deliverables and milestones and reporting relevant issues to the designated DNDi technical focal point.
- Track external deliverables and support issue resolution in collaboration with relevant functional leads and/or team members.
- Coordinate activities with relevant internal and external stakeholders involved in trial delivery.
- Provide oversight and coordinate tasks related to clinical trial supplies within the scope of the assigned studies, including identification and reporting of potential supply-related risks or issues Provide training during Site Initiation Visits (SIVs) and investigator meetings.

***5th area - External partner engagement***

- Provide specialized technical and scientific support for engagement activities with Ministries of Health (MoH), the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), academic institutions, and other relevant stakeholders, specifically in relation to the clinical research activities and deliverables defined under this consultancy.
- Promotes the Leishmaniasis Network (RedeLEISH) development in the region, in coordination with Head of the Disease and RedeLEISH Coordinator.

***6th area - Regulatory, Data Quality and Operational Support***

- Coordinate Ethics Committee and Regulatory Authority submissions for assigned projects, ensuring compliance with applicable national regulatory requirements.
