**Position Number**: 5JOED0029PA

**Grade**: NO-A

**Parent Sector**: Education Sector (ED)

**Duty Station**: Amman

**Job Family**: Education

**Contract Type**: Project Appointment

**Duration of contract**: 1 year

**Recruitment open to**: Internal and external candidates

**Application deadline (Midnight Paris Time)**: 18/11/2026

## **ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT**

UNESCO supports national institutions and stakeholders in Jordan to strengthen inclusive, equitable and labour-market-responsive education and skills systems, with particular attention to technical and vocational education and training (TVET), youth employment and lifelong learning.

UNESCO and the International Labour Organization (ILO) will jointly implement the European Union-funded TVET for Decent Work in Jordan project. The 36-month initiative seeks to strengthen the coherence, quality, inclusiveness and labour-market relevance of Jordan’s TVET system and improve pathways to decent work for women, youth, persons with disabilities and groups in vulnerable situations.

The project works primarily at policy, institutional and system levels. UNESCO’s responsibilities include support to TVET governance and inter-institutional coordination; data and evidence systems; quality assurance, accreditation and qualifications; institutional capacity development; work-based learning (WBL); employer engagement; career guidance; graduate tracking; and pathways from secondary TVET into tertiary education. Capacity development will emphasize sustainable institutional arrangements, including training-of-trainers and other approaches that enable national institutions and providers to replicate and scale project-supported practices.

The Associate National Project Officer will support the day-to-day implementation, monitoring, documentation and stakeholder follow-up of UNESCO-led activities. The incumbent will work under close supervision and within approved workplans, budgets, technical guidance and procedures. The role supports, rather than independently leads, policy reform, high-level negotiation or strategic project management.

## **KEY ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

Under the overall authority of the Head of the UNESCO Jordan Office, the technical guidance and the oversight of the Head of the Education Unit, and the direct supervision of the designated TVET Project Officer , the incumbent will be responsible for carrying out the following functions:

**1. Implementation planning and follow-up**

- Support implementation of UNESCO-led activities in line with the approved Project Document, results framework, annual workplans, budgets and timelines.
- Prepare and update activity schedules, action trackers, deliverable calendars, mission plans and implementation records.
- Follow up with counterparts, consultants, partners and service providers on agreed actions and deadlines, and promptly flag delays or bottlenecks to the supervisor.
- Support logistical and substantive preparation of consultations, workshops, institutional capacity-development activities, missions and project meetings.

**2. Institutional and technical support**

- Provide research, drafting and coordination support for institutional strengthening activities related to TVET governance, WBL, quality assurance, qualifications, data systems, career guidance, employer engagement and graduate tracking.
- Support national institutions and TVET providers in applying project-supported tools, guidelines, standard operating procedures and capacity-development packages.
- Support the preparation and implementation of training-of-trainers approaches, including participant coordination, training documentation, feedback collection and follow-up on institutional cascade plans.
- Help ensure that gender equality, disability inclusion, learner-centred approaches, safeguarding, digital and green skills, and decent-work principles are reflected in implementation materials and activities.
- Review routine technical and operational documentation for completeness and consistency, consolidate comments, and refer substantive policy or quality issues to the responsible technical lead.

**3. Partnerships and coordination**

- Maintain regular working-level liaison with designated focal points in relevant ministries and institutions, including MoEHRD/MoE, MoL, VTC, AQAC, Sector Skills Councils, TVET providers, employers’ and workers’ organizations, universities and civil society organizations.
- Support coordination with ILO and other implementing and development partners, including preparation of agendas, background notes, minutes and action points.
- Support the secretariat functions of project governance and technical coordination mechanisms and systematically follow up agreed actions.
- Contribute to coordination with EU-funded and other TVET initiatives to promote complementarity and avoid duplication.

**4. Consultants, partners and operational processes**

- Support preparation of terms of reference, scopes of work, technical specifications and other implementation documents using approved templates and guidance.
- Maintain trackers for contracts, deliverables, review processes and payment milestones, and alert the supervisor to deviations from agreed schedules or requirements.
- Coordinate routine inputs and information required by consultants, implementing partners and service providers.
- Work with finance, procurement, administration and programme colleagues to initiate and follow up authorized procurement, contracting, travel and payment actions.

**5. Monitoring, risk management and reporting**

- Collect, verify, organize and consolidate monitoring data and supporting evidence against approved indicators and targets, with required disaggregation.
- Maintain implementation, risk, issue and results trackers and support follow-up of agreed mitigation measures.
- Draft implementation updates and contribute data, evidence, lessons learned and success stories for internal and donor reports, reviews, evaluations and audits.
- Support institutional monitoring of the uptake and use of project-supported tools and training, including ToT cascade and follow-up actions.

**6. Communication and knowledge management**

- Draft correspondence, briefing notes, meeting records, presentations, technical summaries and other project materials in English and Arabic.
- Support compliance with UNESCO and EU communication and visibility requirements in coordination with relevant colleagues.
- Maintain complete, accurate and accessible electronic and hard-copy project records to support accountability and institutional memory.
- Perform other related duties within the scope and level of the position, as assigned.

## **COMPETENCIES - Core (C) & Managerial (M)**

- Communication (C)
- Accountability (C)
- Innovation (C)
- Knowledge sharing and continuous improvement (C)
- Planning and organizing (C)
- Results focus (C)
- Teamwork (C)
- Professionalism (C)

For detailed information, please consult the [UNESCO Competency Framework](https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000245056/PDF/245056qaa.pdf.multi).

## **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

**EDUCATION**

- Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in education, TVET, skills development, public policy, international development, social sciences, project management or a related field.

**WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Less than two years of relevant professional experience in education, TVET, skills development, employment, project implementation, institutional capacity development or a related field.
- Experience supporting coordination, monitoring, reporting or delivery of multi-stakeholder projects.

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES**

- Knowledge of Jordan’s education, TVET, skills and employment landscape and relevant national institutions.
- Basic understanding of institutional capacity development, TVET governance, WBL, quality assurance, qualifications, career guidance or labour-market-responsive skills development.
- Ability to apply project cycle management and results-based management principles to routine implementation and monitoring tasks.
- Strong planning, organization, follow-up, analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail.
- Ability to draft clear workplans, trackers, minutes, briefs, presentations and reports in English and Arabic.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural team and maintain constructive working relationships with public institutions and diverse stakeholders.
- Good digital skills, including office productivity, collaboration, presentation and basic data-management tools.
- Commitment to integrity, accountability, gender equality, disability inclusion and respect for diversity.

**LANGUAGES**

- Excellent knowledge of Arabic and English, written and spoken, is required.

## **DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS**

**WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Experience with UNESCO, another United Nations entity, the European Union or an international development programme.
- Experience supporting institutional or system-strengthening work in TVET, WBL, teacher or trainer development, ToT, quality assurance, qualifications, career guidance, private-sector engagement or graduate tracking.
- Experience supporting procurement, contracts, financial follow-up, donor reporting or project monitoring.
- Familiarity with EU-funded project implementation and visibility requirements

jobs.description:
**Background:**

Displacement in Somalia remains a complex and protracted challenge affecting millions of displaced people and returning refugees. NRC responds through integrated, multi-sectoral and area-based approaches that not only meet immediate needs but address systemic barriers preventing displaced people from progressing towards durable solutions. This response is also closely aligned with influencing and enabling the implementation of policies that promote greater inclusion and rights of displacement affected communities in both countries. The Durable Solutions (DS) Programme Manager provides strategic leadership and technical expertise, coordinates funding and partnerships, engages key stakeholders, and supports policy and advocacy efforts to achieve sustainable outcomes for displacement-affected communities.

**What you will do:**

The overall purpose of the Durable Solutions (DS) Programme Manager position is to lead and oversee the implementation of NRC's Durable Solutions programming in Somalia. The position provides strategic leadership, technical guidance, and managerial oversight to ensure the effective delivery, quality, and growth of the Durable Solutions portfolio. The DS programme manager may also provide support to NRC Kenya programme on ad-hoc basis.

The DS Programme Manager is responsible for managing and strengthening the capacity of programme teams, providing strategic direction and technical guidance on the design and implementation of DS programming, ensuring the development of timely, high-quality proposals, reports, and programme documentation, and maintaining compliance with NRC standards and donor requirements. The role also represents NRC externally, builds and sustains strategic partnerships with key stakeholders and coordination fora, and coordinates resource mobilization efforts to support the expansion and sustainability of the Durable Solutions portfolio.

General Responsibilities:

1. To be responsible for providing technical support to colleagues working on DS programmes and develop relevant DS training including coaching of newly recruited staff to ensure they meet NRC’s standards. Also contribute to the induction of new staff with a role in the DS project implementation processes.
2. Assume overall responsibility of coordinating and managing the DS programme design and implementation (activities, budget and project documentation) in line with proposals, strategies and donor requirements.
3. Responsible for Overall backstopping of DS program staff to ensure integrated and area-based programming is realized within NRC DS operation areas and closely support and coordinate DS programmes.
4. Compliance to donor standards, and grant management and regular reporting to donor in Country Office
5. Ensure compliance with contractual commitments and extracting, documenting and implementing key learnings from project implementation

Specific responsibilities:

- Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight of all new and existing projects and activities within the Country Durable Solutions portfolio throughout the project cycle, ensuring project design, start-up, implementation, monitoring, and close-out are aligned with NRC quality standards and donor requirements.
- Work with NRC Country and Area Programme teams, including CC Specialists, Managers, and Coordinators, both remotely and on-site, to develop and apply context-specific technical solutions for Durable Solutions programming, policy influence and strategic planning.
- Support the application of standards, best practices, partnership approaches, programme tools, and MEAL systems to ensure high-quality programme implementation and evidence-based decision-making.
- Lead programme learning, information management, research, and evidence-generation initiatives, identifying opportunities for learning and innovation and facilitating the documentation and dissemination of lessons learned and good practices.
- Promote the integration of innovations, best practices, and programme learning into programme design, implementation, and strategic decision-making to improve programme quality and impact.

**Please read the** [**full Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDmGBbZc4zTQpPhkkfE_P5eAX8p5o8IeXlZ_3VZEPXnxsc?e=jkF1j6) **as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

**Generic professional competencies:**

- Minimum first level university degree in Development Economics, Social Sciences or other relevant fields.
- Demonstrated flexibility and the ability to work under pressure in a complex and changing environment.
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts
- Knowledge of the displacement context(s) in Somalia
- Experience with returns and reintegration programmes
- Documented results in project and program management
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal
- Resilient, with the ability to live and work in a complex, insecure and challenging context.

**Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Minimum of 5 years’ experience from a senior level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- In-depth knowledge of the main protection and humanitarian standards and legal frameworks.
- Significant work experience in INGOs or UN in assisting IDPs, refugees and returnees with a focus on durable solutions.
- Clear understanding of durable solutions, self-reliance, and related concepts, and experience designing and implementing integrated approaches which effectively advance them.
- Experience in ensuring programming aligns with and contributes to inclusive policy implementation.
- Experience in building strong coalitions and strong networks and designing programs and resource mobilization for multi-year programs in an international environment.
- Solid budgeting skills and understanding of working with multiple donors including FCDO, EU, WB, SIDA, DANIDA, and others.
- Strong experience working in a partnership model and establishing and maintaining coordination and communication systems at inter-agency level
- Knowledge of the context in Somalia and Horn of Africa in general.
- Experience with start-up, exit or similar

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Any of the NRC’s area offices (Mogadishu, Kismayo, Galkayo or Hargeisa) **(national contract)**
- Contract: Fixed Term **national contact.**
- Travel: *50%*
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **national** salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
- **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
- **Your most updated Cover Letter**
- **Do not attach certificates or any other documents from the two mentioned above.**
- **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Somalia. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency permits.
- **If the internal pool is competitive, NRC will prioritize the assessment of internal staff before reviewing applications from external candidates.**
- **Qualified female candidates are particularly encouraged to apply.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Area Manager Ouaddaï – Tchad
jobs.description:
**Lieu : Adré, Est du Tchad**
**Date souhaitée de démarrage : 04/01/2027**
**Durée de contrat : 6 mois (renouvelable)**

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org/).

**CONTEXTE :**
Le Tchad fait partie du programme régional Sahel et Afrique de l’Ouest (SAO), qui couvre également le Bénin, le Burkina Faso, le Mali, le Niger, le Sénégal et le Togo. Dans ce cadre, la mission s’appuie sur une organisation régionale favorisant la mutualisation des ressources, l’harmonisation des pratiques et la coordination des expertises, au service de la qualité et de l’efficacité des interventions.

HI est présent au Tchad de façon discontinue depuis les années 1990 et de façon permanente depuis 2014.

HI intervient aujourd’hui à N’Djamena mais aussi dans les provinces de Borkou au Nord, du Ouaddaï et de Wadi Fira à l’Est, du Mandoul et du Langone Oriental au Sud et enfin du Kanem, du Lac et de Barh-El-Gazel à l’Ouest.

Les principaux secteurs d’intervention actuels sont les suivants :

- La réadaptation fonctionnelle et la thérapie de stimulation en complément des réponses nutritionnelles ;
- L’éducation inclusive et l’éducation en contexte d’urgence avec la protection de l’enfance ;
- L’insertion socio-économique des ménages les plus vulnérables notamment à travers le développement d’AGR, et la formation professionnelle ainsi qu’une assistance en urgence ;
- La SMSPS ;
- La mutualisation de stockage
- La transformation de conflits et la cohésion sociale.

HI intervient à l’Est depuis avril 2023, où nous implémentons plusieurs projets d’urgence et de résilience contribuant à la réponse humanitaire à la crise Soudanaise auprès des populations réfugiées, déplacées, retournées et hôtes vulnérables. Les opérations de HI à l’Est du Tchad mobilisent actuellement plus de 110 employés répartis entre les bases opérationnelles suivantes :

- Equipe du Ouaddaï - Bureau de Adré dans la ville de Adré et une équipe projet basée à Abéché.
- Equipe du Wadifira - Bureau de Guéréda dans la ville de Guéréda et une équipe projet basée à Iriba.

**VOTRE MISSION :**
Sous la supervision hiérarchique directe de L’Operations Manager, l’Area Manager Ouaddaï sera basé à Adré (Ouaddaï). Des déplacements réguliers sur le terrain sont à prévoir pour suivre et accompagner l’extension de nos activités. Des déplacements très occasionnels aux bureaux de coordination en capitale sont également à prévoir.

L’Area Manager Ouaddaï, en lien avec les responsables de service basés au bureau de coordination, aura notamment pour mission de :

Mission 1 : Management

- Être capable d'accompagner les membres des équipes opérationnelles, techniques et support de sa zone dans leur progression : développer l'autonomie de ses collaborateurs.
- Savoir se positionner pour faire avancer les choses.
- Savoir simplifier et prioriser.

Mission 2 : Stratégie et pilotage

- Contribuer à l'élaboration de la stratégie opérationnelle du programme, à sa mise en œuvre et à son suivi annuel dans sa zone tout en tenant compte de l’évolution rapide du contexte humanitaire et sécuritaire.
- Contribuer à la transformation organisationnelle, notamment par l'évolution des pratiques managériales, l'amélioration continue et l'optimisation des processus de travail.

Mission 3 : Standards et expertise

- Assurer le déploiement et le respect des règles et cadres globaux (HI et bailleurs) et notamment de la politique qualité projet (PQP)
- Assurer le déploiement et le respect des normes et politiques institutionnelles de HI (PSEAH, Code de Conduite, Fraude et Corruption…)

Mission 4 : Mise en œuvre opérationnelle

- Assurer la bonne gestion et le suivi des projets sous sa responsabilité.
- Contribuer au suivi et à l'analyse des opportunités et des risques potentiels et proposer des mesures d'atténuation, le cas échéant.
- Développer le rayonnement externe de HI (forums, alliances opérationnelles et stratégiques, etc.) et la représentation externe de l'organisation (partenariats, consortium, événements, médias) dans sa zone.

Mission 5 : Collaboration avec le programme Soudan

- Favoriser la collaboration avec HI-Soudan, d’un point de vue RH et logistique, mais également en termes d’analyse contextuelle et sécuritaire ainsi que le cas échant opérationnel et de relation bailleur.

Mission 6 : Autres

- Agir en tant que représentant légal de HI en interne et en externe auprès des autorités locales, et promouvoir une excellente réputation et une image positive de HI dans sa zone.
- Coordonner, en liens fonctionnels, les équipes Support (RH, Log, Finance) afin de garantir la qualité et l'adéquation des ressources aux besoins dans sa zone ; certaines ressources sont partagées avec la base d’Adré et cela requiert une forte coordination avec l’Area manager Est.
- Soutenir le Directeur de Pays et le Humanitarian Access and Security Manager (HASM) dans le suivi de la sécurité des biens et du personnel de HI dans sa zone et garantir l'adéquation des ressources au contexte.
- Assurer la bonne collaboration et la complémentarité avec le programme HI Soudan

Et remplir toutes autres missions qui pourraient être confiées par le Operations Manager ou le Directeur Pays.

**SPECIFICITES/PARTICULARITES DU POSTE :**

- Adré est une base frontalière de l’Est tchadien, proche du Soudan, dans un environnement nettement plus isolé et opérationnel que N’Djamena : les options de loisirs et de services (restaurants, commerces, activités sportives) y sont limitées et la vie sociale expatriée y est réduite.

**VOTRE PROFIL :**

- Vous avez une solide expérience en tant que Coordinateur de programmes, Coordinateur Terrain,
- Vous avez déjà eu à gérer plusieurs bases et de multiples zones d’interventions, dans un contexte volatile,
- Vous avez une bonne connaissance de la gestion de la sécurité,
- Vous avez une bonne expérience en tant que manager avec parfois des équipes à distance,

**CONDITIONS :**

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle : [https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi](https://hi.org/fr/travailler-chez-hi)

- Contrat International de **6 mois** (renouvelable) **à compter idéalement du 04/01/2027** ;
- Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :
- Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE ;
- Assurance retraite ;
- Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé ;
- **Salaire** : à partir de 2869 € brut/mois ; selon expérience professionnelle ;
- **Perdiem** : 824 € net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;
- **Hardship :** 500 € net/mois
- **Congés payés** : 25 jours par an ;
- **R&R** : 5 Jours toutes les 8 semaines => + prise en charge éventuelle transport/forfait ;
- **Poste non-accompagné**
- Logement : Collectif pris en charge par HI ;
- Si vous êtes résident(e) dans le pays : package local.

jobs.title: Projects and Partnerships Support Assistant ( Re-advertised)
jobs.description:
## **Mission**

The REACH team – based in Damascus – has been supporting the humanitarian response in Syria since 2013 through the implementation of various assessments, including yearly Multi-Sector Needs Assessments (MSNAs), Humanitarian Situation Monitoring, Joint Market Monitoring Initiative, Area-Based Assessments, and other assessments as necessary. REACH is continuing to explore new and innovative ways to effectively inform the humanitarian and early recovery responses in Syria.

Under the direct supervision of the IMPACT Country Representative (CR) and technical supervision of the IMPACT Regional Projects and Partnerships Manager (RPPSM), the REACH PPSA is responsible for supporting the identification, development and management of grants within the IMPACT/REACH Syria mission. The ideal candidate would be eager to work within a dynamic and motivated team and will have a clear focus on project development as a tool to improve the efficacy of the humanitarian and recovery response in Syria. The priorities will be determined together with the RPPSM and the CR.

NUMBER OF REQUIRED CANDIDATES: 1
Damascus

**OBJECTIVES**

Grant management

- Proposal development and contracting with donor agencies
- Continuous follow-up of project implementation and progress against contractual requirements
- Contractual reporting; deadline guardkeeping
- Support to formalisation of downstream/unfunded partnerships and due diligence / vetting of partners

Support to positioning and fundraising

- Support to day-to-day coordination with sister organisation, Acted
- Stakeholder analysis; donor mapping
- Regular monitoring of funding opportunities for Syria

Cross-cutting: Filing and archiving of all relevant documentation on dedicated server and database

**FUNCTIONS**

**SUPPORT TO Positioning and Fundraising**

All of the below tasks are in support of the CR, and involvement may vary according to the profile, seniority and context.
**1.1 Context Analysis**

- Support to analysis of Syria’s socio-economic situation, (donor) trends, funding trends, needs and gaps. Regularly conduct stakeholder analysis, who does what and where.
**1.2 Strategy development and Fundraising**
- Based on the IMPACT country strategy, support the identification of funding opportunities and donors to ensure funding continuity as well as support the diversification of IMPACT’s donor portfolio through tracking funding opportunities, also potentially engaging with donors and donor working groups.
- In line with IMPACT strategy and expertise, contribute to partners mapping, to support identifying potential relevant international and/or local partners (academia, think tanks, national and international NGOs, private sector partners, etc.) as well as funding opportunities in Syria
**1.3 External relations**
- In coordination with the CR, support the overall cooperation with Acted in relation to project development and grants management ensuring communication is regular and timely and synergies are sought and built.
- Contribute to establishing, maintaining and improving active and regular working relationships with donors and, where relevant, act as point of contact for formal/informal donor communication.
- Establish, maintain and improve active and regular working relationships with IMPACT partners, NGOs, UN agencies, relevant working groups, consortia and academia in relation to project implementation and proposal development.
- Maintain an up to date directory of donors, international and local NGOs, other partners and stakeholders.
- Ensure fundraising activities are appropriately tracked in the Funding Tracker (or similar tool), which is updated on a regular basis to log latest negotiations and proposal possibilities with donors

**Grant Management**

**2.1 Proposal Development**

- Oversee project proposal conceptualisation, and the development of other fundraising documents (e.g. expressions of interest, concept notes) in line with IMPACT country strategy, donor requirements and in close collaboration with IMPACT/Acted, as well at the IMPACT HQ and Regional Projects and Partnerships Support (PPS) and Finance teams.
- Liaise with the CR, Research Managers and other relevant departments to ensure proposals are relevant and technically sound, as well as with other internal stakeholders such as Finance for the budget and other budget related documents (e.g. budget narrative)
- Ensure validation of all proposals before submission to IMPACT HQ PPS / RPPSM, and validation from IMPACT HQ PPS / RPPSM, as well as relevant HQ partner’s through partner’s field focal point (where relevant) is sought.
- Address and coordinate the timely response and submission to all comments by donors on proposals in liaison with relevant staff in country, IMPACT HQ PPS / RPPSM and Finance teams.

**2. 2 Contracting**
- In coordination with the CR and IMPACT HQ PPS / RPPSM, review/negotiate proposals and/or contracts with donors, ensuring requirements are clear and understood.
- Contribute to due diligence exercises of funding partners in liaison with HQ PPS / RPPSM.
**2.3 Project Implementation and Follow up**
- Ensure the timely completion of grant related processes such as the Reporting Deadline Tracker.
- Ensure timely kick-off meetings are held involving all project components and focal points. Ensure the establishment and regular update of project progress, key findings and success stories (including key M&E findings – where relevant).
- Ensure that all contractual obligations are clearly defined and communicated internally in terms of deliverables as well as narrative and financial reporting requirements, in close coordination with HQ PPS / RPPSM and (as relevant) with Acted’s Project Development (grants) and Finance departments.
- When any issue is identified in meeting contractual deliverables/requirements in the given timeframe and budget, inform relevant staff in country and suggest potential solutions that would meet donor rules. Ensure ad-hoc requests from donors are addressed in liaison with the CR, Research and Support teams.
**2.4 Reporting**
- Oversee the development of quality project narrative and M&E reports (in support of donors’ requests), reflecting the progress and status of projects in a transparent, timely and professional manner, in liaison with IMPACT HQ PPS / RPPSM and Finance.
- In a timely manner and well ahead of contractual deadlines, liaise with Research teams when preparing reports, and with Finance to ensure coherence and alignment between financial and narrative reports by crosschecking the matching of data in the narrative and financial reports.
- Oversee the monthly PPS check and ensure smooth and regular communication with IMPACT HQ PPS / RPPSM.
- Where relevant, ensure regular coordination with Acted’s Project Development, Finance and other departments at all stages of project development and implementation, including consultations for donor discussions, participation in project kick off and lessons learnt meetings, and drafting of donor reports or amendment requests.

**Ad hoc & Cross-cutting**

- Other tasks falling within his/her functions as requested by the CR and IMPACT HQ PPS.

In relation with all aforementioned tasks, ensure continuous and rigorous filing and archiving of key documentation and information, via IMPACT’s dedicated online server and project database. Implement and oversee the country-specific filing system for grant management, under the technical guidance of the RPPSM.

**TECHNICAL SKILLS**

Academic:

- Excellent academic qualifications, preferably including a Bachelor / Master’s degree in relevant discipline or demonstrable skills in this area.

Work experience:

- At least 1 year of relevant work experience in project development, grant management, partnerships management or M&E in humanitarian or development organisations.
- Grant management with institutional humanitarian donors is a definite asset.

Language / Communication skills:

- Excellent spoken and written communication skills in English and Arabic.

Communication/reporting skills:

- Coordination, organisational and planning skills required, including ability to manage large workloads with attention to detail, effectively meet deadlines, through an ex cellent ability to multi-task and prioritise in complex environment.

Level of independence:

- Ability and willingness to work autonomously.

Software skills:

- Applicant must have strong skills in Microsoft office products, including Word, Excel, Outlook/SharePoint, and PowerPoint. Experience with Adobe Suite is an asset.

Cross-cultural work environment:

- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Positive work ethic and desire to work in the humanitarian field.

jobs.title: Terms of Reference: Eye Health Integration Consultant
jobs.description:
The Fred Hollows Foundation (FHF) invites applications from individual consultants to provide part-time technical support and coordination for an 18-month eye health integration pilot in Adamawa State, Nigeria.

**Contract Type:** Individual consultancy, part-time.
**Duration:** 18 months from the agreed commencement date.
**Location:** Nigeria, preferably Adamawa State.
**Contract Manager:** FHF Africa Cluster Director.
**Key Working Relationships**: ThinkMD, Adamawa State Primary Health Care Development Agency (ADSPHCDA), FHF technical and monitoring teams, eye health stakeholders and participating PHC facilities.

**1. Background and Context**
The Fred Hollows Foundation (FHF) has partnered with ThinkMD and the Adamawa State Primary Health Care Development Agency (ADSPHCDA) of Nigeria to develop and test an eye health module into ThinkMD's Clinical Intelligence platform through an 18-month pilot. FHF is the specialist eye health partner in the pilot providing clinical direction on the module, co-design, ongoing technical assistance throughout implementation, monitoring and evaluation support, and strategic input into possible scale-up. ThinkMD leads platform development and functionality while ADSPHCDA leads government implementation.
Beyond testing a digital eye health module, the pilot presents an important opportunity to generate practical evidence on how eye health can be integrated into routine primary healthcare.

**2. Purpose of the Consultancy**
The consultant will provide ongoing coordination, technical and implementation support for FHF’s contribution to the ThinkMD Nigeria pilot, ensuring that the Foundation’s eye health priorities and technical requirements are incorporated throughout its design and delivery. This will include supporting alignment with relevant WHO eye care guidance, Nigerian national guidelines and the local primary healthcare context.
Working closely with ThinkMD, Adamawa State PHCDA and FHF technical teams, the consultant will support effective implementation, systematic documentation and the generation of practical evidence and learning to inform sustainable integration of eye health into primary healthcare and future scale-up.

**3. Objectives and Scope of Services**
**3.1 Pilot Implementation and Coordination:**
•Support the overall coordination and implementation of FHF's role in the pilot.
•Coordinate FHF inputs into pilot planning, implementation and review processes.
•Establish regular coordination with partner focal persons; maintain action and decision records; track progress against agreed plans and escalate delays and unresolved decisions to the contract manager.
• Identify implementation delays, bottlenecks and emerging issues and escalate to the FHF Contract Manager
• Support regular pilot coordination and review meetings.
• Develop an inception plan outlining the consultant's approach, key activities, deliverables, stakeholder engagement arrangements, milestones and reporting schedule.
• Maintain an updated implementation tracker covering FHF commitments, technical inputs, outstanding actions, dependencies and agreed timelines.

**3.2 Eye Health Technical Implementation Support:**
• Coordinate FHF technical inputs into the development and refinement of the eye health module.
• Check consistency with agreed national protocols and worker competencies.
• Support implementation-focused user testing using agreed scenarios and frontline worker feedback.
• Document lessons on how eye health referral pathways can be integrated into routine primary healthcare.
• Monitor referral bottlenecks in an agreed sample of participating PHC and document gaps.

**3.3 Technical Review and Quality Assurance:**
• Undertake structured technical reviews of the eye health module, clinical content, workflows, user-testing findings and proposed revisions, documenting recommendations and tracking their resolution.
• Coordinate relevant FHF specialist reviews where additional clinical or subspecialty expertise is required.
• Maintain a technical issues and recommendations log to document identified gaps, proposed actions and their resolution.

**3.4 Monitoring Evaluation and Learning:**
• Undertake targeted field visits and follow-up under an agreed sampling and supervision plan.
• Track agreed pilot indicators.
• Support data-quality checks and analysis.
• Coordinate sample clinical case reviews with qualified eye care professionals, recording corrective actions and their closure.
• Identify and document the implementation, workforce, health-system and referral requirements for scale-up, including practical barriers to adoption and lessons for future implementation.
• Support development of scale-up recommendations and contribute to discussions with ThinkMD and other stakeholders on future integration of eye health.
• Prepare and submit quarterly progress reports to FHF.

**3.5 Learning and Sustainability:**
• Gather structured feedback on usability, workload and service integration.
• Contribute to mid-pilot and final reviews and any separately commissioned evaluation.
• Develop practical continuation and scale-up options with partners, identifying conditions, costs where available, evidence gaps and responsible actors.
• Support FHF’s assessment of relevance to other settings.

**3.5 Risk and Information Management:**
• Maintain a risk register covering clinical safety, adoption, referral capacity, stakeholder alignment, safeguarding, and data protection; track mitigation actions and escalate concerns promptly.
• Identifying operational, technical, stakeholder, safeguarding and implementation risks.
• Supporting development of mitigation measures and monitoring agreed mitigation actions.

**3.6 Expected Deliverables:**
• Inception report, detailed workplan and stakeholder engagement plan (Month 1).
• Technical review and recommendations on the eye health module (Initial development phase and subsequent revisions).
• Implementation monitoring and field visit reports (Following agreed field visits).
• Technical issues, recommendations and action tracker (Maintained throughout).
• Quarterly progress reports (Every three months).
• Clinical case-review summaries and follow-up actions (Periodically, as agreed).
• Mid-pilot implementation and learning report (Month 9).
• Final implementation, learning and scale-up recommendations report (Month 18).

**4. Authority and Professional Boundaries**
The consultant coordinates FHF’s contribution and accesses FHF specialist support. ThinkMD retains responsibility for software development, release and platform performance; ADSPHCDA and service providers retain responsibility for government operations and clinical service delivery. The consultant does not independently authorise clinical algorithms, commit FHF funds, sign agreements or make public commitments on FHF’s behalf. Access to facilities, staff and data will be coordinated through ADSPHCDA and ThinkMD and remains subject to authorisation.

**5. Consultant Qualifications and Experience**
FHF seeks an individual with strong eye health and PHC implementation experience who can coordinate specialist inputs, work effectively with government and translate pilot findings into practical improvements. Software development expertise is not required.

**Essential Requirements:**
• A recognised qualification in ophthalmology, optometry, ophthalmic nursing, public health, health systems or a related discipline, supported by demonstrable experience in eye health service delivery or programme implementation. A non-clinical qualification must be complemented by substantial eye health implementation experience and effective coordination of clinical expertise.
• At least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including at least three years supporting eye health programmes, PHC integration or closely related referral and service-strengthening work.
• Demonstrated experience working with Nigerian government health structures and frontline facilities, including practical understanding of PHC service delivery, health worker cadres and referral constraints.
• Experience coordinating multi-partner implementation, developing workplans, tracking risks and actions, and producing clear reports with limited day-to-day supervision.
• Ability to interpret eye care guidance and clinical workflows, recognise issues requiring specialist review, and support safe implementation within professional and organisational boundaries.
• Competence in routine monitoring, basic quantitative analysis, data-quality review and qualitative feedback, with the ability to turn findings into recommendations.
• Based in Nigeria, available for the agreed part-time commitment.

**Desirable Requirements:**
• Experience with digital health, clinical decision support, user testing or technology-enabled service integration, including collaboration with technical product teams.
• Experience in Adamawa State or comparable settings in northern Nigeria; Hausa and/or other languages relevant to participating communities.
• Experience assessing referral completion, implementation costs, sustainability or scale-up; familiarity with relevant WHO primary eye care and vision-screening resources.

**6. Level of Effort**
The engagement is part-time over 18 months. For proposal costing, use an indicative allocation of 10 working days per month, up to 180 days in total. Work may combine remote coordination with in-person meetings and targeted facility visits in Adamawa State. Applicants should state their proposed base and travel approach. Field activity is subject to security review, agreed travel arrangements.

**7. Consultancy and Commercial Arrangement**
This is a consultancy for defined services and deliverables. Fees, approved level of effort, invoicing, termination provisions and other conditions will be set out in the consultancy agreement. No employment benefits are included.

Applicants should submit a daily professional fee, currency, and total professional fees. Show applicable taxes separately and provide a separate estimate of travel, accommodation, and other expenses, stating assumptions. Identify any costs expected to be arranged or paid directly by FHF. The final expense and tax treatment will be
confirmed through contracting.

jobs.description:
## Starting Date / Initial Contract Details

December 2026, Full-time, 12 months

## Role Summary

The Ebola Health Advisor r will oversee all technical aspects of Medair’s Ebola response in DR Congo. Reporting to the Country Ebola Coordinator, and closely coordinating with Medair’s in-country Health and Nutrition Advisor, the Ebola Health Coordinator will represent Medair at a senior level in all technical Ebola coordination meetings, reporting back to relevant internal stakeholders ensuring Medair is strategically positioned. The job-holder will provide technical oversight to Ebola-related activities in Medair-supported health facilities and Ebola Treatment centres in Ituri and Nord Kivu Provinces, working with specialist staff to ensure that health facility staff are adequately trained and Ebola protocols are strictly observed.

## Project Overview

Medair is significantly scaling up its programming in DR Congo in response to the recent Ebola outbreak. Medair is implementing specific pillars of the response to the outbreak, including Infection Prevention control, Case Management, Surveillance, Risk Communication and Community Engagement and Mental Health/ Psychosocial Support.

## Workplace & Conditions

Bunia, Ituri province, with regular travel to Beni and Butembo, Nord Kivu Province.

## Responsibilities:

External Representation: Take a lead in external coordination with other partners involved in the Ebola response, including representing Medair at high-level meetings. Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders.

Technical programme management: strategic and overall technical supervision to ensure successful implementation of the Ebola response. Share best practices for Ebola response across different Medair bases.

Technical capacity building and supervision of Medair’s staff and health facility workers on Ebola protocols.

Ebola Preparedness: Coordinate with managers of Medair’s “routine” health, nutrition and WASH programmes to ensure that Ebola preparedness and appropriate adaptations are put in place.

Quality Control: Ensure quality of Ebola medical care and that implementation is in accordance with WHO and national guidelines. Define policies, guidelines and protocols relating to Ebola as required.

## Qualifications, Experience & Technical Competencies:

Medical Doctor, MSc in Public Health a plus with 3 years minimum experience post qualification

At least 3 years’ experience in managing programmes in international public health work, with at least 1 year in humanitarian emergency context. Experience in Ebola/VHF or infectious disease outbreaks strongly preferred.

Good English and French (spoken and written).

Experience in the design, monitoring of implementation and evaluation of public health programmes.

Strong knowledge of humanitarian principles, Sphere and CHS Standards.

Good report and proposal writing skills. Experience of external representation.

## Behavioral Skills

Strong servant leadership skills with a consultative management style.

Creative, open-minded, flexible, self-learner, with good understanding of cross-cultural issues.

Capacity to work under pressure and manage personal stress levels.

Able to oversee multiple tasks, prioritising and delegating as required.

Excellent communication and diplomacy skills. Ability to represent the organization confidently externally.

## Team Spiritual Life

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

jobs.title: Director of Global People Operations
jobs.description:
## **About IDinsight**

*We're a global data and evidence advisory, working with governments, philanthropies, and non-profits to improve lives at scale, using technology and AI where they can deliver the most impact.*

IDinsight is a global non-profit that equips leaders with the data, evidence and technology to improve lives at scale. We partner with governments, NGOs, multilaterals, and funders to support decisions at every stage of their impact journey – from bold pilots to nationwide scale-ups. Our teams bring rigorous evidence and practical insights so leaders can make informed decisions that truly change lives. With our partners, we are pioneering the next frontier of social impact, where data and technology accelerate progress for millions. We help leaders overcome the three main barriers to impact:

1. Figuring out what works
2. Learning and improving
3. Reaching and operating at scale

We work across Asia and Africa, in sectors including agriculture, education, health, governance, sanitation, financial inclusion, among others. We have expertise in a variety of rigorous approaches and methodologies, which we tailor to each client depending on their needs and constraints. To achieve a positive social impact we:

- Support our partners with the full ‘data and evidence’ value chain – from primary data collection to data systems, monitoring evaluation and learning tools, and data science
- Inform funding decisions – toward high-impact initiatives and away from less effective programs or approaches
- Create cutting-edge AI-for-good products that make the delivery of social interventions and learning tools more cost-effective and scalable

Our diverse, growing team of roughly 250 outstanding colleagues operate in nearly two dozen countries around the world. Learn more about our mission, values, and principles at [www.IDinsight.org](http://www.IDinsight.org).

## **Joining IDinsight at this moment**

IDinsight is entering an exciting new phase of growth. As demand for rigorous evidence and AI-enabled solutions accelerates across the sectors and geographies we work in, we are actively investing in our teams, deepening our regional footprint, and expanding the frontier of what data and technology can do for social impact. This is a moment of real momentum for IDinsight. We're looking for people who want to use data and evidence to improve lives at scale; who are energized by taking on problems without a playbook; and who want a hand in shaping what IDinsight becomes as we grow.

## **About the Director of Global People Operations role**

This is not a traditional HR role. IDinsight is lean, non-hierarchical, innovative, and fast-moving, and we need someone who can set people strategy and execute on it with the same spirit and speed. IDinsight is entering its next phase of growth (expecting to grow 35-50% over the next 12-18 months) and the Global People Operations team is central to making that happen. We are investing heavily on two fronts at once: bringing in best-in-class talent to deliver our most ambitious work, and building the retention strategy, culture, and learning systems that keep our existing team growing with us. The Director of Global People Operations leads a team of 12+ and owns making IDinsight the workplace of choice in global development. This role reports to the Chief Financial and Operations Officer (CFOO).

### **Responsibilities**

**Strategy and Organizational Leadership**

- Co-develop and lead the implementation of IDinsight’s global People Strategy, alongside the CFOO and senior leadership.
- Work with leadership on org design and change management to keep the org high-performing, motivated, and impactful.
- Lead 1–2 organization-changing initiatives a year (e.g., a new performance system, a comp overhaul, a leadership pipeline).
- Build and maintain strong collaborative working relationships across several regions and functions, and amongst key leaders in all teams.
- Serve as the CFOO’s primary advisor on org design, workforce planning, and the tradeoffs behind the big people calls.

**Team Leadership**

- Lead IDinsight’s Global People Operations team of 12+ people across multiple regions, and own their performance, growth, and career development.
- Run the team efficiently: manage workload, hit deadlines, and keep day-to-day operations strong, while leading with care.
- We are in a growth phase where the biggest constraint on IDinsight’s impact is whether we can hire, develop, and retain the right people fast enough. Lead the Global People Operations team through this moment.

**Culture**

- Steward how IDinsight’s values show up operationally as it scales, through policies, recognition, and systems.
- Champion the parts of IDinsight’s culture that make us who we are (non-hierarchical, innovative, scrappy, ambitious, fast), and make sure they don’t get lost as we scale.

**People Development**

- Own our compensation philosophy; benchmark pay and benefits every two years to ensure IDinsight is able to attract the best talent in the development sector while remaining fair and transparent internally.
- Track retention and attrition by region and build targeted fixes wherever needed.
- Diagnose skill gaps across the org with leadership and design L&D programs that reach teammates across all 7+ countries and meet the needs of IDinsight’s rapidly evolving portfolio.
- Build manager-development programs for IDinsight’s many first-time and newer managers.
- Be a trusted advisor to the senior leaders and invest in their development through internal and external coaches.

**People Enablement**

- Lead the team in building and strengthening IDinsight’s recruitment pipeline across its countries of operation, with direct ownership of senior and leadership hires.
- Own IDinsight’s employer brand and candidate experience, and streamline hiring to cut time-to-hire without compromising rigor.
- Own payroll accuracy and timeliness across every country we pay people in.

**Business Operations**

- Keep IDinsight compliant with local labor law and employment requirements across every country we operate in, including global mobility and employer-of-record arrangements.
- Own and keep IDinsight’s people policies current and consistent across ~20 countries (leave, parental leave, expenses).
- Lead a revamp of our policies and benefits: find efficiencies without cutting corners, stay generous and competitive within what a non-profit can offer, and make sure every policy reflects that we care about our people while staying compliant.
- Own core people systems (BambooHR, Airtable, Ashby, and others), improve data quality, and use people data to inform strategy and report to leadership.
- Own risk assessment and mitigation for people-related and workplace-safety risks, and maintain data security and privacy practices for people systems. Duty of care across 20+ countries that IDinsight works in is a core part of the role.

**AI and Innovation**

- Make the People Ops team AI-first: champion AI-native ways of working within the team and ensure AI tools are embedded in how the team works day to day.
- Own how the rest of the org interacts with People Ops through AI, identifying where AI tools can make people processes like recruiting screens, policy drafting, data analysis, onboarding content better or faster.
- Set the standard for AI fluency in people ops at IDinsight and bring the rest of the team up with you.

## **Qualifications**

**Required**

- 12+ years of experience in a people-facing leadership role, with direct experience building or substantially improving people systems and programs from the ground up.
- Proven experience leading and developing managers across multiple countries or regions, in a non-hierarchical, fast-moving environment.
- [Values-aligned](https://www.idinsight.org/about/): IDinsight is a unique workplace, and this is not a traditional HR role -- we need someone who is low ego, high innovation, non-bureaucratic, non-hierarchical, and is excited to own IDinsight’s people strategy in this exciting moment.
- Comfortable rolling up their sleeves. We are a lean organization and recognize that small gestures often shape culture as much as big decisions
- Comfortable going from raw people data to a clear, defensible recommendation for leadership.
- Ability to navigate people and policy decisions with nuance and discretion -- IDinsight teammates live in more than 20 countries and people decisions often require striking a balance between multiple cultural and legal realities of different places.
- Familiarity with BambooHR, Airtable, Ashby, Lattice, or comparable HRIS/ATS/LMS tools.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills (clear, yet tactful).
- Familiarity with MS Office, Google Docs, and other relevant systems.
- Deep, hands-on fluency with AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) in daily work – drafting, research, analysis. You will be expected to use them well yourself, and to identify where they can make people processes better or faster.
- Passion for improving lives through evidence-informed policy.

**Preferred**

- Experience in a lean or fast-growing global nonprofit, social enterprise, or similarly mission-driven organization.
- Lived or professional experience in one of IDinsight’s countries of operation.
- Interest in and familiarity with research on organizational design, behavioral economics, or management best practices.

## **Professional development**

Skill and career development are core to IDinsight's values and long-term impact strategy, and have been noted highlights of teammates’ experiences. IDinsighters receive significant mentorship from IDinsight leadership, support from talented peers, and are given considerable autonomy when ready. They maintain professional development plans and are given "stretch" opportunities designed to strengthen a variety of skills. Real-time feedback is embedded in our culture and formal structure enables maximum professional growth. Additionally, teammates have access to an annual professional development stipend that they are encouraged to utilize to explore their career interests and develop their skills.

## **Nuts & bolts**

### **Location**

This position will be based in IDinsight’s ***Dakar, Senegal; Delhi, India; Lusaka, Zambia; Manila, Philippines; Nairobi, Kenya; or Rabat, Morocco***office(s).

This position is not eligible for remote work, or otherwise, from the United States. Preference will be given to those with pre-existing work authorization in these countries; however, IDinsight will seek work permits where possible for exceptional candidates.

### **Start date**

The start date of this position is **January 1, 2027**, with preference for candidates who can start immediately. We expect a 2-year minimum commitment, with regular professional development conversations and potential for a long-term career at IDinsight.

### **Compensation**

Compensation and benefits are commensurate with the qualifications and experiences IDinsight is hiring for, and competitive within the global development sector. We are especially proud of the people-focused benefits we offer including comprehensive international health insurance, including mental health coverage; paid vacation, sick, and parental leave; relocation benefits; a travel stipend; technology and work from home stipends; a professional development budget; and more.

Please note, as a non-profit, we are unable to provide compensation similar to leading private sector organizations.

## **How to apply**

This application includes several questions and requires a CV (one to two pages) covering your professional and personal experience as well as academic qualifications. Please omit headshots, parental details, birth dates, marital status, and similar personal information — these aren't relevant to our review.

More information, including details on [I**Dinsight’s hiring process**](https://www.idinsight.org/about/careers/the-idinsight-hiring-process/)and [**frequently asked questions**](http://idinsight.org/about/careers/frequently-asked-questions/), can be found online at [IDinsight Careers](https://www.idinsight.org/about/careers/). Any questions should be directed to careers@IDinsight.org.

## **IDinsight’s commitment to reducing power asymmetries**

IDinsight is committed to [**reducing power asymmetries in the social sector**](https://www.idinsight.org/about/careers/reducing-power-asymmetries-in-the-social-sector-an-idinsight-organizational-priority/). Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion reflects our understanding of the need for the sector to abandon unhealthy practices of the past. We wish to be part of a new generation of international NGOs who are honest about this history and transparent about our role in the present. Our commitment is also aligned with the impact of our work.

We seek a workforce that is inclusive of a variety of perspectives that will help us refine and improve our methods and relationships, and strengthen the services we provide our clients and their communities or constituencies. The following commitments represent our vision for the IDinsight team:

1. IDinsight will have greater representation from the **populations with whom we work** and **clients we serve**.
2. IDinsight will have greater representation from the **countries in which we work**.
3. Across all countries in which we recruit, we will seek **greater representation from historically excluded communities**.
4. IDinsight will foster an **inclusive work culture that empowers a diverse team** to do their best work.

IDinsight is committed to non-discrimination in our recruitment, employment practices, and organizational culture, regardless of people’s age, disability, gender, gender identity, national origin, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Technical Officer (Cold Chain)
jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:
1\. **International knowledge hub for health** – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.
2\. **Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health** – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.
3\. **Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats** – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.
4\. **Driver of health system transformation** – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.
5\. **Voice for health equity** – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

The purpose of this position is to provide technical support to the Ministry of Health (MOH) of Ukraine in strengthening the immunization cold chain system. This position will enable the WHO Regional Office for Europe (WHO/EURO) to be more responsive and to play a leading role in strengthening of vaccine management and safety practices for further diseases preparedness and control. Under the overall guidance of the Head of WHO Office in Ukraine and direct supervision of the Health Programme Lead, with close collaboration with the Vaccine Preventable Diseases and Immunization (VPI) unit in WHO European Regional Office in Copenhagen, the incumbent will undertake the following specific responsibilities:
1\. Contribute to the implementation of Standard Operation Procedures (SOPs) for Vaccine storage and distribution at national warehouse and WHO outsource premises. In addition, considering power outages and current situation with electricity system conduct specific risk assessment.
2\. Serve as a technical resource to the programme concerning vaccine safety in regards of storage and distribution.
3\. Arrange for capacity building and training on storage, logistic and actions on emergency situations.
4\. Monitor and conduct situation analysis of available cold chain equipment and prepare tables, graphs and other statistical data and report outcome of analysis for generating evidence for needs and decision making process.
5\. Conduct regular risk assessment at the national and district level warehouses for vaccine storage.
6\. Provide technical advice to strengthen cold chain capacities.
7\. Monitor performance and compliance with established SOPs for performance qualifications of cold rooms, equipment at the level of healthcare delivery providers and remote temperature monitoring system.
8\. Liaise with national counterparts, and partners (UN and bilateral) to harmonize implementation activities related to cold chain.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential**: A university degree (Bachelor's level) in cold chain engineer, logistics, supply chain management, medicine, pharmacy, biomedical engineering, or a related field relevant to this position.

**Desirable:** Master's degree or advanced training in any of the above.

### Experience

**Essential:** At least 2 years of professional experience at the national level in cold chain logistics, vaccine management, or immunization program implementation. Demonstrated experience working with/within public projects and working with multiple stakeholders, such as national policymakers, NGOs, and the private sector, in the area of cold chain and logistics. Good knowledge of cold chain system in Ukraine.

**Desirable:** Experience in planning and implementing health-related projects, knowledge of global vaccine supply chains, and familiarity with immunization and cold chain systems in Ukraine.

### Functional Skills

1\. Demonstrated knowledge of infectious diseases surveillance systems and global and regional standards.
2\. Familiarity with national immunization, cold chain and public health systems.
3\. Knowledge of the principles of physics, engineering and cold chain equipment.
4\. Demonstrated analytical, presentation, and report-writing skills.
5\. Proven ability to work comfortably in an international, multi-disciplinary, fast-paced environment.
6\. Demonstrated knowledge of the goals and procedures of international organizations (United Nations system, donors, major nongovernmental organizations)
7\. Ability to identify and manage one's own emotions, as well as helping others do the same.

### WHO Competencies

Teamwork
Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences
Communication
Producing results
Building and promoting partnerships across the organization and beyond

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of another United Nations language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 47,491 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - Technical Officer (Cold Chain) (2604809)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2604809&tz=GMT%2B02%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Assist with housing set-ups for new arrivals as needed.
- Assist clients in completing initial medical appointments as needed.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in ETO and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $186 per month, dental starting at $9.00 per month, and vision starting at $4 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Compensation:** ($20.97$). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: National Professional Officer (Health Financing)
jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME
