jobs.title: Business & Human Rights Data Analyst - MyVox Product Owner
jobs.description:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

In Cambodia, GRC works with trade unions and civil society organisations to strengthen labour rights accountability in the garment and apparel sector. It supports garment workers and their representatives to document and monitor labour rights violations, and to use that evidence to secure remedy through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, and international accountability routes. Alongside monitoring, the project delivers awareness-raising, community building and tailored legal aid.

We are seeking a Business & Human Rights Data Analyst to join our team. The Data Analyst supports the analysis of data collected through MyVox (including the mobile/web app and the live dashboard). The role is responsible for managing, analysing, and interpreting data collected through the mobile and web application to provide actionable insights that will inform advocacy and awareness-raising efforts.

**The Role**

- Collect, organize, and clean data from the MyVox application, ensuring data integrity and accuracy by identifying and rectifying any data anomalies or errors.
- Perform statistical analysis and interpret the results to identify trends, patterns, and insights.
- Use data visualization tools to present data in a clear and actionable manner.
- Develop quarterly comprehensive reports and presentations based on data analysis.
- Collaborate with the development team to ensure data-related issues are addressed promptly.
- Provide ongoing support for data-related inquiries and troubleshooting.
- Support and contribute to the ongoing development of the team’s work by identifying potential areas for future activity and collaboration, consistent with strategic priorities.
- Develop documentation and guides for data management and analysis processes.

**Your Background**

- Bachelor's degree in data science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field. A master’s degree is preferred.
- 5+ years experience as a Data Analyst or in a similar role.
- Strong proficiency in data analysis tools and software (e.g., Python, R, SQL, Excel).
- Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex data clearly and concisely.
- Experience working with non-profit organizations is a plus.
- Work or academic experience focused on topics related to peacebuilding, conflict, human rights, and/or global affairs (or similar).
- Ability to work remotely with limited supervision.
- Excellent organization and time management skills.
- Good judgement and high attention to detail.
- Fluency in English - both written and verbal skills.

jobs.title: Coordinateur.trice Finance Régional, Grands Lacs (f/h/x)
jobs.description:
## **NOTRE MISSION**

Médecins du Monde est une ONG internationale de développement médical faisant partie d'un réseau international. Nous fournissons une assistance médicale aux groupes vulnérables, en Belgique et dans le reste du monde.

Nous voulons une couverture universelle de santé où chaque personne a accès aux soins, sans obstacles (financiers, culturels, géographiques, etc.).

Pour mener à bien notre mission, nous nous basons sur trois piliers :

- **Soigner** : donner un réel accès aux soins aux populations.
- **Changer**: plus qu'aider, nous voulons changer les choses à long terme.
- **Témoigner** : nous ne restons pas silencieux. Grâce à notre expérience et notre présence sur le terrain, nous interpellons les pouvoirs (locaux, régionaux et (inter)nationaux) avec des faits, des chiffres et des réalités.

Nos projets suivent une série de valeurs communes à toute notre organisation : Justice sociale, Empowerment, Indépendance, Engagement, Equilibre.

## **L’ESSENTIEL**

Sous la supervision hiérarchique du Directeur Régional Grands-Lacs et en lien étroit avec la Direction Financière du siège, le/la Coordinateur·rice Finance Régional·e définit, pilote et garantit la stratégie, la gestion et la conformité financières des pays (missions) de la régional Grands-Lacs.

Il/Elle assure le cadrage budgétaire, la consolidation comptable, le contrôle de gestion et la soutenabilité financière des projets dans le strict respect de la législation locale, des exigences bailleurs et des procédures de MdM-Be. Acteur·rice clé du pilotage stratégique et du contrôle interne, il/elle apporte un conseil avisé à la Direction Régionale, veille à la maîtrise des risques financiers, encadre les équipes finance de la région et renforce les capacités techniques des collaborateurs opérationnels et des partenaires.

## **TACHES ET RESPONSABILITES**

**Définition et monitoring de la stratégie financière**

- Élaboration de la stratégie financière de la région
- Fournir des conseils à la direction régionale sur le développement stratégique de la structure financière dans la région des Grands-Lacs, afin d'assurer un soutien efficace aux pays de la région et de promouvoir une culture de sensibilisation à une gestion responsable des ressources.
- Accroître la visibilité financière dans la région au moyen de rapports sur les indicateurs clés de performance et d'analyses financières partagés mensuellement avec l'équipe de coordination régionale et la direction au siège afin d'appuyer la prise de décision.
- Mettre en œuvre les initiatives/outils/systèmes financiers dans la région et développer et mettre en œuvre des procédures financières spécifiques, des SOP, des lignes directrices et des outils dans la région, y compris des prévisions.
- Être le point de contact régional pour la direction financière de MdM-BE à Bruxelles.

**Consolidation & contrôle des livrables financiers**

- Diriger le processus annuel de budgétisation régionale, maintenir les prévisions financières régionales et fournir des informations financières pour les rapports finaux et périodiques destinés à la direction régionale et au siège.
- Vérifier et valider l'avancement financier des projets en cours, avec la collaboration des responsables financiers des pays de la région.
- Consolider les rapports financiers régionaux et assurer leur transmission au siège ou aux bailleurs.
- Garantir les mécanismes de contrôle des finances dans les missions de la région, la conformité et l'adhésion aux politiques, orientations et procédures de MdM-BE.
- Fournir un soutien financier technique pour l'élaboration des subventions régionales et assurer le suivi et l'établissement de rapports sur les subventions régionales.

**Renforcement de capacités des équipes pays**

- Veiller à ce que des routines et des systèmes de gestion financière adéquats soient en place et à ce que les pratiques et les normes budgétaires et comptables de MdM-BE soient respectées, opportunes et conformes aux exigences des donateurs, des auditeurs et des autorités.
- Assurer l'orientation, le soutien et le renforcement des capacités du personnel financier et des responsables hiérarchiques dans les pays de la région, ainsi que veiller à ce que des formations soient organisées pour le personnel financier et non financier dans l'ensemble de la région sur les questions et les outils liés aux finances.
- Assurer le monitoring des performances et le développement du personnel de l'unité financière de la région.
- Assumer les fonctions des Coordinateurs (Responsables) financiers des pays en cas d’absence ou de vacances temporaire d’un des postes.

## **VOTRE PROFIL**

**Formation et expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire supérieur (BAC+5) en finance, économie, en comptabilité, gestion, ou dans un domaine similaire.
- Un minimum de cinq (5) ans d'expérience pertinente au poste de la Coordination Finance ;
- Une expérience de la coordination et du développement d'une équipe, ainsi qu'une expérience de la mise en œuvre de programmes réussis de développement du personnel, de renforcement des capacités et de coaching sont requises, ainsi qu'une expérience des systèmes de gestion et d'établissement de rapports financiers et de la création d'outils financiers adaptés aux besoins des utilisateurs.
- Une expérience avérée de la collaboration avec des organisations internationales et multilatérales de développement, en particulier dans les domaines liés à la santé.

**Compétences spécifiques**

- Capacité avérée en analyse des risques financiers
- Force de proposition de solutions adaptées aux contextes différents de chaque pays.
- Création & animation de formation technique financière
- Maitrise de la langue française
- Connaissance de l’anglais est fortement souhaitée

## **NOUS OFFRONS**

- Une fonction enrichissante et essentielle au cœur des projets de Médecins du Monde Belgique
- Un contrat à durée déterminée à temps plein de 1 an
- Conditions salariales :
- Rémunération brute : 3 694,85€ brut/mois pour 5 ans d’expérience ; 3 883,32€ brut/mois pour 10 ans d’expérience ; expérience pertinente reconnue
- Perdiem : 651 €/mois
- Excellente couverture assurantielle : santé, rapatriement, prévoyance
- Cotisation à un mécanisme de retraite ou paiement de l’équivalent de 421,95€ supplémentaire par mois
- Prise de poste : 01/01/2027
- Lieu de mission : Bukavu avec des déplacements possibles dans les pays de la région

jobs.title: Supply Chain and Admin Officer - Hassaka
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

To act as the main buyer and Supply Chain focal point for the Hasakeh and Raqqa offices and project centers, including Tal Abyad operations, providing overall management and oversight of procurement, administration, logistics and asset management. The jobholder processes and manages all PRs, POs and contracts on the Provision system, ensures compliance with World Vision and donor requirements, maintains effective internal controls, supervises assigned support staff, and provides efficient operational support to programme implementation. Reports directly to the Area Manager – NES (Hasakeh & Raqqa) and technically to the Supply Chain Manager – Amman.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Administration & Facility Management 20%**

- Oversee office administration and support services for the Hasakeh and Raqqa Offices and project centres.
- Manage office facilities, leases, service agreements, maintenance requirements, utilities, and workplace readiness.
- Coordinate travel, accommodation, meetings, events, and administrative support services.
- Monitor office supplies, consumables, and service contracts to ensure operational continuity.
- Act as a focal point for administrative support requests and coordinate solutions with relevant departments and service providers.
- Support budget estimation, cost control, and administration reporting activities.
- Coordinate with the Amman IT team and external IT service providers to keep office IT equipment, systems, and connectivity functional.
- Maintain organized filing of office, procurement, and logistics records on the designated SCM folder.

**Procurement Management 50%**
- Create, review, process and close all PRs, POs and contracts on the Provision system, including approvals follow-up, supplier and contract records, amendments, and attachment of complete supporting documents.
- Coordinate with the Amman Supply Chain and Finance teams for Provision access, system support, and escalation of system or process issues.
- Lead and coordinate the end-to-end procurement process for assigned locations, including PR review, sourcing, solicitation, bid management, evaluation coordination, award recommendations, contract follow-up, delivery monitoring, and file closure.
- Manage procurement activities for Hasakeh and Raqqa Offices and projects centers, including Tal Abyad operations, and provide procurement oversight and support to assigned operational locations.
- Coordinate competitive procurement processes, including RFQs, ITBs, RFPs, bid openings, evaluations, and procurement committee documentation.
- Conduct market assessments, supplier mapping, due diligence, supplier performance monitoring, and maintain updated supplier databases.
- Ensure procurement activities comply with WVI policies, donor requirements, and Delegation of Authority.
- Monitor procurement plans, lead times, delivery schedules, and procurement status, escalating risks and delays when required.
- Coordinate with Finance and request departments to ensure timely processing, complete documentation, and audit-ready procurement files.
- Provide guidance to requesting units on procurement planning, specifications development, market conditions, and compliance requirements.
- Review partner procurement policies and procurement packages (tender documents, bid evaluations, supporting records) for partner-implemented projects, and ensure partners submit complete procurement documentation to the WVSR SCM team for review and approval in a timely manner.
- Participate in project kick-off meetings and bi-weekly coordination meetings with partners to review procurement updates and address challenges.

**Logistics Management 20%**
- Oversee fleet operations, vehicle rentals, maintenance coordination, documentation, utilization monitoring, and compliance with fleet policies.
- Supervise asset management activities including asset registration, assignment, tracking, physical verification, maintenance, transfers, and disposal processes.
- Maintain an asset list for each WVI-funded project and verify that partner-held assets are documented, reported, and managed according to WVI and donor requirements.
- Coordinate shipments and delivery of supplies to field sites, including clearance documentation, shipment tracking, and delivery follow-up when required.
- Manage storage, stock levels, and distribution of materials and office supplies, conduct regular stock takes, and submit a monthly inventory balance report to the line manager and the Supply Chain Manager.
- Ensure logistical records and supporting documentation are maintained accurately and securely.
- Identify and escalate logistics, fleet, or asset-related risks and compliance concerns.

**People Management & Coordination 10%**
- Supervise assigned support staff including supply chain assistant, cleaners and guards, and oversee day-to-day workload allocation and operational coverage.
- Monitor performance, provide coaching, and contribute to performance management processes.
- Assess training needs and provide on-the-job training and guidance to supervised staff and requesting units on PR/BoQ preparation, procurement procedures, and the Provision system.
- Liaise with partner NGOs to support Organizational Capacity Assessment (OCA) and Organizational Capacity Development (OCB), and guide partners on WVI supply chain policies and procedures.
- Promote compliance with safeguarding and organizational policies.
- Maintain effective coordination with Programme, Finance, P&C, IT, and Supply Chain teams.
- Support the implementation of internal controls and ensure segregation of duties within procurement and operational processes.
- Escalate compliance, fraud, conflict of interest, safeguarding, or operational risks as required.
- Maintain dual reporting: update the line manager on daily operations and the Supply Chain Manager on technical SCM matters, and submit monthly reports summarizing procurement progress, inventory status, key issues, and next steps.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- 4 years' experience in administration and supply chain management responsible role

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor Degree (preferable in Business Administration or relevant field of studies)

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Personal Management including initiative, self-motivation and direction
- Ability to set priorities and undertake new tasks quickly
- Ability to interpret and explain complex formal documents and systems and assist others to apply them
- Strong management skills including attention to details.
- Advanced Computer skills (Word, Excel, Access, Outlook)
- Experience with procurement or ERP systems; knowledge of the Provision system is an asset
- Strong communication and negotiation skills & Good market knowledge
- Knowledge of local Customs and Tax regulations
- Strong Analytical skills

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- When required between Hasakeh, Raqqa and Tal Abyad
- Position requires willingness and ability to continue to function during a crisis situation, including during a World Vision response to a manmade or natural disaster.

1. **Physical Requirements**

- Office based with field visits when needed

1. **Language Requirements**

- Arabic fluent
- Good English communication skills (oral and written)

jobs.title: Mental Health Specialist
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**DESCRIPTION:**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 to respond to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of refugees from Darfur into eastern Chad. Assistance to Sudanese refugees expanded to include the management of eleven camps in the east and one camp in the west, providing support to refugees and local communities in the areas of health, nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation. In 2012, IRC expanded its geographic coverage to Guéra Province, where the organization currently works in five health districts and provides malnutrition prevention and treatment services to the local population, as well as family planning, response, and prevention activities related to gender-based violence (GBV). In May 2016, IRC established a presence in Lac Province to respond to the crisis caused by Boko Haram. In its 2022–2024 Strategic Action Plan, IRC Chad is committed to continuing to provide essential humanitarian services in health, nutrition, and protection/GBV, while improving the economic well-being and strengthening the resilience of beneficiaries, particularly women and girls. IRC Chad will continue to work closely with and support government actors and line ministries in key sectors to ensure that IRC’s actions are integrated into national policies, thereby fostering greater ownership of the initiatives undertaken.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Senior Health Coordinator, the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist based in Hadjer Hadid will be responsible for the overall management and implementation of a high-quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) program in all of IRC’s areas of operation, and more specifically in refugee camps. The Mental Health Specialist will work closely with the Ministry of Public Health’s mental health program, UNHCR, IRC, HIAS, and all members of the mental health working group in Chad to facilitate the coordination of mental health interventions in the country and strengthen their integration into the minimum package of services provided in health centers and hospitals. The mental health and psychosocial support specialist will supervise health workers in providing prevention, diagnosis, and treatment services for patients with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, using the guidelines of the WHO/UNHCR Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP), and will train new providers on the mhGAP model. She/he will develop standard operating procedures for providing psychological support and psychiatric care, as well as psychosocial support through group psychoeducation and community-based programs. She/he will represent IRC at all mental health working group meetings.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Program Coordination:
- Coordinate mental health needs assessments;
- Organize regular meetings on mental health with health program managers and the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) team, in collaboration with other technical coordinators;
- Ensure that mental health and psychosocial support are fully integrated into the various sectors of the health program (primary health care, sexual and reproductive health, nutrition, environmental health) and other IRC programs (WPE and ERD);
- Coordinate the implementation of all interventions in the field of mental health and psychosocial support
- Contribute to capacity building for the MHPSS team to enable them to effectively carry out their duties and ensure a smooth transition;
- Participate in capacity building for local partners (Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, United Nations agencies, etc.) in the field of mental health and psychosocial support;
- Contribute to the development of new funding proposals for mental health and psychosocial support;

**Evaluation and Monitoring of the Quality of Clinical and Community Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services**

- Conduct a situational analysis to identify and assess mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) needs in IRC’s areas of operation in Chad
- Provide formative supervision and/or refresher training for healthcare providers and community health workers.
- Provide specialized mental health consultations and psychosocial support to people with specific needs, including survivors of gender-based violence
- Support the organization of community-based services to improve care, follow-up, and referrals between the community and health facilities.
- Conduct formative supervision of health workers to improve the quality of mental health services provided in health facilities and the community using IRC supervision checklists.
- Ensure that essential medicines and psychotropic drugs approved by the Ministry of Public Health (MSP)/WHO are available in health facilities and that they are properly stored and prescribed by providers.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, Learning, and Reporting**

- In collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator, conduct a monthly analysis of mental health and psychosocial support data and share the database and report with the Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribute to improving the quality of periodic health program reports and donor reports.
- Support the monitoring and evaluation framework for the mental health program through regular data analysis and supervision of program activities in the field;
- Document lessons learned, innovative approaches, and the generation of information and evidence to contribute to IRC’s overall learning;
- Work with the MEAL Coordinator and program managers to ensure that health data collection systems meet the requirements of IRC, the Ministry of Public Health (MSP), and donors

**Partnership, Coordination, and Representation**

- Represent IRC at meetings with partners from the Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, and United Nations agencies working in the mental health and psychosocial support sector
- Participate in the development of the mental health working group’s roadmap
- Provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Public Health in the development and review of national policies, guidelines, standards, protocols, and programs/modules.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Direct Supervisor: Senior Health Coordinator
- Positions under direct supervision: Mental Health Manager in MIP with the Medical Doctor responsible for the health program
- Indirect supervision: Deputy Director of Programs
- Internal: Communications, Protection, ERD, Grants, Finance & Logistics Departments
- External: Government partners, humanitarian NGOs, and United Nations agencies

**Job requirements:**

- Advanced degree in clinical mental health, preferably a medical degree with a specialty in psychiatry and experience in neurology;
- Three years of professional experience in the development and management of mental health and psychosocial support programs, preferably in emergency situations or refugee camps;
- In addition to the clinical degree, an additional degree in public health is preferred.
- Knowledge of and experience applying the IASC MHPSS guidelines and best practices as part of previous professional experience.
- Experience in assessment, program design, technical training, and supervision using the WHO’s Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP).
- Flexibility in work;
- Ability to work independently while also being an excellent team leader;
- Technical expertise in program development and in assessing and facilitating training needs;
- Strong organizational and supervisory skills.
- Strong analytical skills demonstrating an understanding of current concepts, priorities, and issues related to monitoring, data collection, and program evaluation;
- Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work in a multicultural environment;
- Fluency in French is required; fluency in English is a plus.

**Work Environment:**

**Security:** He or she will be based in Hadjer Hadid and will travel frequently to IRC’s areas of operation. This is an unaccompanied position.

**Gender Equality**: The IRC is committed to reducing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that enable women to participate in the workforce, including parental leave, safety protocols that take into account the specific needs of men and women, and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**The IRC is an equal opportunity employer**. The IRC evaluates all candidates based on merit, without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability.

**French Version:**

**DESCRIPTION :**

IRC a commencé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire causée par l’afflux de réfugiés du Darfour à l’est du Tchad. L'assistance aux réfugiés soudanais s’est étendue à la gestion de onze camps dans l'Est et d'un camp dans l'Ouest en apportant un appui aux réfugiés et aux communautés locales en matière de santé, nutrition et eau, hygiène et assainissement. En 2012, IRC a étendu sa couverture géographique dans la province du Guéra où l’organisation travaille actuellement dans cinq districts sanitaires et fournit des services de prévention et de traitement de la malnutrition à la population locale ainsi que des activités de planification familiale, de prévention des violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et de réponse à celles-ci. En mai 2016, IRC a établi sa présence dans la province du Lac pour répondre à la crise liée à Boko Haram. L’IRC Tchad s'engage dans son plan d'action stratégique 2022-2024 à continuer à fournir des services humanitaires essentiels en santé, nutrition et protection / VBG, tout en améliorant le bien-être économique et en renforçant la résilience des bénéficiaires, en particulier des femmes et des filles. L’IRC Tchad continuera à travailler avec et à soutenir étroitement les acteurs étatiques / ministères sectoriels des domaines clés afin que les actions de l'IRC s'intègrent dans les politiques nationales pour assurer une meilleure appropriation des actions entreprises.

**Description du poste:**

Sous la supervision directe du Senior Health Coordinator, le spécialiste de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial basé à Hadjer Hadid sera responsable de la gestion globale et de la mise en œuvre du programme de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (SMSPS) de qualité dans toutes les zones d’intervention d’IRC et plus spécifiquement dans les camps de réfugiés. Le spécialiste en santé mentale travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le programme de santé mentale du ministère de la Santé publique (MSP), le HCR, l'IRC, HIAS et tous les membres du groupe de travail en santé mentale au Tchad afin de faciliter la coordination des interventions en santé mentale dans le pays et renforcer leur intégration dans le paquet minimum des activités fournies dans les centres de santé et les hôpitaux. Le spécialiste de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial supervisera les agents de santé dans la fourniture des services de prévention, de diagnostic et de traitement des patients souffrant de troubles mentaux, neurologiques et de toxicomanie en utilisant les directives du programme d'action pour les lacunes en matière de santé mentale (mhGAP) de l'OMS / HCR et formera de nouveaux prestataires sur le modèle mhGAP. Elle / il développera des procédures opérationnelles standard pour la fourniture d'un soutien psychologique et de soins psychiatriques, ainsi qu’un soutien psychosocial par le biais de la psychoéducation de groupe et de programmes communautaires. Elle /Il représentera IRC dans toutes les réunions du groupe de travail en santé mentale.

**Responsabilités principales :**

**Coordination de programme :**

- Coordonner les évaluations des besoins en santé mentale ;
- Organiser des réunions régulières sur la santé mentale avec les gestionnaires du programme santé et l’équipe SMSPS en collaboration avec les autres coordinateurs techniques ;
- S’assurer que la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial sont pleinement intégrés aux différents secteurs du programme santé (santé primaire, santé sexuelle et reproductive, nutrition, santé environnementale) et aux autres programmes de l’IRC (WPE et ERD) ;
- Coordonner la mise en œuvre de toutes les interventions dans le domaine de la SMSPS
- Contribuer au renforcement des capacités de l’équipe SMSPS pour leur permettre d’assurer efficacement leurs fonctions et d’assurer la relève ;
- Participer au renforcement des capacités des partenaires locaux (MSP, ONG, agences des Nations Unies, etc.) dans le domaine de la santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial.
- Contribuer à l’élaboration de nouvelles propositions de financement en santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial;

**Évaluation et suivi de la qualité des services cliniques et communautaires de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial**

- Mener une analyse de la situation afin d'identifier et d'évaluer les besoins en SMSPS dans les zones d’intervention de IRC au Tchad
- Réaliser des supervisions formatives et/ou des recyclages à l’intention des prestataires de soins et des agents de santé communautaires.
- Réaliser les consultations spécialisées en santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial des personnes ayant des besoins spécifiques, y compris les survivants des VBG
- Apporter un appui à l’organisation de l’offre des services communautaires pour une meilleure prise en charge, le suivi et le référencement entre la communauté et les établissements de santé.
- Réaliser les supervisions formatives des agents de santé afin d’améliorer la qualité de services de santé mentale fournis dans les établissements de santé et la communauté à l'aide des listes de contrôle de supervision d’IRC.
- S’assurer que les médicaments essentiels et les psychotropes approuvés par le MSP/OMS sont disponibles dans les établissements de santé et qu’ils sont correctement stockés et prescrits par les prestataires.

**Suivi, évaluation, recherche, apprentissage et rapportage**

- En collaboration avec le Coordinateur MEAL, faire une analyse mensuelle des données de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial et partager la base des données et le rapport avec le Senior Health Coordinator.
- Contribuer à l’amélioration de la qualité des rapports périodiques du programme santé et des rapports bailleurs.
- Soutenir le dispositif de suivi et évaluation appliqué au programme de santé mentale à travers des analyses régulières des données et la supervision des activités du programme sur le terrain ;
- Documenter les leçons apprises, les approches innovantes et la production d’informations et de données probantes afin de participer à l’apprentissage global d’IRC ;
- Travailler avec le Coordinateur MEAL et les responsables du programme afin de s’assurer que les systèmes de collecte des données santé remplissent les exigences d’IRC, du MSP et des bailleurs.

**Partenariat, Coordination et Représentation**

- Représenter IRC aux réunions avec les partenaires du ministère de la santé, les ONG et les agences des Nations Unies qui interviennent dans le secteur de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial
- Participer à l’élaboration de la feuille de route du groupe de travail en santé mentale
- Apporter une assistance technique au MSP dans l’élaboration et l’examen des politiques, directives, normes, protocoles, programmes/modules nationaux.

**Principales relations de travail:**

- **Superviseur Hiérarchique :** Senior Health Coordinator
**Position sous supervision directe :** Manager Santé Mentale en MIP avec le Médecin responsable du programme santé
- **Supervision indirecte:** Directeur adjoint des Programmes
- **Internes :** Département de communication, Protection, ERD, Grants, Finance & logistique
- **Externes** *:* Les partenaires de l’État, ONG humanitaires & Agences des Nations Unies

**Exigences du poste:**

- Diplôme supérieur en santé mentale clinique, de préférence un diplôme de médecin avec une spécialisation en psychiatrie et une expérience en neurologie ;
- Trois années d'expérience professionnelle dans le développement et la gestion de programmes de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial, de préférence dans les situations d'urgence ou dans des camps de réfugiés ;
- En plus du diplôme clinique, un diplôme supplémentaire en santé publique est préférable.
- Connaissance et expérience d’application des directives et des bonnes pratiques de l’IASC en matière de SMSPS dans le cadre de son expérience professionnelle antérieure.
- Expérience de l'évaluation, de la conception de programmes, de la formation technique et de la supervision à l'aide du programme d'action contre les lacunes en santé mentale (mhGAP) de l'OMS.
- Flexibilité dans le travail ;
- Capacité à travailler de manière autonome tout en étant un excellent chef d'équipe ;
- Une expertise technique dans l’élaboration de programme et dans l’évaluation et facilitation des besoins en formation ;
- Solides compétences en matière d'organisation et de supervision.
- Solides capacités d’analyse démontrant une compréhension des concepts, priorités et problèmes actuels en matière de suivi, de collecte de données et d'évaluation de programmes.
- Solides compétences interpersonnelles et capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel.
- La maîtrise de la langue française est requise ; la maîtrise de l'anglais est un atout.

**Environnement de travail :**

**Sécurité :** Il (elle) sera basé/e à Hadjer Hadid avec des déplacements fréquents dans les zones d’intervention d’IRC.Le poste est non accompagné**.**

**Égalité des sexes :** L'IRC s'est engagé à réduire l'écart entre les sexes dans les postes de direction. Nous offrons des avantages qui permettent aux femmes de participer à la vie active, notamment un congé parental, des protocoles de sécurité tenant compte des spécificités des hommes et des femmes et d'autres avantages et allocations de soutien.

**L'IRC est un employeur soucieux de l'égalité des chances. L'IRC** examine tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans considération de race, de sexe, de couleur, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, d'état civil, de statut d'ancien combattant ou de handicap.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Tupande Health, Safety, Security, and Transport (HSST) Coordinator
jobs.description:
## Job Description

Seeking a strategic leaders to lead Transport, OSH, and Security operations. You will manage a team, drive efficiency and compliance, and optimize budgets to ensure a safe, cost-effective environment for Tupande staff and partners.

## Job Level

JL 5

## Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Expected Manager

Ignetius Mukokho

## Will this position be managing others?

Yes, One Transport and Dispatch Senior Supervisor JL4 and three Senior Transport Officers JL2

## Key Job Responsibilities

Manage the Transport workstream.

- Oversee transport workstream daily operations to maintain high-quality standards and exceptional service provision.
- Implement and audit transport workstream management systems to maintain expected performance standards.
- Manage the transport workstream assets through their life cycle for adequate work resourcing.
- Manage large and minor transport workstream projects, ensuring timely completion and customer satisfaction.
- Act as the primary decision-maker for day-to-day transport operational roadblocks, resolving driver or vehicle issues that the supervisors cannot handle.
- Enforce transport policies and maintenance schedules, ensuring the supervisors keep vehicles compliant, clean, and roadworthy.

Support the Occupational Safety and Health workstream

- Engage with relevant internal and external stakeholders to plan, implement, and complete annual OSH audits and related training.
- Organize all audit reports and training certificates for ease of sharing with relevant stakeholders
- Support in overseeing the OSH compliance for all relevant Tupande locations across all our regions of operation.
- Coordinate the implementation of all OSH audit recommendations to ensure 100% implementation rate across all audited locations.

Support Security Operations

- Act as the primary daily contact for the Vendor Security Manager regarding routine deployment updates, ad-hoc requests, and immediate operational issues.
- Validate the daily/weekly reports submitted by the security service provider against the internal observations to ensure "ghost guards" or missed shifts are flagged before invoicing.
- Follow up with the vendor's technical team on maintenance and track their turnaround time to ensure they meet the maintenance Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
- Collaborate with the Security service provider during initial incident responses; ensure the vendor’s Incident Reports capture the full internal context and accuracy required.
- Track recurring performance issues to provide data and talking points for the HSST lead during the monthly stakeholder sync-ups.
- Coordinate with the security vendor to ensure access control protocols are being enforced on the ground as per Tupande’s policy across all locations.

Budget and Cost Management

- Collate and track expenditure data for Transport, OSH, and Security to assist in budget analysis.
- Analyse HSST workstream expenditure to develop strategies to manage or reduce recurring expenses while maintaining quality.
- Support in preparation of monthly BvA reports for leadership review.
- Monitor budget levels to curb overspends and achieve 10% budget savings annually.
- Review vendor invoices against LPOs to ensure accurate vendor payments

People Management

- Recruit the right team members to fill any personnel gaps.
- Identify and facilitate opportunities for professional growth and development.
- Develop and train the team on HSST workstream performance metrics so they know what success in their roles looks like.
- Track, audit, and report on HSST workstream performance metrics to ensure the team achieves performance expectations.
- Identify potential future leaders within the team and develop their skills to prepare them for leadership roles.
- Foster a collaborative and inclusive workplace culture, implementing initiatives to boost team morale and motivation.

## Top Skills and Qualifications

Technical skills:

- Google Suite applications, i.e., Google Sheets and Google Docs.
- Proficiency in software and systems that manage and track transport operations.
- Experience with tools used for raising PRs and managing vendor payments.

Knowledge:

- Knowledge of fleet management and logistics principles, including route efficiency, scheduling maintenance, conducting safety checks, and ensuring proper vehicle performance.
- Familiarity with safety regulations and compliance standards in the transport industry.
- Knowledge of applicable safety regulations and transport industry-specific compliance requirements.
- Knowledge of OSHA and safety regulations in Kenya.
- Ability to conduct a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment to assist the HSST Lead.
- Knowledge of fire suppression systems and evacuation drill protocols.
- Understanding of security and basic access controls, technology and regulation
- SLA management and understanding of how to hold private security firms accountable to Guard Force Instructions (GFIs).

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Sponsor International Candidates

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

12 November 2026. Applications after this date will be accepted on a rolling basis.

*For more information reach out to ignetius.mukokho@oneacrefund.org*

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

The IRC is implementing programs in the West Bank and Gaza working closely with partners and implementing directly in health, protection, WASH, early childhood development, and cash programming to meet the most critical humanitarian needs.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Grants Coordinator is responsible for the timely and effective management of a multi-donor grant portfolio. This position manages all functions of the grants unit at IRC oPt, inclusive of proposal development, reporting, donor compliance, and other administration.

The Grants Coordinator reports to the Deputy Director for Programs (DDP) The position will work closely with the MEAL Coordinator, Partnerships Coordinator, finance department, and program sector leads.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Proposal Development**

- In collaboration with the DDP and HQ colleagues, proactively identify new funding opportunities by monitoring and analyzing donor strategies and funding trends.
- Support the DDP and program sector leads in the development of new program design.
- Prepare for and lead Go/No Go meetings for funding opportunities as required.
- Assist in ensuring that Go/No Go discussions and program design are consistent with the SAP partnership ambition and program approach.
- In coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator, proactively engage partners in program development efforts.
- Ensure robust and effective representation and resourcing of IRC’s partnership strategy, approach and management in donor proposals and reports.
- Oversee the development of all concept notes and proposals, acting as or delegating responsibility for lead writer or editor. Develop efficient process management tools for proposal development.
- Outline and communicate clear roles and responsibilities and timelines for each department. Facilitate effective cross-departmental coordination.
- Thoroughly review all proposal documents to ensure coherence throughout narratives, logframes, and budgets.
- Act as focal point with HQ during proposal review, editing, and submission.
- Ensure all proposal outputs are accurate, complete, of high quality, and submitted on time.

**Grants Management**

- Act as focal point for communications with HQ on all grants administration functions.
- Review donor agreements and coordinate their review and signature with relevant HQ offices. Coordinate the approval of pre-award spending as required.
- Coordinate with the Partnership Lead to obtain any necessary donor approvals relating to partnerships.
- Lead and/or support all project revisions, amendments, and budget realignments.
- In close coordination with Finance team, facilitate BvAs to bring teams together to ensure sound financial management
- Serve as the country program expert on the facilitation of Project Cycle Meetings (PCM), including project design, opening, implementation, closing, and learning meetings.
- Actively promote full partner participation in program delivery in the context of PCM.
- Maintain and disseminate a regularly updated grants tracker.
- Ensure all departmental communication with IRC colleagues and donors is constructive, clear, and organized.
- Maintain a well-organized and comprehensive information management and grants filing system.
- Ensure IRC’s internal Opportunity Tracking Information System (OTIS) is updated and maintained throughout the awards lifecycle
- Participate in due diligence processes and collaborative partnership risk management as appropriate.
- Strengthen the capacity of IRC and partner staff in grants management functions by facilitating trainings and providing targeted support as required.

**Donor Compliance**

- Provide programs and operations teams with routine technical guidance to ensure that all grants are implemented in compliance with IRC and donor regulations.
- Coordinate with HQ on specialized compliance matters as required.
- Proactively raise potential compliance issues to senior management; work closely with HQ compliance colleagues to resolve any related concerns.
- Disseminate existing resources on donor compliance, liaise with regional counterparts for the development and updating of compliance cheat sheets for all grants.
- In coordination with the DDP and Advocacy Coordinator, assist in ensuring appropriate and effective IRC and donor visibility in program sites and materials.

**Reporting**

- Oversee the development and delivery of all internal and external reports in collaboration with the programs, finance, and MEAL departments.
- Maintain a comprehensive reports tracker and regularly communicate with all relevant team members about upcoming deadlines and specific report requirements.
- Lead the production of high-quality and well-written reports which meet donor and IRC requirements.
- Thoroughly review and confirm that all reports and supplementary documents are complete and accurate.
- Coordinate HQ and technical unit reviews and approvals prior to donor submission.
- Ensure strict compliance with internal and donor deadlines.

**Departmental Leadership and Staff Management**

- Lead the grants unit and provide professional development opportunities for staff as needed.
- Ensure clear delineation of roles and responsibilities and logical portfolio allocation for all team members.
- Coordinate performance management within the department and ensure a culture of high performance through staff engagement and accountability.
- Identify and support capacity building of grants team and as requested other team members to understand IRC’s Grants processes
- Oversee recruitment of new staff as required. Ensure comprehensive onboarding and training for new hires.

**Other**

Other relevant duties as assigned by supervisor to further IRC programs.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Between five - six years of experience in humanitarian grants management in a multi-donor, multi-sector working environment.
- Demonstrated experience in an inter-departmental coordination role and the ability to communicate with and balance the priorities of a range of stakeholders.
- Extensive experience leading the development of large multi-sector funding proposals.
- Advanced skills in donor report drafting and compilation, including the coordination of inputs and development of complex documents across different departments.
- In-depth knowledge of institutional donor compliance required. Knowledge of ECHO, SIDA, GFFO, BMZ and Gulf donor requirements a particular advantage.
- Exceptional English writing and editing skills required. Able to draft and edit detailed documents for donor submission with minimal oversight.
- Previous experience in a conflict-affected or protracted crisis setting preferred.
- Exceptional advance planning and organizational skills. Able to effectively prioritize and follow multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated positive attitude that can positively and constructively engage across programmatic and support departments

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances

**IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.** IRC considerall applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: SOUTH SUDAN -HUMAN RESSOURCES HEAD OF DEPARTMENT - JUBA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/02/2026**
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**
**Location: Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement, this year El Nino), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- South Sudan has also been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of October 2026, more than 1,400,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may raise further division and tensions.

\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.

As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk, Malakal and Ulang (since 2025). The response has focused on cholera, response to acute food insecurity and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up since 2025.

The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

'The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The HR team is 1/ HR Coordinator+ 1 Deputy Human Resource Coordinator and one HR Assistant

## About the job

**General objective:**

The HR Head of Department oversees the implementation of Solidarités International’s (SI) Human Resources framework and policies within the Country Team, ensures the smooth administrative running of the Country Office and that all staff comply with SI procedures, donor procedures and the laws of the country concerned. They regularly visit field offices to ensure the harmonisation and application of these procedures across the entire Country Office.

They are the point of contact within the Country Office for all matters relating to human resources, and acts as the liaison between headquarters and the Country Office on these matters.

**The main challenges:**

- Manage a team that needs support
- Complex and demandind labor aurhorities with different specificities depending on the location
- Growing teams in all bases that need follow up on HR procedures
- Creation of Policies on missing procedures
- Communication with other NGOs in the country
- Strong collaboration with other departments for various issues
- Follow up with a high number of expats on their documentation and off-boardings when needed

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Stabilize the Private Insurance payments and follow ups
- Stabilize the Shared Cost processes to be on time
- Follow up on revised DW Policy, updated function grid & salary grid
- Visit the bases and introduce himself/herself to the teams and to authorities

**Security constraints:**

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.

The situation in South Sudan is volatile, please document yourself before applying. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves

There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.

Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).

In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : BA in Psychology, Business Administration or similar, MA in HR preferable

Experience in the humanitarian sector : More than 5 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. HOMERE user and familiarity with SI HR tools preferable
2. Good and comfortable to use Excel
