jobs.title: Consultoría técnica – Instalación y puesta en funcionamiento de la planta de RCD y unidad de producción de áridos - Venezuela
jobs.description:
## 1. Contexto de la Organización

CESVI es una asociación laica e independiente fundada en Italia en 1985 que trabaja por la solidaridad mundial y el ideal de la justicia social a través de acciones humanitarias de desarrollo. El mismo nombre CESVI, *Cooperazione e Sviluppo* (Cooperación y Desarrollo), expresa su filosofía de acción, basada en la promoción del protagonismo de sus beneficiarios en favor de su propio progreso, a fin de que la ayuda internacional no se reduzca a una acción temporal benéfica, sino que promueva un auténtico desarrollo sostenible de las poblaciones más necesitadas.

CESVI está presente en Venezuela desde 2019, desarrollando una respuesta humanitaria cada vez más integrada frente a la prolongada crisis socioeconómica y humanitaria del país en los estados de Amazonas, Distrito Capital, Falcón, Miranda, Sucre, La Guaira (Vargas) y Zulia. Durante este período, CESVI ha trabajado principalmente en Protección, incluyendo violencia basada en género (VBG), protección infantil, prevención de la explotación y la trata, gestión de casos, apoyo psicosocial y de salud mental (MHPSS), asistencia legal y salud sexual y reproductiva; Seguridad Alimentaria y Necesidades Básicas, mediante asistencia alimentaria, transferencias monetarias y cupones, y apoyo con artículos esenciales para los hogares; WASH, incluyendo acceso a agua segura, asistencia e iniciativas de promoción de higiene; y Medios de Vida y Recuperación Temprana, apoyando a hogares vulnerables para recuperar sus ingresos y fortalecer su resiliencia. A principios de 2026, CESVI puso en marcha un proyecto para la Movilidad Segura de los venezolanos que regresan al país. Los programas de CESVI en Venezuela cuentan con una base de financiamiento diversificada que incluye donantes institucionales, fundaciones y fondos privados, lo que permite a la organización implementar tanto intervenciones humanitarias a gran escala como respuestas más flexibles y focalizadas.

Tras el terremoto del 24 de junio de 2026, CESVI amplió significativamente sus operaciones de emergencia para incluir Alojamiento de Emergencia y Artículos No Alimentarios (NFI), WASH, Seguridad Alimentaria, asistencia monetaria multipropósito y sectorial mediante efectivo y cupones electrónicos, Protección y MHPSS, Movilidad Segura, Recuperación Temprana y Medios de Vida, combinando asistencia inmediata para salvar vidas con apoyo a la recuperación y resiliencia a más largo plazo.

### Objetivos específicos

- Planificar, coordinar y supervisar técnicamente la instalación y puesta en funcionamiento de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos en El Junko, asegurando condiciones operativas, de seguridad, ambientales y de calidad adecuadas, en coordinación con CESVI y el equipo técnico GIRS de HELVETAS.
- Organizar, gestionar y verificar las actividades necesarias para instalar la infraestructura, servicios básicos, maquinaria y equipamiento de ambas unidades.
- Desarrollar los procedimientos operativos estándar y preparar al personal operador para una operación segura, mediante formación y pruebas de funcionamiento y producción.

## 3. Responsabilidades y Funciones Principales

**Resultado 1: Instalación de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD** **y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos en el Junko**

- Verificar el estado actual de los Sitios al inicio de las instalaciones de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos.
- Coordina con el equipo de expertos de GIRS de HELVETAS y la unidad de compras de bienes y servicios asignados al programa, para la Construcción de infraestructura en la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos, la provisión de servicios básicos y para la adquisición de Equipos, materiales e insumos (comités de evaluación, cotizaciones, licitaciones, cuadros comparativos, órdenes de compra, etc).
- En coordinación con el equipo de expertos de GIRS de HELVETAS, realizar el replanteo de la Línea de Producción de áridos y la Planta de RCD en función del levantamiento topográfico y el estudio de la línea base.
- Coordinar y dar seguimiento a la instalación de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD en el Junko y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos, en el marco de la aplicación de las políticas institucionales, principalmente del Manual de Compras, Código de Conducta, etc.
- Coadyubar a la obtención de eventuales autorizaciones ambientales para la instalación de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos
- Coordinar la logística durante la Instalación de la Planta de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos.
- Dirigir la Instalación adecuada de la infraestructura, servicios básicos y equipamiento Adquirido para la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y La Unidad de Producción de Áridos
- Realizar pruebas de funcionamiento de equipos, maquinaria y otras instalaciones adquiridas.

**Resultado 2:Planificación Operativa de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD en el Junko, y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos**

- Identificación de capacidades, en los operarios que realizaran las actividades de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos, conformando las cuadrillas por turno en cada área de trabajo (Demolición, CDT-Producción de áridos y Planta de Tratamiento de RCD)
- Asignación de puestos dentro la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos de acuerdo a capacidades identificadas, por turnos.
- Capacitación de operarios en temas de Operación Segura de la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos (Seguridad y Protección laboral)
- Capacitación especifica en el manejo de equipos, roles y responsabilidades por tipo de puesto asignado
- Establecer procedimientos operativos estándar para la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD que incluya también la provisión de servicios básicos, especialmente abastecimiento de agua y el saneamiento (gestión de los baños) y abastecimiento de materiales e insumos para la planta de tratamiento de RCD (especialmente áridos y cemento)
- Realizar Pruebas de Operación y Producción en la Planta de Tratamiento de RCD y la Unidad de Producción de Áridos

## 4. Productos y Plazos de Entrega

El/La consultor/a deberá presentar los productos a la Jefe de Misión y Coordinador de Emergencia de CESVI y la Gerencia del Programa de Respuesta al Terremoto en Venezuela de HELVETAS:

Producto 1. Plan de trabajo detallado: cronograma, metodología, recursos y coordinación técnica para la instalación. **Plazo propuesto: A los 3 días hábiles**

Producto 2. Informe de preparación operativa: selección/asignación y capacitación de operadores de planta, unidad de áridos y separación en origen; procedimientos operativos estándar (POE/SOP).

**Plazo propuesto: A los 60 días hábiles**

Producto 3. Informe final de instalación y puesta en marcha: evidencias de montaje, resultados de pruebas de equipos, operación y producción, ajustes efectuados y recomendaciones.

**Plazo propuesto: A los 45 días hábiles**

CESVI podrá solicitar aclaraciones o correcciones antes de aprobar los productos. Los informes y documentos se entregarán en formato PDF y en versión editable cuando corresponda.

Todos los productos serán materia de aprobación por parte de la Gerencia del Programa de Respuesta al Terremoto en Venezuela de HELVETAS y a Coordinador de Emergencia de CESVI por lo que cualquier observación, atingencia o similar que pueda efectuarse sobre el producto y que merezca subsanaciones, aclaraciones o similares por parte de **EL CONSULTOR**, serán solicitadas a través del Jefe de Mision de CESVI por ser responsable de aprobar y garantizar la entrega final de los productos.

Los productos, las observaciones / comentarios a los productos y el levantamiento de las observaciones o ajustes a dichos productos se podrán entregar vía e-mail en el formato estabilizado (tipo PDF) y el formato modificable (Word).

## 6. RESPONSABILIDADES DEL CONTRATO

a. Nivel de Coordinación

Reporta al Gerente del Programa de Respuesta al Terremoto en Venezuela de HELVETAS y administrativamente a Jefe de Misión de CESVI. Coordina con el Equipo de Expertos GIRS de HELVETAS y con el Coordinador de Emergencia de CESVI.

b. Derecho de Propiedad intelectual

Los derechos de propiedad intelectual de los productos y documentos elaborados por la Empresa Consultora son propiedad de HELVETAS, respectivamente, así como el derecho a utilizar la información, a publicarla o comunicarla a terceros total o parcialmente por cualquier medio.

c. Confidencialidad

El/la Consultor/a no podrá comentar, divulgar, reproducir ni comunicar bajo ningún concepto el contenido de los documentos y registros oficiales a que tenga acceso por el trabajo que realice como consecuencia de este Contrato, salvo que sea autorizado expresamente por HELVETAS. Estas obligaciones se extienden hasta después de concluido su contrato.

d. Seguros

HELVETAS proporcionará al Consultor/a un seguro contra accidentes durante la vigencia del contrato y cubrirá gastos de transporte local para desplazarse a las áreas de intervención del programa y/u para llevar a cabo otras actividades relacionada al desarrollo de los productos solicitados en el marco de esta consultoría.

## 8. PERFIL REQUERIDO

**Formación Académica obligatoria:**

- Arquitectura o Ingeniería Civil.
- Deseable mas no indispensable: maestría en Gestión ambiental, Economía Circular, Gestión Integral de Residuos Sólidos, o programas afines

**Experiencia profesional obligatoria:**

- 7 años mínimo de experiencia profesional relevante.
- 3 años mínimo de experiencia especifica en entidades privadas, gubernamentales o no gubernamentales que incluye de forma referencial más no limitativa en lo siguiente:
- Experiencia Producción de Bloques y prefabricados de hormigón.
- Experiencia en producción de áridos reciclados.
- Conocimiento del marco jurídico de la seguridad laboral en el país
- Experiencia de trabajo en equipo.
- Deseable más no indispensable, experiencia de trabajo en organismos de cooperación internacional.
- Disponibilidad para desplazarse frecuentemente a El Junko.

## 9. SALVAGUARDA Y POLÍTICAS INSTITUCIONALES

CESVI mantiene una política de tolerancia cero frente a la explotación, el abuso y el acoso, así como frente a cualquier daño contra niños, niñas y personas adultas en situación de vulnerabilidad. La persona consultora deberá observar las políticas institucionales de salvaguarda, protección, confidencialidad, prevención del fraude y Código de Conducta aplicables durante toda la prestación del servicio.

Los datos, registros y documentos obtenidos durante la consultoría deberán ser tratados confidencialmente y utilizados exclusivamente para los fines autorizados. Los productos elaborados y sus condiciones de uso y titularidad se regirán por el contrato suscrito por las partes.

jobs.title: Baseline Study Consultant
jobs.company: Amal Organization for Relief and Development
jobs.description:
**Baseline Study Consultant**

**Organisation**

Amal Organization for Relief and Development

**Position**

Baseline Study Consultant

**Type of Contract**

Short-Term Consultancy

**Location**

Home-based with field mission travel to Aleppo, Syria

**Relevant languages**

English, Arabic

**Application Deadline**

17.11.2026

**Starting Date**

01.12.2026

**Project Title**

Fostering climate-resilient livelihoods,
inclusive learning environments,
and social cohesion in conflict-affected Aleppo

**Background and Organisational Setting**

This baseline study is commissioned, prior to project implementation, under the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) budget for development projects run by private organisations.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Amal Organization for Relief and Development (Amal)being the local implementing partner.

The project aims to sustainably strengthen the resilience and recovery capacities of conflict-affected communities in Eastern Aleppo through an integrated approach that links livelihoods, education, and social cohesion. In the livelihoods component, market-oriented and sustainable vocational training, entrepreneurship support, on-the-job training and apprenticeship schemes, as well as small grants will be provided to promote sustainable income opportunities. In parallel, the project supports access to quality education by rehabilitating educational infrastructure, integrating mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and social-emotional learning (SEL), and strengthening teachers’ capacities. Complementary activities will foster social cohesion through dialogue-based youth- and women-led initiatives, contributing to trust-building in conflict-affected Aleppo. By combining these components, the project contributes to community stabilisation and the creation of long-term development prospects.
Direct target group: 3,850 people

**Baseline Study Objectives**

The purpose of the baseline study is to provide SoH with a sound basis for developing a complete project concept, by identifying project prerequisites, opportunities and risks. This process includes an assessment of the baseline of the proposed project intervention to assess if it can plausibly achieve planned objectives given existing contextual realities.

This comprehensive study will verify relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the proposed project intervention. The study will provide concrete and practical recommendations that will assist with the finalisation of project design elements, including the logframe, risk analysis, problem analysis and relevance of the proposed project intervention, stakeholder analysis, among others.

The study will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process regarding the funding of the proposed project activities.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The selected Consultant will work in close cooperation with the responsible SoH Officer and the local implementing partner.

The duties and responsibilities of the consultant will include:

- Develop a work plan outlining the proposed research methodology, geographical coverage, and schedule to conduct the baseline study,
- Carry out a project site visit to the project location to conduct research, collect data and establish contact with the local implementing partner, potential beneficiaries and relevant project stakeholders,
- Review existing policies and structures, government development strategies as well as relevant studies and research projects that could serve as a basis for the baseline study,

Identify relevant project stakeholders at various levels (local, district and national if applicable), including local governing bodies, academia and industry as well as lessons learned and best practises of similar on-going and implemented projects relevant to the project, including the identification and assessment of existing formal and informal organisational structures among the target groups, comprising their composition, membership, roles, capacities, representativeness and level of participation,

- Evaluate all available data and sources providing background information on identified issues, the problem analysis as well as the selected intervention and establish the baseline values for all indicators included in the project impact matrix using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods, including the respective data sources and measurement methods,
- Assess the proposed activities, as well as their timing and required financial resources.
- Assess the physical condition, safety, accessibility and functionality of the four selected schools and the existing VTC facilities, including relevant equipment and refurbishment needs,
- Examine institutional, technical, staffing and financial capacities of the selected implementing partner, as well as its relationship with the target group. Based on the findings, determine if there are areas in which capacities of the local implementing partner need to be developed,
- Review main governmental and non-governmental stakeholders with a purpose to see if there is a potential overlap or conflict of interest as well as opportunities for coordination with the aim of creating synergies and new cooperation partnerships, while also assessing the alignment of the proposed project with the national recovery plan,
- Examine the identified target group, its needs and role in the broader social context as well as the relevance of the planned project activities for addressing their needs,
- Assess the environmental and climate-related production practices of selected enterprises, including energy and water use, waste generation, raw material efficiency, procurement and processing practices.
- Identify potential obstacles and alternatives to overcome the foreseen challenges,
- Review and analyse all available project design elements and draft documents related to the project concept, if necessary,
- Critically review the planned project in terms of OECD/DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability (please see [http://www.oecd.org/development/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.html](http://www.oecd.org/development/evaluation/daccriteriaforevaluatingdevelopmentassistance.html)),
- Prepare a report containing the findings on the above items, specific recommendations for the project concept with a view to planning and implementing foreseen project activities.

**Expected Deliverables**

The study will produce the following deliverables:

- a baseline study outline, including the proposed methodology and data collection tools, table of content and a timeline of research activities (inception report) prior to the site visit to the project location,
- a summary containing a brief overview and the main findings of the study,
- Baseline values for all indicators included in the project impact matrix, specifying the respective data sources and measurement methods.
- a comprehensive report of a maximum of 30 pages with practical recommendations and relevant annexes,
- Findings and recommendations regarding the condition of the four selected schools and the existing VTC facilities, including identified refurbishment and equipment needs.
- a review of the main project design elements and provision of concrete recommendations for improvement,
- an analysis of the institutional structure required for project implementation, stipulating the roles and responsibilities of staff members involved, a detailed problem analysis, a stakeholder analysis, a revision of the target group, an analysis of the potential risks and recommendations on how to mitigate these risks, a schedule of project activities, a financial plan (planning budget), a detailed project logframe with SMART indicators for the project objective and results listing related activities and required resources,
- a “Do-no-harm analysis” including recommendations on how to mitigate potential harm and conflict situations that can potentially arise during or as a result of the project activities
- a Gender mainstreaming analysis identifying potential risks and recommendations to ensure gender equality in all aspects of the project design and implementation.

A template will be provided to serve as a guide and suggested structure for the final report.

**Process/Timeframe**

- A total duration of the assignment is up to 20 working days within the period of 01.12.2026 to 28.12.2026.
- A planning meeting with Amal, handover of relevant documents 1 day
- Initial document review and preparing inception report 3 days
- Sharing inception report with SoH and Amal 1 day
- Data collection site visit to a project location 5 days
- Data analysis, draft report with annexes, presenting to SoH 5 days
- Incorporating received feedback and finalising the report 5 days

**Qualifications and Experience**

Essential:

- Minimum of 5 years of project evaluation and/or implementation experience in the result-based management framework
- Proven experience of conducting baseline studies, evaluations and other research projects
- Technical and methodological knowledge to conduct research projects and formulate conclusions based on a solid methodology, assessing projects for relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of projects
- Experience working with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and partnered projects
- Access to technical expertise to assess the condition of the selected schools and identify needs for minor refurbishment works.
- Fluency in written and spoken English

Desirable:

- Experience in the relevant field
- Fluency in written and spoken Levantine Arabic
- Professional familiarity with the project country/region
- Practical experience of working for and/or evaluating BMZ-funded projects

**Academic Background**

An advanced level university degree (Masters’ degree or equivalent) in social sciences, public administration, international development studies, law and/or another relevant field. A first-level university degree in combination with additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted.

The consultant is to be independent and impartial with no liabilities to any other organisation or government entity regarding this evaluation.

Companies as well as independent consultants are invited for this tender. Female and differently abled candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

Please note that due to a large number of applications we may limit establishing contact to shortlisted applicants.

Bids received after deadline will not be considered. If offers are incomplete, bidders may be able to hand in missing documents within a deadline upon request by SoH.

The selection of the consultant will be conducted jointly by Amal and SoH. Interviews with shortlisted candidates will be held online.

The consultancy agreement will be set up by SoH and Amal. Consultancy agreements set up by consultants won’t be accepted.

**Criteria and weighting for the evaluation of the submitted proposals:**

1. Essential and desirable competencies, proposed methodology: 11 %
2. Financial proposal (fee): 11 %
3. Performance during interview: 35 %
4. Writing samples: 7 %
5. Minimum amount of years of relevant experience: 3 %
6. Language skills: 3 %

Annexe 1: Impact Matrix. Please download the annex by visiting the following link:

[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yH19NSOMraW08M_lYPBB0TmdmlDV6anU?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1yH19NSOMraW08M_lYPBB0TmdmlDV6anU?usp=sharing)

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. Amal Organization unequivocally prohibits and will not tolerate (zero tolerate) any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (whether sexual or otherwise), based on race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. Employees and associated personnel must strictly refrain from engaging in any discriminatory, harassing, or abusive behavior, whether physical, sexual, verbal, or otherwise, both within and outside the Amal organization.

**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**

Amal Organization recognizes that ensuring a secure environment for children begins with the recruitment of qualified employees equipped with the necessary competencies and skills to perform their duties effectively, safely, and reliably. This commitment is geared towards safeguarding children from all forms of exploitation, labor, or potential harm.

In our dedication to children's safety, our selection process incorporates comprehensive background checks, underscoring our unwavering commitment to preventing abuse and ensuring the well-being of children.

**SAFEGUARDING EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:**

In line with our commitment to fostering a secure and respectful work environment, the post holder is required to adhere to Amal's anti-harassment policy. This policy underscores our dedication to safeguarding the well-being of our staff by promoting a workplace culture characterized by mutual respect and professionalism. The role holder plays a vital part in this commitment, ensuring a supportive atmosphere and actively contributing to the safeguarding of their colleagues through the promotion of positive employee relations.

jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Country Director/Response Director, Central African Republic**, you will provide overall leadership and oversight of World Vision’s humanitarian and recovery response, ensuring programmes are timely, effective, compliant, secure, and adequately resourced. You will lead strategy execution, programme quality, financial and operational performance, risk management, donor compliance, and delivery of measurable impact for vulnerable children and communities affected by humanitarian crises. As the senior leader and principal representative, you will engage government authorities, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, church partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen coordination, mobilize resources, and advance recovery outcomes. You will ensure alignment with World Vision’s Child Well-Being objectives, humanitarian principles, national priorities, and organizational policies.

**1) Strategic Leadership and Response Management**

You will provide overall vision, leadership, and direction for the response, ensuring humanitarian and recovery programmes remain relevant, evidence-based, integrated, and responsive to evolving needs. You will oversee grant implementation, performance reviews, donor compliance, reporting, audits, risk management, sub-grants, consortium agreements, and implementing partners. You will strengthen grant-management capacity, maintain donor relationships, and ensure adequate funding to support response goals and long-term programme sustainability.

**2) Program Quality, Accountability, Learning, Reporting and Information Management**

You will ensure humanitarian programmes meet quality standards, deliver measurable impact, promote accountability to affected populations, and support evidence-based decision-making, learning, coordination, and continuous improvement.

**3) Resource Mobilization**

You will ensure sustainable and diversified funding by leading donor engagement, strategic partnerships, proposal development, and grant acquisition to achieve response objectives.

**4) Financial Management & Stewardship**

You will ensure sound financial management, accountability, and responsible utilization of organizational resources to maximize programme impact, maintain financial sustainability, and uphold stakeholder confidence.

**5) Risk Management, Compliance & Governance**

You will strengthen organizational resilience, accountability, governance, and ethical conduct by proactively identifying and managing risks, ensuring compliance with regulatory and donor requirements, and maintaining effective oversight mechanisms.

**6) External Representation, Partnerships, Advocacy, Communication and Visibility**

You will represent World Vision externally and strengthen strategic relationships that enhance humanitarian impact, resource mobilization, organizational visibility, and influence.

**7) Faith and Community Engagement**

You will strengthen engagement with churches, faith leaders, and faith-based organizations while promoting World Vision’s Christian identity, values, and faith-inspired approaches to sustainable change and child well-being.

**8) People Leadership and Organizational Culture**

You will build and sustain a high-performing, accountable, and values-driven workforce with the leadership capacity, organizational structure, and culture required to deliver quality programmes and achieve response objectives.

**9) Safeguarding, Ethics, Accountability and Compliance**

You will provide strategic leadership and oversight for safeguarding, ethics, accountability, and compliance, ensuring a safe, ethical, transparent, and accountable operating environment while protecting children, vulnerable adults, staff, and affected communities.

**10) Security, Staff Wellbeing and Safety**

You will provide strategic leadership and accountability for security, risk management, staff safety, well-being, and business continuity to safeguard personnel, assets, operations, beneficiaries, and organizational reputation while enabling effective programme delivery in a complex operating environment.

**Requirements include:**

- Over 15 years of progressive humanitarian leadership experience, including more than 7 years in senior country-level management roles, leading large-scale emergency and recovery operations in fragile, conflict-affected, and high-risk environments.
- Master's degree in International Development, Humanitarian Affairs, Public Administration, Business Administration, International Relations, Public Health, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Alternatively, a university degree in a relevant field combined with extensive humanitarian leadership experience.
- Advanced certification in Humanitarian Leadership, Emergency Management, Project Management, Organizational Leadership, or related disciplines.
- Proven track record managing complex multi-sector humanitarian responses, overseeing portfolios exceeding USD 20 million, and administering grants from major institutional donors such as Global Fund, USG-funding, ECHO, UN agencies, EU, SDC, Philantrhopy, etc..
- Extensive experience leading multicultural, multidisciplinary teams and engaging effectively with governments, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, civil society, media, and private-sector stakeholders, including serving as an organizational spokesperson.
- Strong expertise in humanitarian operations within war zones and crisis settings, fostering innovation and calculated risk-taking while managing competing priorities under pressure.
- Preferred background includes experience as a Country Director or Response Director, work in Central or West Africa, and service with faith-based organizations and international NGOs.

**Work Environment/Travel:**

- The position requires ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 25% of the time.
- Work hours are often in excess of 12 hours per day during difficult periods of the response.
- Responses are often mounted in insecure or natural disaster-prone contexts, which may disrupt normal work patterns and generate staff safety issues.
- Work and housing environments may at times be well below normal standards in terms of facilities, equipment, food availability and hygiene.

**Language Requirements**

- Full professional fluency in **English** and **French** (written and spoken).

**Applicant Types Accepted:** Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Expression of Interest – Inclusion Adviser, Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program
jobs.description:
**About DT Global**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**Program Context**

The Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program is a DFAT funded program that is part of the Pacific Australia Skills work in Solomon Islands. Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across Timor-Leste and the Pacific. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of prior Australian Government support for skills and training in Timor-Leste. The SIRIS program will focus on support for rural training centres (RTCs) and other training providers to strengthen their institutional capability, improve the quality and relevance of skills delivery, and respond effectively to labour-market needs. Effective delivery of the activity will require coordinated planning across program, operational and technical functions, with resources aligned to agreed activities and results.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Country Director in close collaboration with the SIRIS Activity Lead, the SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser will provide technical leadership and advice to strengthen Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) outcomes across the Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program. The SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser will also work closely with the Regional Inclusion Lead position to support inclusion outcomes across the broader work of Pacific Australia Skills in the Solomon Islands.

The role is responsible for operationalising the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy and Implementation Plan in Solomon Islands, ensuring that inclusion is systematically embedded across programme design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning. The SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser will work closely with staff, partners and stakeholders to strengthen inclusive approaches that promote equitable access, participation and outcomes for women, people with disabilities, youth and other underrepresented groups.

To strengthen inclusive practice at the country level, the SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser with the support of the regional Inclusion team, will facilitate professional development, coaching and capacity-building initiatives for Pacific Australia Skills staff, partners and stakeholders. The role will also support the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) and Communications teams to ensure inclusion is integrated into systems, reporting, knowledge products, communications and country planning processes.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

Pacific Australia Skills uses the term Inclusion to describe its work in advancing Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI). The Inclusion and Safeguarding Adviser will:

**Inclusion Leadership and Technical Advice**

- Lead the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy and Inclusion Implementation Plan across Solomon Islands.
- Provide technical advice on Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) throughout programme planning, implementation and review across Solomon Islands.
- Support programme teams and partners in Solomon Islands to identify and address barriers affecting participation and access.
- In line with the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy, promote inclusive programme design and delivery that supports equitable outcomes.
- Advise on practical and sustainable approaches to inclusion within skills development and training initiatives.

**Implementation, Capacity Development and Organisational Learning**

- Lead the implementation of inclusion specific activities outlined in the Solomon Islands Strategy and workplan
- In collaboration with the regional inclusion team, design and facilitate inclusion training, workshops and awareness initiatives for programme staff, partners and stakeholders in Solomon Islands.
- Deliver inclusion orientations for new staff, advisers and consultants in Solomon Islands.
- Provide coaching and mentoring to strengthen inclusion knowledge and practice.
- In collaboration with the regional inclusion team, develop practical inclusion resources, tools and guidance materials.
- Promote learning and sharing of good practices across programme teams.

**Inclusive Program Design and Partnership Support**

- Support partner organisations and stakeholders to strengthen institutional capacity and approaches for inclusion in Solomon Islands.
- Review programme activities and initiatives to ensure inclusive participation, engagement and accessibility.
- Work closely with partners in Solomon Islands to identify opportunities to improve participation of women, people with disabilities, youths and marginalized groups.
- Support integration of inclusion (gender equality, disability and social inclusion) considerations into work planning and activity design.

**Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning**

- Support the MEL team to integrate inclusion indicators within programme monitoring systems.
- Support in analysing participation and outcome data relating to gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion.
- Contribute to inclusion reporting requirements and programme performance reviews.
- Support evidence generation and learning activities to strengthen programme effectiveness.
- Document lessons learned and emerging good practice.
- Contribute to reflection workshops and participate in Pacific Australia Skills inclusion community of practice.

**Communications and Knowledge Sharing**

- Support development of accessible and inclusive communication products.
- Ensure diverse participant experiences are appropriately represented in programme communications.
- Contribute to inclusion success stories, case studies and knowledge products.
- Promote inclusive and accessible approaches to stakeholder engagement and communications.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Sector Strengthening**

- Build strong relationships with government agencies, training institutions, disability organisations, women's organisations and community stakeholders in Solomon Islands.
- Represent Pacific Australia Skills Solomon Islands at relevant inclusion and GEDSI forums.
- Establish and facilitate a Community of Practice focused on GEDSI learning and collaboration.
- Contribute to broader sector discussions that strengthen inclusion within skills development and training systems.
- Support strategic partnerships that advance inclusive development outcomes.
- Contribute to policy dialogue and systems strengthening initiatives relevant to inclusion within the skills and training sector in Solomon Islands.

**Other Duties**

- Contribute to positive working relationships across the SIRIS Programme and Pacific Australia Skills.
- Support organisational learning and continuous improvement.
- Undertake other reasonable tasks consistent with the objectives of the role and duties as required to ensure the smooth and effective delivery of Pacific Australia Skills in Solomon Islands.

## **Selection Criteria**

### **Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- Tertiary qualifications in gender, international development, social sciences, community development or another relevant field.
- Demonstrated experience in a similar role within development programs or donor-funded projects, preferably Australian Government within Solomon Islands.
- Willingness and ability to facilitate rather than direct and to provide support to build staff and partners’ knowledge, confidence and skills in applying participatory and adaptive inclusion and safeguarding approaches.
- Experience building and sustaining productive and trusted relationships with partners and counterparts through stakeholder engagement, program delivery, or project implementation activities.
- Experience supporting the coordination of training, workshops, or capacity building activities.
- Experience supporting partner engagement, program delivery, or project implementation activities.
- Demonstrated cultural awareness and ability to work effectively in Solomon Islands context with oral communication skills in Pijin.
- Understanding of and commitment to Social Inclusion, Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.

### **Desirable**

- Ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and maintain confidentiality
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and document management

jobs.title: Maintenance Assistant (Plumbing)
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I) collective** delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The role – **Maintenance Assistant (Plumbing)** willsupport the Maintenance Supervisor in delivering safe, compliant, and high‑quality maintenance services across SPC facilities. The role provides specialised plumbing expertise, including repairs, installations, troubleshooting, and preventative maintenance. The Maintenance Assistant (Plumbing) will also contribute to general building maintenance, minor carpentry works, and refurbishment tasks to ensure SPC properties remain functional, safe, and well‑maintained.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Facility Maintenance**

- Carry out plumbing repairs, installations, and preventative maintenance in accordance with building codes and OHS requirements.
- Respond to plumbing‑related faults (leaks, blockages, fixtures, drainage issues) in a timely manner.
- Assist the Team to carry out routine and general maintenance of the SPC properties in accordance with the Maintenance work plan.

**Office Space Refurbishment and Special Projects**

- Assist the Team to carry out office space refurbishment and special maintenance projects to ensure timely completion of projects.
- Assist in moving, carrying out fitting and removal of furniture or any additional requests as required.
- Assist in the arrangement of storage for items etc. as required.

**Increased Activity to Support Programmes/Divisions**

- Support of maintenance necessary work within Programme/ Divisions and in cases of additional activities.

**Assist During Official Functions and Meetings**

- Assist in set up, preparation, set down and any other Maintenance required tasks during functions and meetings, including logistics.
- Assist in staff requests to Maintenance.
- Assist in other duties as and when required.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Relevant TVET qualification in Plumbing and Sheetmetal trade.

**Technical expertise**

- 4-5 years practical plumbing experience in building maintenance or construction.
- Strong knowledge of plumbing systems, fixtures, drainage, pipework, and water supply troubleshooting.
- Ability to interpret plumbing schematics and building plans.
- Experience in minor carpentry works is an advantage.
- Basic knowledge of construction plans and architectural drawings.
- Control of the use and all techniques used for maintenance of the various structures.
- Good knowledge of the different building bodies.
- Good organizational skills.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration –** the **Maintenance Assistant (Plumbing)** is band 4 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a commencing taxable salary range of FJD 1,323-1,654 per month, plus local staff benefits. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration being given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised locally (EPAL) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides medical and life insurance for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

jobs.title: Expression of Interest – Inclusion Adviser, Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program
jobs.description:
**About DT Global**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**Program Context**

The Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program is a DFAT funded program that is part of the Pacific Australia Skills work in Solomon Islands. Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across Timor-Leste and the Pacific. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of prior Australian Government support for skills and training in Timor-Leste. The SIRIS program will focus on support for rural training centres (RTCs) and other training providers to strengthen their institutional capability, improve the quality and relevance of skills delivery, and respond effectively to labour-market needs. Effective delivery of the activity will require coordinated planning across program, operational and technical functions, with resources aligned to agreed activities and results.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Country Director in close collaboration with the SIRIS Activity Lead, the SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser will provide technical leadership and advice to strengthen Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) outcomes across the Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program. The SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser will also work closely with the Regional Inclusion Lead position to support inclusion outcomes across the broader work of Pacific Australia Skills in the Solomon Islands.

The role is responsible for operationalising the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy and Implementation Plan in Solomon Islands, ensuring that inclusion is systematically embedded across programme design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning. The SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser will work closely with staff, partners and stakeholders to strengthen inclusive approaches that promote equitable access, participation and outcomes for women, people with disabilities, youth and other underrepresented groups.

To strengthen inclusive practice at the country level, the SIRIS program Inclusion Adviser with the support of the regional Inclusion team, will facilitate professional development, coaching and capacity-building initiatives for Pacific Australia Skills staff, partners and stakeholders. The role will also support the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) and Communications teams to ensure inclusion is integrated into systems, reporting, knowledge products, communications and country planning processes.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

Pacific Australia Skills uses the term Inclusion to describe its work in advancing Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI). The Inclusion and Safeguarding Adviser will:

**Inclusion Leadership and Technical Advice**

- Lead the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy and Inclusion Implementation Plan across Solomon Islands.
- Provide technical advice on Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) throughout programme planning, implementation and review across Solomon Islands.
- Support programme teams and partners in Solomon Islands to identify and address barriers affecting participation and access.
- In line with the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy, promote inclusive programme design and delivery that supports equitable outcomes.
- Advise on practical and sustainable approaches to inclusion within skills development and training initiatives.

**Implementation, Capacity Development and Organisational Learning**

- Lead the implementation of inclusion specific activities outlined in the Solomon Islands Strategy and workplan
- In collaboration with the regional inclusion team, design and facilitate inclusion training, workshops and awareness initiatives for programme staff, partners and stakeholders in Solomon Islands.
- Deliver inclusion orientations for new staff, advisers and consultants in Solomon Islands.
- Provide coaching and mentoring to strengthen inclusion knowledge and practice.
- In collaboration with the regional inclusion team, develop practical inclusion resources, tools and guidance materials.
- Promote learning and sharing of good practices across programme teams.

**Inclusive Program Design and Partnership Support**

- Support partner organisations and stakeholders to strengthen institutional capacity and approaches for inclusion in Solomon Islands.
- Review programme activities and initiatives to ensure inclusive participation, engagement and accessibility.
- Work closely with partners in Solomon Islands to identify opportunities to improve participation of women, people with disabilities, youths and marginalized groups.
- Support integration of inclusion (gender equality, disability and social inclusion) considerations into work planning and activity design.

**Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning**

- Support the MEL team to integrate inclusion indicators within programme monitoring systems.
- Support in analysing participation and outcome data relating to gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion.
- Contribute to inclusion reporting requirements and programme performance reviews.
- Support evidence generation and learning activities to strengthen programme effectiveness.
- Document lessons learned and emerging good practice.
- Contribute to reflection workshops and participate in Pacific Australia Skills inclusion community of practice.

**Communications and Knowledge Sharing**

- Support development of accessible and inclusive communication products.
- Ensure diverse participant experiences are appropriately represented in programme communications.
- Contribute to inclusion success stories, case studies and knowledge products.
- Promote inclusive and accessible approaches to stakeholder engagement and communications.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Sector Strengthening**

- Build strong relationships with government agencies, training institutions, disability organisations, women's organisations and community stakeholders in Solomon Islands.
- Represent Pacific Australia Skills Solomon Islands at relevant inclusion and GEDSI forums.
- Establish and facilitate a Community of Practice focused on GEDSI learning and collaboration.
- Contribute to broader sector discussions that strengthen inclusion within skills development and training systems.
- Support strategic partnerships that advance inclusive development outcomes.
- Contribute to policy dialogue and systems strengthening initiatives relevant to inclusion within the skills and training sector in Solomon Islands.

**Other Duties**

- Contribute to positive working relationships across the SIRIS Programme and Pacific Australia Skills.
- Support organisational learning and continuous improvement.
- Undertake other reasonable tasks consistent with the objectives of the role and duties as required to ensure the smooth and effective delivery of Pacific Australia Skills in Solomon Islands.

## **Selection Criteria**

### **Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- Tertiary qualifications in gender, international development, social sciences, community development or another relevant field.
- Demonstrated experience in a similar role within development programs or donor-funded projects, preferably Australian Government within Solomon Islands.
- Willingness and ability to facilitate rather than direct and to provide support to build staff and partners’ knowledge, confidence and skills in applying participatory and adaptive inclusion and safeguarding approaches.
- Experience building and sustaining productive and trusted relationships with partners and counterparts through stakeholder engagement, program delivery, or project implementation activities.
- Experience supporting the coordination of training, workshops, or capacity building activities.
- Experience supporting partner engagement, program delivery, or project implementation activities.
- Demonstrated cultural awareness and ability to work effectively in Solomon Islands context with oral communication skills in Pijin.
- Understanding of and commitment to Social Inclusion, Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.

### **Desirable**

- Ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and maintain confidentiality
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and document management

jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I) collective** delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The role – **Maintenance Assistant (Mechanical & Electrical)** will provide hands‑on support to the Maintenance Supervisor in the servicing, repair, and upkeep of SPC’s air‑conditioning units, minor electrical fixtures, and general building maintenance. The Maintenance Assistant (Mechanical & Electrical) will ensure all works are carried out safely, efficiently, and in compliance with SPC OHS standards, contributing to a secure, functional, and well‑maintained campus environment.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Air Conditioning Servicing & Support**

- Assist with routine servicing, cleaning, and basic troubleshooting of air‑conditioning units.
- Support the Maintenance Supervisor in diagnosing faults and carrying out minor repairs.
- Assist in installation, relocation, and removal of AC units.

**Minor Electrical Maintenance**

- Assist with minor electrical tasks such as replacing lights, switches, sockets, and basic wiring support.
- Support safe isolation of circuits under supervision.
- Assist contractors during major electrical works.

**General Building Maintenance & Campus Support**

- Assist with general maintenance tasks including carpentry, painting, plumbing support, and minor repairs.
- Support upkeep of tools, machinery, and workshop areas.
- Assist in maintaining campus environment (drains, footpaths, gardens).

**Support for Functions & Divisional Requests**

- Assist with set‑up, logistics, and technical support for official functions and meetings.
- Support programme/divisional maintenance requests.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Relevant TVET qualification in Air‑Conditioning & Refrigeration or Electrical Trades.

**Technical expertise**

- 4-5 years’ experience in AC servicing, minor electrical work, and general maintenance.
- Basic knowledge of AC systems, servicing, and minor repairs.
- Basic electrical troubleshooting skills.
- Ability to read simple technical diagrams.
- Good organisational and time‑management skills.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration –** the **Maintenance Assistant (Mechanical & Electrical)** is band 4 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a commencing taxable salary range of FJD 1,323-1,654 per month, plus local staff benefits. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

jobs.title: Award Management Team Programme Officer, Africa - NL (preferred) or UK
jobs.description:
## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

### **The Awards Management Team**

The Awards Management Team (AMT) works in lockstep with Prosper Global’ country teams to ensure they have the resources, tools, and information they need to succeed in the implementation of high-quality programs across three areas by:

- Stewarding award management from kick-off to close out, supporting adherence to donor requirements, aligning donor contractual deliverables with internal program quality and compliance standards to deliver program impact, resolving compliance issues, and promoting knowledge management;
- Contributing to strategic new business development by identifying new funding opportunities, supporting high-quality program design, and leading submission efforts aligned with donor requirements; and
- Serving as liaison between Prosper Global' program teams and their most critical relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Prosper Global works across 14 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, leading a large and diverse portfolio of programming with a focus on fragile and conflict-affected countries and regions. Across the region, Prosper Global works to address the interrelated and compounding factors that drive vulnerability, including conflict and climate shocks, responding to humanitarian needs while strengthening the systems that contribute to stability, economic growth, inclusive governance and sustainable service delivery. Key areas of focus include resilience, economic opportunity, market systems development, climate adaptation, water security, food security, governance, peacebuilding, youth employment and humanitarian response. The region also presents growing opportunities for private-sector engagement, blended finance, and innovative partnership models, enabling Prosper Global to bridge relief and long-term development needs through climate-smart, evidence-driven and market-oriented programming.

### **The Position**

The Awards Management Team Programme Officer (AMT PO) supports strategic, impactful, high-quality programming within the Awards Management Team structure within Africa. They are responsible for a portfolio of institutional and private donor awards within the region, working closely with country teams and fundraising teams to oversee current awards and support new business opportunities.

### **Essential Responsibilities**

#### **AWARD MANAGEMENT & OVERSIGHT**

- Oversee assigned portfolio of awards to ensure compliance with donor requirements, monitor overall award health, and provide guidance and oversight on award requirements (i.e., narrative reporting, prior approvals)
- Support country teams’ adherence to donor rules and regulations, serving as main point of contact for institutional donor compliance and communication, and supporting Corporate and Foundations Team (CFT) Relationship Managers with private donor communications and stewardship related to award management
- Provide guidance to country teams on narrative reporting; review reports and other award deliverables, ensuring quality and adherence to donor requirements and internal standards. Manage the submission of institutional donor reports and support CFT Relationship Managers in the submission of private donor reports.
- Facilitate internal award agreement and amendment review and negotiation processes
- Prepare and communicate award kick-off and closeout tools, including new award initiation summary
- Provide training and capacity building to country teams on award management, compliance, and donor requirements on an as-needed basis

#### **BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT**

- Review assigned draft proposals for completeness, compliance, alignment with donor requirements, and overall quality; manage or support proposal and concept submissions.
- Support or lead coordination for assigned proposals or concept notes, monitoring timelines, tracking status, and communicating with relevant parties.
- May contribute to proposal writing (narrative, annexes), potentially traveling to country offices if needed.
- Coordinate with other Global and Regional departments (e.g., Finance, Compliance, Technical Support) during proposal development.
- Provide administrative support for proposal development as needed, such as drafting standard annexes (e.g., Past Performance Reports, capacity statements), copy-editing, formatting, obtaining signatures, and final compilation/submission.

#### **DONOR LIAISON AND REPRESENTATION**

- Serve as HQ focal point for donor communications on institutional award management matters, communicating updates, amendments, or key programmatic changes
- Support CFT Relationship Managers in coordinating private donor communications regarding agreement review, award updates, amendments to existing agreements, reporting deliverables and/or key programmatic changes.
- With guidance from the AMT Manager, represent regional/country interests and programs with external stakeholders.
- Participate in representational visits, events, and meetings as requested

#### **ADMINISTRATION AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT**

- Maintain internal knowledge management systems for assigned awards (e.g., GAIT, Digital Library)
- Responsible for record retention of key award documents in accordance with record retention policy

#### **OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Support internal communications, ensuring information flow between country teams, HQ, and other stakeholders.
- Facilitate learning across portfolios and share lessons learned and knowledge of agency resources/tools/best practices.
- Provide dedicated support during emergencies or complex program start-ups as assigned.
- Support regional team on special projects, as assigned.
- All other duties as assigned.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

None

- **Reports Directly To: Awards Management Team Manager, Africa**
- **Works Directly With:** Regional Program teams, Country Directors and in-country Programs and Awards/Grants Management teams, Donor Compliance, International Finance, Institutional Donor Engagement, Philanthropic Growth & Engagement

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field is preferred.
- 3+ years of professional experience in international relief and development, including managing the development, implementation, administration, and compliance of grants (especially government-funded awards). Field-based experience is highly desirable, ideally in Africa
- Experience with proposal development (support and writing) with various donors e.g., US Government, UK Government, European institutions (ECHO and European Commission), other European bilateral donors, private foundations, corporations.
- Experience with monitoring and evaluation and other learning efforts is preferred.
- Experience representing an organization to external stakeholders is preferred.
- Proficiency with MS Office software required (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Fluency in written and spoken English required.
- Proficiency in French is required.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information clearly and concisely for various audiences.
- A detail-oriented, multi-tasker who is able to communicate clearly and work under pressure.
- A problem solver, adept in successfully dealing with issues of complexity.
- Proven ability to build and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with diverse internal teams and external stakeholders across different cultures and time zones.
- Able to harness the expertise, experience and ideas of colleagues and effectively use this to improve their own work and support that of others.
- Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, track deadlines, and ensure timely completion of tasks for self and direct reports.
- A demonstrable passion for, and a clear empathy with, the organization’s aims and values.

### **Success Factors**

The successful AMT Programme Officer will be a proactive, dependable, and service-oriented collaborator who builds trusted relationships across country, regional, and global teams. They will bring sound judgment, attention to detail, and a strong sense of accountability to managing a varied portfolio, anticipating deadlines and emerging risks rather than waiting for issues to escalate. They will be comfortable navigating complexity and ambiguity, asking thoughtful questions, drawing on colleagues’ expertise, and translating donor requirements and internal processes into clear, practical guidance for country teams. Success will also require concise and responsive communication, cultural awareness, adaptability across different donors and operating contexts, and the ability to balance compliance requirements with a pragmatic focus on program delivery and donor stewardship. Over time, the Officer will deepen their knowledge of assigned awards and donor expectations, share learning across the AMT, and contribute to a cohesive team culture grounded in mutual respect, continuous improvement, and high-quality support.

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

This position may require up to 10% travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited. Prosper Global Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short term assignment to a field posting. Staff are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and Prosper Global's policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

### **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

### **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).
