jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Lebanon**

MdM has been working in Lebanon for 30 years and actively contributed to respond to needs of the most vulnerable communities as the context unfolded (2011 Syrian crisis, 2019 severe economic crisis, 2020 Beirut Blast) and the current period since October 7th, 2023 – especially as the war resumed in Lebanon since March 2nd, 2026.

MdM’s intervention in Lebanon aims to strengthen the national health system and increase access to quality healthcare.

MdM is recognized in Lebanon as a major actor in the areas of mental health (MHPSS) and sexual and reproductive health (SRH). MdM supports several health centers and mobile clinics in the South, Beirut Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and Baalbek Hermel; and works with other partners.

Despite the June 2026 ceasefire, the situation remains highly volatile and high needs remain, particularly in the South of the country. MdM continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure an appropriate, timely and flexible intervention, always in line with the needs of the various conflict-affected populations.

## **About the role**

You are responsible for the overall strategy and compliance, through the management of logistics, human resources and finance departments in the MdM Lebanon mission.

You ensure support services are fully compliant with MdM policies, donor requirements, national authorities' regulations, and applicable legislation.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the line management of the General coordinator, and the technical management of the Desk manager, you work in close collaboration with the other departments: Program, Medical/MHPSS, Grants, Security-Safety-Access, MEAL.

## **What you’ll do**

**Support services leadership & strategic planning**

- Provide strategic leadership and guidance to the General Coordinator and Country Management Team on all support-related matters
- Contribute to country strategy development, annual planning and financial planning processes
- Lead support services planning and ensure alignment between operational and programme priorities
- Anticipate operational challenges and oversee contingency planning to ensure humanitarian response continuity

**Development & reporting**

- Ensure support functions contribute effectively to proposal development, reporting and donor-related processes
- Coordinate the timely provision of analyses and support inputs required for programme development and decision-making

**Support services management & quality**

- Oversee the quality, compliance and performance of all support functions in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements and local regulations
- Ensure sound resource management, accountability and legal compliance across the mission
- Monitor support systems, identify risks and corrective actions, and strengthen tools and procedures to support informed decision-making
- Promote effective integration and collaboration between Finance, HR, Logistics and programme teams

**Risk management, compliance & internal control**

- Strengthen internal control systems and ensure appropriate management of mission resources
- Identify and mitigate financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding, fraud and corruption risks
- Lead or coordinate audits, investigations and follow up on recommendations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
- Promote adherence to anti-fraud, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies across the mission

**Team management & capacity building**

- Recruit, manage and develop the support services team through coaching, performance management and capacity-building initiatives
- Foster effective coordination, communication and information sharing across teams
- Identify learning and development needs and ensure access to appropriate technical support and resources

**Coordination & representation**

- Ensure strong coordination between support, programme, field and headquarters teams
- Facilitate effective information sharing and contribute to organizational reporting
- Represent the organization with authorities, partners and donors, alongside the General Coordinator, when required.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Have significant experience in humanitarian operations, including in complex contexts, and have held a senior support coordination role within an international NGO
- Have strong expertise across HR, Finance, Logistics and Administration, ideally supporting health programmes and donor-funded projects
- Are a strategic and analytical leader, able to drive operational performance, manage risks and support decision-making
- Have a proven ability to lead, coach and develop teams while fostering collaboration across departments
- Are organized, adaptable and solution-oriented, with the confidence to make decisions and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Are an excellent communicator and relationship builder, comfortable engaging with partners, authorities, donors and diverse teams
- Are comfortable using Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel
- Are fluent in English; knowledge of French and/or Arabic and experience in the Middle East are strong assets.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer a specialist role rather than overseeing multiple support functions and leading cross-department coordination
- Are uncomfortable working in complex, evolving humanitarian environments where priorities can shift rapidly
- Are not motivated by team leadership, capacity building and stakeholder engagement responsibilities

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info:
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3392€
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Beirut, Lebanon
- Field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Philanthropy Support Team Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Philanthropy Support Team Coordinator!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The Philanthropy Unit of MSF Switzerland is responsible for the acquisition, cultivation and stewardship of around 2,000 major donors — Foundations, Individuals, Corporates, Cantons and Communes — through relationship management and one-to-one donor engagement. The Unit generates a significant share of MSF Switzerland’s annual income, enabling much-needed medical emergency responses.

The three donor-facing teams, comprising 14 Philanthropy Advisors and two interns based in Geneva, Zurich and Lugano, are supported by two teams: experienced, multilingual Writing Officers responsible for producing proposals and reports, and the Enablers team, consisting of two experienced Support Specialists and an intern, covering Due Diligence, Business Intelligence, Prospect Research, Processes and the interface with the CRM Unit. Their work is key to ensuring donor satisfaction, proximity to MSF’s social mission, professionalism and adaptation to changing donor behaviour and market conditions.

The Philantropy support team coordinator is a newly created role in response to the Unit’s growth in investment, income and complexity. The role steers the contribution of the support functions to long-term income growth through effective coordination, clear prioritisation and team management. It provides line management to Writers and Enablers, ensures alignment with the Unit’s needs, manages workloads and facilitates collaboration with donor-facing teams, while anticipating changes in the philanthropy environment.

Writers and Enablers continue to work directly with colleagues across the Unit in their respective areas of expertise, with the role supporting them in bringing this expertise into the Unit’s work.

As a member of the Philanthropy Management Team, the coordinator contributes to Unit-wide planning and decision-making and represents the perspective and needs of the support functions. The role also directly stewards a small portfolio of selected high-value donors.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

**Strategic alignment:**

- Ensures that the priorities and work of Writers and Enablers are aligned with the Unit’s strategies and yearly objectives.
- Supports clear prioritisation when demands exceed available capacity or when priorities conflict.
- Ensures that Writers and Enablers receive regular feedback on their services and products and that relevant learnings are followed up.
- Supports the Unit in making effective use of data and business analysis for planning and decision-making.
- Brings relevant insights from the support functions into Unit-wide discussions.
- Ensures that the Unit’s needs from Operations and Finance are clearly understood and addressed.
- Works with the relevant colleagues to develop solutions and prepares the analysis and arguments needed for the Head of Unit to raise issues requiring senior-level support or decisions.

**Team coordination:**

- Provides people management for the Writers and Enablers, including recruitment, performance management, development and support.
- Enables Writers and Enablers to contribute their expertise directly and effectively, while ensuring clarity on priorities and workload.
- Avoids unnecessary bottlenecks in validation and ensures that Enablers and Writers continue to work directly with relevant colleagues.
- Intervenes when competing requests, workload constraints or unclear responsibilities cannot be resolved directly between colleagues.
- Contributes directly to support work when needed, particularly during periods of high workload, staff absences or specific priority needs.
- Manages the support-function expense budget and coordinates annual planning and reviews for Writers and Enablers.
- Ensures that issues requiring a Unit-wide decision are brought to the Philanthropy Management Team or Head of Unit as appropriate.

**Management of a poll of high-value donors:**

- As a Senior Philanthropy Advisor, the Support Coordinator is accountable for the income from and management of a portfolio of selected high-value donors.
- Develops tailored engagement and growth strategies, including personalised proposals and reports.
- Presents and defends MSF’s case for support to donors.
- Leads negotiations and multi-year funding discussions.
- Ensures high-quality stewardship and long-term partnership development.
- Represents MSF in high-level external engagements.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Advanced university degree in business administration, international relations, social sciences, public policy, economics, or a related field.
- Additional training in fundraising, compliance, data analytics, or leadership is an asset.

*Experience*

- Minimum of 3 years of demonstrated experience leading and developing multidisciplinary teams.
- Minimum of 5 years’ experience in philanthropy in a large organisation with professional philanthropy support in place.
- Experience in philanthropy at MSF is a strong advantage.
- Proven experience managing high-value and complex donor relationships.

*Languages*

- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Working proficiency in either French or German is required.
- Good knowledge of additional Swiss national languages is considered an advantage.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Strong understanding of philanthropy and institutional funding cycles, including prospect management and portfolio structuring.
- Understanding of due diligence frameworks and risk management principles.
- Familiarity with business analytics tools and performance dashboards.
- Strong understanding of financial planning, donor-funded project management, and reporting standards.
- Competencies and a vivid interest in the use of CRM and other tools for philanthropy.
- Competencies in data protection, performance and results management are an advantage.
- Understanding of compliance requirements in philanthropic partnerships.
- Competencies and a vivid interest in the use of CRM and other tools for philanthropy.
- Competencies in data protection, performance and results management are an advantage.
- Understanding of compliance requirements in philanthropic partnerships.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Proven leadership and team management skills, with the ability to lead experienced staff and build diverse, inclusive teams in a participatory way.
- Mature leadership with consistency in decision-making, sound judgement, and high integrity.
- Strategic mindset: forward-looking, systems-oriented, and open to change.
- Ability to translate strategic objectives into clear priorities and adjust workload and resources when needs change.
- Strong communication and influencing skills.
- Donor-centric mindset and service orientation.
- Solution orientation focusing on improvement and practical outcomes.
- Excellent ability to work successfully in a multicultural environment and to demonstrate commitment to and support for diversity.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Geneva
- Ideal start date: beginning of January 2027
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 94’440.- to CHF 111’432.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Finance and Administrative Officer, Kenya
jobs.description:
**Reports to:-** Finance Manager

**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya (With frequent trips to Kakuma Refugee Camps)

**Note: Due to the urgency of the position applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis**

**THE ORGANIZATION**

“Outraged by the injustice faced by people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, we aspire to a world of solidarity and inclusion, enriched by our differences, where everyone can live in dignity”

Handicap International Federation operating name Humanity & Inclusion (HI). HI, Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid and development organisation with no religious or political affiliations operating in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. We work alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable people to help meet their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights. Currently the organization is in 58 countries with over 200 projects globally.

In Kenya, HI works in Nairobi, Nakuru, Turkana, Kisumu, Kilifi, Embu, Kakuma and Dadaab refugee camps to promote inclusive access to healthcare, education and employment opportunities, with a particular focus on youth, women and persons with disabilities. For further information about the association: [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org).

**JOB CONTEXT:**

We are seeking a qualified and experienced Finance and Administrative Officer to join our team. This role is critical in ensuring the continuity of our financial operations and HR administration. The successful candidate will step into a dynamic environment, providing high-quality financial information, ensuring compliance with donor rules, and supporting HR functions at the geographical level.

**YOUR MISSION:**

**1. Strategy & Financial Steering**

- Implement and monitor HI’s financial strategy action plans within your area of responsibility.
- Update financial information, monitor key indicators, and proactively report financial risks to line and functional managers.
- Contribute to the mitigation of identified financial risks.

**2. Standards, Compliance & Expertise**

- Deploy HI's financial policies, processes, and tools; ensure compliance with legal obligations and produce required financial documents.
- Stay informed of changes in financial standards, case law, and sector practices.
- Ensure compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
- Contribute to the programme's operational strategy and assist in drafting new project proposals for continuity and expansion.
- Implement financial document archiving procedures and contribute to internal control and corrective actions.

**3. Operational Implementation – Financial Management**

- Budget Management: Optimize the use of HI's own funds, adhere to the financial calendar, consolidate cash flow needs, and support responses to internal/external auditors.
- Donor Funding: Assist in drafting institutional funding proposals and optimize funding schedules. Inform budget holders of donor financial rules, verify application, monitor expenditure, and prepare donor budget monitoring reports. Anticipate slippage and prepare contractual amendments as needed.

**4. Operational Implementation – HR Administration**

- Contribute to the quality of Programme resources by supporting the recruitment process (sourcing, compliance, and manager assistance).
- Participate in the Programme's HR reporting schedule and meet global HI deadlines.
- Ensure the quality of personnel administration for HI staff in the geographical area.
- Assist managers with the implementation of HI's HR policies and communicate frameworks effectively.
- Support social dialogue, staff representative bodies, and contribute to the management of disputes in conjunction with the HR Manager.

**5. Emergency Preparedness**

- Contribute to the programme's emergency preparedness actions and adapt working modalities during a humanitarian response.

**YOUR PROFILE :**

**A. Educational background and experience**

- University degree in a finance, accounting, or related discipline.
- At least CPA (K) Section 4 certification.
- Minimum of 4 years of practical experience as a Finance Officer, preferably within an NGO or international organization.
- A certificate in Human Resource Management is an added advantage

**B. Knowledge and Skills**

**Skills Required:-**

**Professional Skills**

- Cash-flow management
- Accounts management
- Tax management
- Financial and budget management
- Financial management of institutional funding
- Sourcing and Recruitment
- Personnel administration
- Payroll
- Remuneration and management of the wage bill
- Employment law
- HR IT Tools

**Cross-Sector Skills**

- Frameworks and references
- Office and collaborative tools
- Stress management
- Collaborate in a global organization

**Language skills**

- English and Kiswahili

jobs.title: Venezuela: Líder de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

**¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia?**

**Funciones claves / Responsabilidades**

El/La Líder de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH) será el/la referente técnico nacional de la Cruz Roja Venezolana en materia de agua, saneamiento e higiene, responsable de liderar técnicamente, coordinar y supervisar las intervenciones WASH a nivel nacional, tanto en programas regulares como en situaciones de emergencia. Será responsable de asegurar la calidad técnica, pertinencia, sostenibilidad y aplicación de estándares en las intervenciones; fortalecer las capacidades del personal, voluntariado y filiales; y contribuir al desarrollo y aplicación de lineamientos, herramientas y capacidades institucionales WASH, bajo la orientación de la Coordinación de Salud y en coherencia con el Plan Estratégico 2026–2030.

Será el/la encargado/a de:

- Diseñar, liderar y supervisar la ejecución de proyectos de agua, saneamiento e higiene en comunidades priorizadas, asegurando el cumplimiento de estándares nacionales e internacionales y promoviendo la sostenibilidad de las intervenciones. Las actividades pueden incluir:
- Respuesta a emergencias WASH.
- Rehabilitación, instalación y mantenimiento de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y saneamiento, incluyendo componentes electromecánicos.
- Rehabilitación, instalación y mejora de sistemas energéticos asociados al funcionamiento de infraestructuras WASH, incluyendo soluciones de energía renovable cuando sean técnica, ambiental y económicamente pertinentes.
- Promoción de la higiene y uso eficiente del agua.
- Liderar técnicamente, bajo la orientación de la Coordinación de Salud, la implementación y actualización de los lineamientos, planes y prioridades nacionales de WASH, en coherencia con el Plan Estratégico 2026–2030.
- Desarrollar, actualizar y promover la aplicación de lineamientos, procedimientos, especificaciones técnicas, herramientas y estándares nacionales de WASH para su utilización por la Sede Central y las filiales, asegurando su alineación con la normativa nacional, los estándares del Movimiento Internacional y otros estándares humanitarios aplicables.
- Gestionar y supervisar un equipo multidisciplinario, promoviendo su desarrollo profesional y fortaleciendo sus capacidades técnicas y de liderazgo.
- Liderar técnicamente el diseño, rehabilitación y seguimiento de sistemas comunitarios de agua de pequeña escala, asegurando mecanismos de operación, mantenimiento, sostenibilidad y monitoreo periódico de la calidad del agua.
- Promover la conformación y fortalecimiento de comités comunitarios de agua y saneamiento y mecanismos participativos para la gestión y sostenibilidad de las soluciones implementadas.
- Identificar oportunidades de mejora e innovación en las intervenciones WASH, con base en las experiencias de campo y las mejores prácticas internacionales.
- Establecer y mantener relaciones técnicas con socios del Movimiento, instituciones públicas, donantes y otros actores humanitarios relevantes para WASH, representando técnicamente a la CRV en espacios de coordinación sectorial cuando sea autorizado y contribuyendo a la identificación de oportunidades de cooperación y fortalecimiento del área.
- Brindar asistencia técnica a los equipos de las filiales para la correcta implementación de las intervenciones.
- Participar en estudios técnicos relacionados con la disponibilidad de recursos hídricos y análisis de calidad del agua, y aplicar sus resultados en el diseño de soluciones.
- Contribuir, en coordinación con PMER, al diseño y aplicación de indicadores, herramientas de monitoreo y mecanismos de evaluación de las intervenciones WASH; validar técnicamente la información generada, analizar resultados y tendencias, y proponer medidas correctivas y recomendaciones para mejorar la calidad, impacto y sostenibilidad de las intervenciones.
- Actuar como referente técnico WASH de la CRV durante emergencias y desastres, participando en evaluaciones rápidas de necesidades, definición de prioridades, diseño de intervenciones, estimación de requerimientos, despliegue de capacidades y seguimiento de la respuesta, en coordinación con Salud, Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres y demás áreas involucradas.
- Coordinar y facilitar procesos de capacitación técnica dirigidos a voluntarios y personal involucrado en proyectos WASH.
- Liderar y supervisar la implementación de estrategias de promoción de higiene y cambio de comportamientos, mediante metodologías participativas como PHAST, CHAST, TANDAS u otras metodologías reconocidas y adaptadas al contexto, incluyendo campañas comunitarias, formación de voluntariado y acciones orientadas al uso seguro y eficiente del agua y al saneamiento básico.
- Asegurar que las intervenciones WASH se diseñen e implementen conforme a los Estándares Esfera, los lineamientos técnicos aplicables del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja, la normativa venezolana vigente y los estándares nacionales aplicables en materia de calidad del agua, saneamiento e infraestructura.
- Elaborar y supervisar informes técnicos y de progreso de los proyectos, asegurando la calidad de los reportes y su alineación con los requerimientos de la Dirección de Programas, donantes y organismos reguladores.
- Colaborar con otros sectores de la organización (como salud, gestión de riesgos, protección, entre otros) para asegurar la integración efectiva de las intervenciones.
- Definir las especificaciones y requerimientos técnicos de equipos, insumos y materiales WASH y acompañar técnicamente los procesos de adquisición, recepción, almacenamiento y distribución, en coordinación con las áreas responsables de Compras y Logística, asegurando su idoneidad técnica y uso adecuado.
- Dar seguimiento al presupuesto asignado para las intervenciones, conforme a los procedimientos internos y garantizando la rendición de cuentas.
- Asegurar la aplicación de protocolos de seguridad y bioseguridad durante la ejecución de actividades en terreno.
- Cumplir y hacer cumplir las normativas internas de la CRV en materia de ética, protección, seguridad y estándares humanitarios, así como las leyes nacionales vigentes.
- Ejecutar otras tareas asignadas por su superior inmediato para contribuir al cumplimiento de los objetivos del área y de la organización.

**Reporte**

El/La **Líder de WASH** le reportará a la **coordinación de salud**.

**Lugar de trabajo**

Caracas, con disponibilidad de viajes a nivel nacional.

**Requisitos**

Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:

- Título universitario en ingeniería civil (requerido).
- Especialización o formación en Gestión de Recursos Hídricos, Saneamiento, Agua Potable y/o Higiene Comunitaria (deseable).
- **Mínimo cinco (5) años de experiencia en diseño, ejecución y gestión de proyectos de agua, saneamiento e higiene en comunidades vulnerables, incluyendo al menos dos (2) años en roles de liderazgo.**
- Experiencia comprobada en el diseño, implementación, supervisión y seguimiento de proyectos WASH en comunidades y/o contextos humanitarios, incluyendo sistemas de abastecimiento de agua, saneamiento y promoción de la higiene.
- Experiencia comprobada en evaluación, diseño, rehabilitación, operación y/o mantenimiento de infraestructura y sistemas WASH, incluyendo sistemas de abastecimiento, almacenamiento, distribución y tratamiento de agua.
- Experiencia en WASH en contextos de emergencia o desastre, incluyendo evaluación de necesidades, definición de prioridades y diseño o implementación de intervenciones de respuesta.
- Conocimiento de los Estándares Esfera y otros estándares técnicos y humanitarios aplicables a WASH, así como de la normativa venezolana relacionada con agua potable, saneamiento y calidad del agua.
- Conocimiento y/o experiencia en metodologías participativas de promoción de higiene y saneamiento, tales como PHAST, CHAST, TANDAS u otras metodologías aplicables.
- Experiencia en capacitación y fortalecimiento de capacidades de personal, voluntariado y/o comunidades en materia de agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Experiencia en manejo de presupuestos, planificación y monitoreo de proyectos humanitarios.
- Manejo de software técnico como AutoCAD, EPANET u otras herramientas de diseño, modelación o análisis aplicables a sistemas WASH es deseable.
- Habilidades avanzadas en liderazgo, gestión de equipos y resolución de conflictos.
- Fuertes habilidades analíticas y de resolución de problemas en contextos humanitarios.
- Excelente capacidad de redacción de informes técnicos y propuestas de proyectos.
- Habilidad para la negociación y coordinación con actores institucionales y comunitarios.
- Dominio del español. Conocimiento de inglés a nivel intermedio o superior es deseable.

jobs.title: Unlocking Opportunities Project Officer, Turkana Hub
jobs.description:
**Reports to:-** Project Manager

**Location:** Lodwar, Kenya

**THE ORGANIZATION**

“Outraged by the injustice faced by people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, we aspire to a world of solidarity and inclusion, enriched by our differences, where everyone can live in dignity”

Handicap International Federation operating name Humanity & Inclusion (HI). HI, Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid and development organisation with no religious or political affiliations operating in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. We work alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable people to help meet their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights. Currently, the organization is in 58 countries with over 200 projects globally.

In Kenya, HI works in Nairobi, Nakuru, Turkana, Kisumu, Kilifi, Embu, Kakuma and Dadaab refugee camps to promote inclusive access to healthcare, education and employment opportunities, with a particular focus on youth, women and persons with disabilities. For further information about the association: [www.hi.org](http://www.hi.org).

**JOB CONTEXT:**

The Unlocking Opportunities project is a three-year project that aims to advance inclusive economic empowerment for youth with disabilities, with a strong focus on young women. Through a twin-track approach personalized support and systemic inclusion the program equips youth with skills, resources, and opportunities to engage meaningfully in the economy as entrepreneurs and employees. It further promotes innovation in areas such as assistive technology and digital accessibility, while working with both public and private sector actors to mainstream disability inclusion across key sectors including agriculture, digital economy, and the creative industry.

The Project Officer reports to the Project Manager and plays a frontline role in the direct implementation of the Unlocking Opportunity Project with participants. They will be responsible for supporting the coherence between project strategy and day-to-day execution at field level, ensuring that planned activities are implemented effectively, inclusively, and in line with approved workplans. The Project Officer contributes to the quality and impact of the project by coordinating activities within assigned hubs, supporting partner organizations during implementation, and applying agreed monitoring and control mechanisms. She/He supports the coordination of project activities with partner organizations, contributing to joint planning, routine progress tracking, data collection, and compliance with HI and donor requirements.

The Project Officer plays a key role in maintaining strong working relationships with partners and stakeholders at local level, following up on activity implementation, timelines, and deliverables. The role includes day-to-day supervision of activities within assigned locations, supporting field teams and partner staff, consolidating activity-level reports and data for submission to the Project Manager, identifying and escalating risks or implementation challenges, and promoting collaboration and learning across hubs. The Project Officer represents the project at operational-level meetings and forums as delegated, and ensures that project activities effectively reach young people with disabilities, particularly girls and women, in line with the project’s objectives.

**YOUR MISSION:**

**Mission 1: Operational Implementation**

**Responsibility 1: Contribute to project planning and implementation in line with the existing frameworks**

- Contributing to planning and preparing activities, tools and the associated resources, and implement the action plan in conjunction with the support services and the technical unit.
- Ensuring that activities are implemented and that resources are correctly allocated as authorized by Project Manager
- Ensuring regular reporting of activities, and contribute to the internal and external reporting as requested by the Project Manager.
- Contributing to identifying areas of the project in which adjustments are required and put forward adaptations to the Project Manager.

**Responsibility 2: Contribute to project monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning**

- Contributing to project monitoring, specifically activity progress indicators and the expected outcomes.
- Contributing to project evaluations at the request of the project manager, and ensure that project evaluation recommendations are followed.
- Contributing to project learning

**Responsibility 3: Ensure project data management**

- Ensuring that the appropriate data collection and management tools are in place and are used correctly on the project, in line with global standards.
- Collecting and compiling project-related data in the relevant database.

**Responsibility 4: Contribute to the coordination of project teams**

- As authorized by the Project Manager, facilitate coordination meetings between the project teams and the support services located in the area when necessary.

**Responsibility 5: Contribute to external project communication**

- Contribute to HI’s external influence by taking part in networks, when required.

**Mission 2: Emergency Preparedness and Response**

- Contribute to the programme’s emergency preparedness initiatives, and in an emergency situation, adapt his/her working arrangements in order to contribute to an effective humanitarian response.

**YOUR PROFILE :**

**A. Educational background and experience**

- Bachelor's degree in a Social Science, Community Development, Sociology or any related discipline or a Diploma with at least 5 years working experience.
- Knowledge and practical skills on project management cycle, economic development, business development, services will be an added advantage
- At least 4 years’ experience working in community development with a background in livelihood/economic development in a humanitarian context.
- Experience working with persons with disabilities is an added advantage
- Experience in Government stakeholder engagement
- TOT certificate will be an added advantage.

**B. Specific Frameworks**

- Knowledge on UNCRPD Article 27 (Work and employment promote opportunities for self-employment, entrepreneurship, the development of cooperatives and starting one’s own business)
- Sustainable development goals, SDG 8 (Decent work and economic growth).

**C. Computer Skills**

- Solid knowledge of MS Office suite.

**D. Language skills**

- English and Kiswahili

jobs.title: Chargé·e de Projet Marketing Relationnel
jobs.description:
## **Rejoignez MSF OCG en tant que Chargé·e de Projet Marketing Relationnel!**

**Nous cherchons des personnes passionnées et prêtes à contribuer à notre mission humanitaire.**

**Découvrez ci-dessous les détails du poste et les qualifications que nous recherchons.**

## **Inclusivité et Diversité chez MSF**

Vos qualifications et votre expérience ne correspondent pas exactement à toutes les exigences ?

À MSF OCG, nous nous engageons à promouvoir une culture inclusive qui soutient et amplifie les voix diverses de nos collaborateurs. Nous nous efforçons de créer des environnements de travail où des équipes de personnes aux parcours, caractéristiques, perspectives, idées et expériences variés collaborent pour faire avancer la mission sociale de MSF et améliorer les résultats pour nos patients et les communautés avec lesquelles nous travaillons.

Nous comprenons que certaines personnes peuvent hésiter à postuler si elles ne répondent pas à toutes les exigences du poste. Les recherches montrent que cela est particulièrement vrai pour les femmes. Si vous pensez que votre profil correspond bien à ce poste, nous vous invitons à postuler, même si vous ne remplissez pas toutes les qualifications listées.

Nous encourageons les candidatures de personnes de tous genres, âges, orientations sexuelles, ethnies, origines, religions, croyances, situations de handicap et toutes autres caractéristiques de diversité.

MSF ne tolère aucune exploitation ou abus sexuels, aucune forme de discrimination ou de harcèlement, y compris le harcèlement sexuel. Tous les candidats sélectionnés feront l’objet de vérifications de références.

## **Contexte & Mission**

Médecins Sans Frontières est une organisation médicale et humanitaire internationale indépendante qui fournit des soins aux personnes dans le besoin, aux populations touchées par des catastrophes naturelles ou d’origine humaine, ainsi qu’aux victimes de conflits armés, sans discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, les convictions ou l’appartenance politique (Charte de MSF).

Le mouvement MSF s’articule autour de cinq centres opérationnels, soutenus par 24 sections et bureaux à travers le monde. Le Centre opérationnel de Genève (MSF OCG) est l’un de ces centres.

Au sein du département Communication et Recherche de Fonds de Médecins Sans Frontières Suisse, le/la Chargé·e de projets marketing relationnel rejoint l’équipe Marketing de la cellule Recherche de fonds grand public. Composée d’une Manager, de trois Chargé·es de projets marketing relationnel, de deux Digital Fundraisers et d’un·e Chargé·e de fabrication marketing direct, cette équipe est dédiée au développement des ressources issues des donateurs privés à travers des campagnes de marketing relationnel.

Sous la supervision de la Manager Marketing, le/la Chargé·e de projets marketing relationnel est responsable de deux axes stratégiques : les Middle Donors, à travers la fidélisation et l’augmentation des contributions des donateurs à potentiel élevé via des campagnes multicanales personnalisées, et les Legs et Héritages, à travers l’acquisition, la conversion et la fidélisation des testateurs potentiels et confirmés.

Dans ce cadre, il/elle conçoit et déploie des parcours donateurs et des campagnes multicanales (print, digital, TV et événementiel), garantit la cohérence des communications auprès des publics cibles et assure un suivi rigoureux des résultats, des budgets et des performances.

Les missions pourront évoluer en fonction des priorités stratégiques et des besoins de l’organisation.

## **Principales responsabilités**

- Élaborer et mettre en œuvre les stratégies multicanales annuelles des programmes Middle Donors et Legs et Héritages, en cohérence avec les autres activités de fundraising.
- Définir les objectifs, les plans d’action, les indicateurs de performance et les budgets associés à chaque programme.
- Concevoir les parcours donateurs et coordonner les campagnes de fidélisation des Middle Donors, sur les canaux print et digital.
- Piloter les campagnes d’acquisition, de conversion et de fidélisation des testateurs potentiels et confirmés.
- Développer les supports de communication du programme Legs et Héritages et superviser les actions de génération de leads (TV, radio, télémarketing et digital).
- Contribuer à l’organisation d’événements de sensibilisation aux legs, afin de favoriser les contacts entre les publics cibles et l’équipe Legs administratifs.
- Coordonner la création des contenus, la rédaction des textes, la production des supports, les traductions et les validations internes.
- Assurer la coordination avec les prestataires externes, notamment pour les appels d’offres et les demandes de devis médias.
- Collaborer avec les équipes Digital Fundraising et Data Analyse pour analyser les profils des Middle Donors et des testateurs potentiels, segmenter les publics et développer des parcours personnalisés et automatisés dans le CRM.
- Garantir la cohérence des communications et des points de contact entre les différents canaux, en complémentarité avec les campagnes imprimées.
- Assurer le suivi des budgets, analyser la performance et la rentabilité des campagnes, documenter les résultats et formuler des recommandations d’amélioration.
- Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Middle Donors, Legs administratifs, Donor Care, Business Intelligence et Communication pour assurer l’alignement des campagnes et des relations donateurs.
- Assurer une veille sur les tendances et les bonnes pratiques du fundraising, réaliser des benchmarks et proposer et tester des approches innovantes.
- Participer aux échanges de la communauté internationale de fundraising de MSF et effectuer des visites auprès des prestataires.
- Contribuer à la stratégie et au budget annuel de l’équipe Marketing, participer aux projets transversaux et soutenir les autres activités de fundraising selon les besoins.

## **Profil recherché**

*Éducation*

- Diplôme en communication, marketing, gestion des ONG, droit ou dans un domaine connexe.

*Expérience*

- Une expérience préalable en collecte de fonds, dans le domaine des legs et héritages ou dans la relation donateurs est souhaitable.
- Expérience confirmée dans l'élaboration et l'exécution de campagnes de recherche de fonds.
- Une expérience en gestion de projets et en coordination d’équipes transversales constitue un atout.

*Compétences Techniques*

- Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale.
- Bonne connaissance des outils CRM et des stratégies de collecte de fonds print et digitales.
- Familiarité avec la cartographie des parcours prospects et donateurs, la segmentation des publics et les techniques d’optimisation de la conversion.
- Solides capacités d’analyse et d’interprétation de données complexes pour orienter les décisions et optimiser les performances des campagnes.
- Connaissance des tendances actuelles et des meilleures pratiques en matière de marketing des legs et de collecte de fonds.

*Langues*

- Français et anglais indispensables.
- La connaissance de l’allemand constitue un atout.

*Qualités personnelles*

- Excellentes capacités d’organisation, de gestion simultanée de plusieurs projets et de respect des délais.
- Esprit de collaboration et capacité à travailler en équipe et à coordonner des interlocuteurs de différents services.
- Aisance relationnelle et capacité à convaincre et sensibiliser des publics variés.
- Proactivité, motivation, orientation vers les résultats et volonté d’apprentissage continu.
- Adaptabilité et capacité à résoudre des problèmes dans un environnement en constante évolution.
- Engagement envers les principes d’action humanitaire et d’éthique médicale de MSF.

## **Conditions de travail**

- Poste à temps partiel 90% (36h par semaine)
- Contrat à durée indéterminée
- Lieu de travail : Genève
- Date de début idéale : début décembre
- Salaire annuel brut (à 90%) : de CHF 78'634.80.- à CHF 93'117.60 (salaire en fonction de l'expérience équivalente et de la grille salariale interne).
- Vacances payées : 25 jours par an, pro rata temporis, plus les jours fériés suisses tombant pendant la durée du contrat.
- Caisse de pension : contribution à la caisse de pension (2e pilier-LPP) couverte à raison de 3/4 par MSF et 1/4 par l’employé.
- Une aide à la réinstallation est proposée aux candidats éligibles.

jobs.title: Request For Proposals To Conduct An End-Term Evaluation for the Urban Community Resilience Building Project (UCRB) in Nairobi and Mombasa Countie
jobs.description:
**Request For Proposals**

**To Conduct**

**An End-Term Evaluation for the**

**Urban Community Resilience Building Project (UCRB) in Nairobi and Mombasa Counties.**

**Document Release Date: 3rd November 2026**

**Last Date for Receipt of Proposals: 24th November 2026**

**Time: 1700HRS**

**Tender Number: PRF33262**

**Submission Method:** email to **tenders@redcross.or.ke**

**Tender Opening Venue and Time:** **Virtually via Microsoft Teams at 1200HRS on 25th November**

**Summary of the End-Term Evaluation**

**Purpose**:

The primary purpose is to conduct the end-term evaluation for **Urban Community Resilience Building Project (UCRB) in Nairobi and Mombasa Counties**. The end-term evaluation seeks to provide relevant data and analysis against the Project indicators, project outcome level and theory of change achievements, determine what was working or not working well in the program, understand the impact of the project interventions and document lessons to inform future programming.

**Partners**

Danish Red Cross, Kenya Red Cross Society and County Government of Nairobi and Mombasa

**Duration**

30days

**Estimated Dates**

1st December to 31st December 2026

**Geographical Location**

Nairobi County-Mathare and Mukuru

Mombasa County-Tudor and Miritini

**Target Population**

Targeted community members, stakeholders (County Government Representatives & Partners), Project Staff and Volunteers.

**Deliverables**

Inception report and tools, Draft and final report including all data sets, 3 new case studies, dissemination of the report.

**Methodology**

Quantitative and Qualitative methods.

**Evaluation Management Team**

KRCS MEA&L team, KRCS Project representatives and Danish Red Cross Representatives.

**Background Information**

The Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), with support from the Danish Red Cross Society (DRC) and funding from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA), has been implementing the Urban Community Resilience Building Project (UCRBP) over the five-year period (2022–2026). The project has been seeking to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable urban communities to multi-hazard risks through community-led disaster preparedness, early warning and early action, public health surveillance, and advocacy for sustainable risk reduction.

Through established community structures, including Community Disaster Management Committees (CDMCs), Community-Based Disaster Response Teams (CBDRTs) and Red Cross Action Teams (RCATs), the project has been supporting communities to strengthen their capacities to anticipate, prepare for and respond to emergencies in informal settlements. The importance of these structures was demonstrated during the October–December 2023 El Niño rains, when communities initiated evacuations before Red Cross Action Teams and other response agencies arrived, helping to save lives and minimize the impact of flooding. Community-led hazard management and disease surveillance have further demonstrated the value of locally driven preparedness and response mechanisms in addressing urban risks.

Building on four years of implementation and lessons from community engagement and urban resilience assessments, the 2026 phase is focusing on consolidating these gains and addressing gaps that could undermine the sustainability of previous investments. Key priorities include strengthening the independent functionality of community structures, enhancing their capacity to mobilize resources, and reinforcing linkages with government institutions, private sector actors, NGOs and other potential financing partners. The project is supporting community structures to access resources, introducing community scorecards to monitor progress against community workplans, and advocating for climate-resilient infrastructure and increased government investment in disaster risk reduction.

The project is also strengthening multi-hazard preparedness and response systems, particularly in water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), public health emergencies and epidemic surveillance. Lessons from cholera and other emerging infectious disease outbreaks continue to highlight the importance of community risk awareness, early detection, timely reporting and coordinated response. In addition, the project is promoting youth resilience through the scaling up of Youth Mentorship and Resilience (YMR) models, healthy lifestyle promotion and access to mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). These interventions are complemented by strengthened protection, prevention of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), and accountability mechanisms to ensure inclusive, responsive and community-centred programming.

The current phase is also concentrating on sustainability-oriented support in selected informal settlements in Nairobi and Mombasa counties. In Nairobi, the project is targeting Mathare and Mukuru. These areas face interconnected risks, including fires, flooding, insecurity, disease outbreaks, poor hygiene and sanitation, and gender-based violence. The project is building on previous investments under UCRBP, YLEP and CISU, as well as established relationships with local administration, community leadership and locally led organizations, including Mathare Emergency Community Response Network (MCERN), Grassroot Six Organization (GRO6) and Africa Fire Mission (AFM), to strengthen collaboration and sustainability.

In Mombasa, the project is focusing on Miritini in Jomvu and Tudor in Mvita, where communities continue to experience social and protection-related vulnerabilities, including SGBV, teenage pregnancies, crime and violence, particularly affecting young people. The project is building on existing community structures, including CDMCs, RCATs and community volunteers, as well as previous and ongoing KRCS interventions such as UCRBP, the Cholera and Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (MNCH) interventions in Jomvu, YLEP and CISU.

**Project Objectives**

- To contribute to well-functioning multi-hazard preparedness and response systems, linked with the county disaster structures
- To empower young people and households with capacities to cope, recover and advocate for safer, healthier and more resilient communities.
- To strengthen multi-hazard preparedness and response systems, with particular attention to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), public health emergencies and epidemic surveillance
- To document lessons and developed knowledge of products to influence county and national policy on urban resilience.

**Key Project Stakeholders**

The project was implemented in close coordination with the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, Ministry of Planning and Devolution, Ministry of Interior and Coordination of National Government, Nairobi and Mombasa County Government. KRCS is a member of the County Steering Group (CSG) to coordinate preparedness and response activities with other actors at county level.

At the community level, the Programme was implemented by KRCS volunteers’ and the community health volunteers (CHVs) supervised by the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) with links to the health facilities structures, Mathare Emergency Community Response Network (MCERN), Grassroot Six Organization (GRO6), and Africa Fire Mision (AFM), community disaster management committees (CDMC), The Programme staff worked closely the extension officers from the Ministry of Agriculture & Livestock as well as hygiene and sanitation officers. Community members: women, men, boys, and girls, including those with disabilities were also important stakeholders at the community level.

**Evaluation Purpose & Scope**

**Purpose.**

The end-term evaluation seeks to provide relevant data against the project indicators, to understand the impact of the project’s interventions. It will also bring out issues that were affecting the project implementation and things that aided the success of the project as well as looking into the impact of the project.

The specific objectives of the end-term evaluation will be:

- To measure project achievements against log frame indicators and compared to baseline findings.
- To determine the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability and coherence of the project results in consideration of its goal and objectives.
- To understand whether intended or unintended shifts in knowledge, attitudes and social norms around disaster preparedness occurred amongst the target community/population as a result of the project interventions.
- To identify and provide evidence for the project’s impact, sustainability measures in place, good practices, lessons learned and recommendations for scale up or cross programming. To review the proposed indicators within the log-frame and set targets based on the findings that will guide the next phase of the project implementation.

**Key Questions**

The following are the key questions to be addressed during the ETE. The evaluator may however suggest changes/additional questions at the inception stage:

**Measuring against indicators and targets**

What are the endline values for indicators?

Did the project achieve the targets?

Are they meaningfully different from baseline?

**Service access and utilization**

To what extent have target communities accessed and utilized information on prevalent local hazards, weather patterns, early warning messages and associated risks to inform their preparedness and decision-making?

To what extent have communities accessed and utilized strengthened multi-hazard emergency preparedness and response systems, including early warning mechanisms, contingency plans, emergency response structures and services?

To what extent have young men and women accessed and utilized skills, resources, support systems and opportunities to strengthen their capacity to cope with and recover from disaster risks and emergencies?

To what extent have communities and other relevant stakeholders benefited from and utilized improved KRCS capacity to deliver urban disaster risk reduction and emergency response programmes?

In what ways were project interventions inclusive or not inclusive to people with disabilities?

To what extent have target communities accessed and utilized information on prevalent local hazards, weather patterns, early warning messages and associated risks to inform their preparedness and decision-making?

**Effectiveness**

To what extent were the project expected results achieved (objectives, outputs and outcomes)? How does that compare to the target and the baseline findings?

What changes as reported by the community/stakeholders can be attributed to the project (positive, negative, expected and unexpected)

What is the level of resilience amongst the targeted groups?

Have there been any positive or negative unintended outcomes of the work?

**Efficiency**

Were all activities done within the budget? If there were any significant variances (whether early or late, over or under expenditure), what caused them?

How did the efficiency affect the effectiveness of the project?

Was there value for money?

What has been done in an innovative way?

**Sustainability**

What sustainability measures were put in place – institutional/financial/technical?

To what extent have socio-cultural factors affected uptake of project interventions? And what measures have been/should be taken to address the same?

**Relevance**

How satisfied are the community members with the interventions undertaken by the project?

What do the beneficiaries feel is the effect of the project on their lives in the short term and in the long run?

The extent to which the intervention objectives and design respond to communities’ needs, policies, and priorities, and continue to do so if circumstances change.

**Coherence**

How well has the project’s intervention been compatible with other interventions in the County.

Was the intervention aligned with the national development plan and other relevant policies and strategies?

Did the intervention contribute to the overall development goals of the country?

**Impact.**

What positive and negative systemic changes has the intervention brought about?

To what extent can the observed changes be directly attributed to the project?

What unintended positive or negative effects did the intervention produce?

How has the project transformed local systems, policies, or institutional frameworks?

What are the long-term effects of the intervention likely to be?

How many people have benefited from the intervention?

What are the main factors that have contributed to the impact of the intervention?

**Community Engagement and Accountability**

To what extend were the KRCS minimum accountability standards integrated?

To what extent were the local community members actively involved in the designing, planning and implementing the interventions?

How inclusive and equitable were the participation mechanisms for marginalized or vulnerable groups?

Did the intervention effectively leverage and build upon local knowledge, capacities, and existing community structures?

How transparent and accessible were the project's information sharing and grievance/feedback mechanisms?

Has the engagement process fostered a sense of local ownership to sustain the project's benefits over time?

What complaints and feedback mechanism were put in place? What were the common community complaints addressed during the project period?

Do the community members think that the project respected their culture/religion/daily routines/community calendars etc. and how did that affect the project uptake?

**Survey Methodology**

The consulting firm will propose the most suitable study design, sampling methods, sample size, data collection and analysis approaches that is suitable end term evaluation. This should be clearly outlined in the bidding document/proposal and if qualified to oral stage to have further discussion with the evaluation management team. The consulting firm will also propose targeted respondents to interview or data sources that can answer the log frame indicators and provide comparable statistics to document any changes. The methodology should consider triangulation of findings, adequate and representative sample size for the targeted beneficiaries with clear sampling methods. All the log frame indicators should be given operational definition in the bid submission. Data analysis plan should be embedded indicating how the indicators will be analyzed and presented.

The evaluation will use the following literature and any other sources for reference and to inform the evaluation process further:

- Final Baseline and Midterms Survey Report
- Project proposal, theory of change and log frame.
- Existing project reports both narrative and financial by the time of data collection.
- Documents, policies and frameworks by partners, county and national government.

The project outcome and output indicators are shown in the table below: -

**Hierarchy of Objectives**

**Objectively Verifiable Indicators (OVI)**

**Contribute to building long-term resilience for the most vulnerable communities in the urban settlements.**

Outcome 1: Strengthen community capacities to anticipate, prepare, respond, cope and recover from disaster risks in urban settlements in Kenya

1.1: Percentage of targeted Sub County and County contingency plans activated / used to inform preparedness and response actions.

1.2: Percentage increase in the preparedness and response drill scores at community and county levels

1.3: Percentage of targeted stakeholders reporting that project learning and findings have informed their planning and decision-making

Output 1: Target communities' awareness and knowledge on most prevalent local hazards and impact of weather patterns are increased

1.1.1: Number of integrated community-based awareness initiatives on urban risks conducted (integrated health outreaches, risk awareness campaigns, climate change)

1.1.2: Number of risk and hazard maps developed and disseminated to communities

1.1.3: Number of preparedness and response training/drills at community and county level conducted

Output 2: Strengthened Emergency preparedness and response multi hazard approach.

2.1.1: Number of multi hazard contingency plan development/review forums at Sub County and county levels supported

2.1.2: Number of community action plans for humanitarian diplomacy on key threats developed/updated

2.1.3: Number of advocacy and knowledge sharing meetings participated in

Output 3: Improve the capability of young men and women to cope and recover from risks, disasters and emergencies

3.1.1: Number of young men and women mobilized and selected (who are to be "role models"/facilitators of YMR and design community activities)

3.1.1: Number of young men and women trained (who are to be "role models"/facilitators of YMR and design community activities)

3.1.3: Number of young men and women receiving counselling support to cope and recover from risks, disaster and emergencies

Output 4: KRCS has improved capacities to implement urban programmes

4.1.1: Number of innovative challenges held around DRR

4.1.2: Number of forums participated in where learnings and findings to key stakeholders was done

4.1.3: Number of trainings conducted to support roll out of caring for volunteers (incl. PFA and Stress management training, counselling sessions after critical events etc.)

**Quality & Ethical Standards**

The consultant shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that the evaluation is designed and conducted to respect and protect the rights and welfare of the people and communities involved and to ensure that the assessment is technically accurate and reliable, is conducted in a transparent and impartial manner, and contributes to organizational learning and accountability. Therefore, the evaluation team shall be required to adhere to the assessment standards and applicable practices as recommended by International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

- **Utility:** Assessments must be useful and used.
- **Feasibility:** Assessments must be realistic, diplomatic, and managed in a sensible, cost-effective manner.
- **Ethics & Legality:** Assessments must be conducted in an ethical and legal manner, with regard for the welfare of those involved in and affected by the assessment.
- **Impartiality & Independence:** Assessments should be impartial, providing a comprehensive and unbiased assessment that considers the views of all stakeholders.
- **Transparency:** assessment activities should reflect an attitude of openness and transparency.
- **Accuracy:** Assessments should be technically accurate, providing sufficient information about the data collection, analysis, and interpretation methods so that their worth or merit can be determined.
- **Participation:** Stakeholders should be consulted and meaningfully involved in the assessment process when feasible and appropriate.
- **Collaboration:** Collaboration between key operating partners in the assessment process improves the legitimacy and utility of the assessment.
- **Inclusion:** The assessment must include clear steps to ensure meaningful engagement and participation of all sections of the community, including persons with disability.

It is also expected that the assessment will respect the seven Fundamental Principles of the Red Cross and Red Crescent: 1) humanity, 2) impartiality, 3) neutrality, 4) independence, 5) voluntary service, 6) unity and 7) universality.

**Qualifications and Experience for Consultants**

The lead consultant must possess the following qualifications:

1. A minimum of a master’s degree in Climate Adaptation/Disaster Risk Reduction/Social science/ community development or related field.
2. A minimum of 5 years’ extensive experience in carrying out comprehensive evaluations or similar assignments.
3. Good understanding of Climate Change, Disaster Risk Resilience interventions, disability and gender inclusion, and age among vulnerable populations in Kenya.
4. Proven experience in participatory and results-based M&E knowledge and practical experience in quantitative and qualitative research methods.
5. Must have led in at least five participatory assessments. Experience of conducting Baseline, End line, Midterm evaluations monitoring and assessment work in the target or similar communities (preferred)
6. High level of professionalism and an ability to work independently and in high-pressure situations under tight deadlines.
7. Strong interpersonal, facilitation and communication skills
8. The team must have a statistician able to analyze quantitative and qualitative data as well as key technical team members to handle specific components of the project evaluation.
9. Team must have experience in participatory data collection methods and using mobile phone technology for data collection, monitoring and reporting.

WASH Technical Advisor
jobs.description:
**Duty station:** Caracas or La Guaira, with regular travel to project locations

**Contract type:** Consultancy contract (100%)

**Contract duration:** 1.1.2027 – 31.12.2027

**Reporting to:** Project Manager

**Eligibility:** Open to Venezuelan nationals and other applicants who are legally authorised to work in Venezuela and are currently residing in the country (no relocation support)

**Background**

Solidar Suisse is a Swiss non-governmental organisation founded in 1936, formerly known as Swiss Labour Assistance. The organisation is committed to promoting social justice, decent work and equal opportunities and implements humanitarian and development programmes across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe.

Following the earthquake that struck Venezuela in June 2026, Solidar Suisse launched an initial humanitarian response to support affected communities. Building on this first intervention, Solidar Suisse is now preparing a new humanitarian project focusing on WASH and Protection in Caracas and La Guaira.

In line with Solidar Suisse’s commitment to locally led humanitarian action, the project will be implemented in close partnership with two Venezuelan organisations with strong expertise in WASH and Protection respectively. Each partner will lead implementation in its core sector, while contributing complementary expertise to the overall response. Solidar Suisse will retain overall responsibility for the project and provide oversight, coordination and quality assurance through a lean in-country structure.

**Position Purpose**

Solidar Suisse is seeking an experienced and practical WASH Technical Advisor to support the implementation of its humanitarian project in Venezuela.

The position will provide technical guidance and oversight for all WASH-related activities implemented through local partner organisations. The successful candidate will work closely with partners to strengthen programme quality, support implementation, monitor progress, provide technical advice and contribute to effective coordination with relevant stakeholders.

The role requires a hands-on professional who is comfortable working in close collaboration with local organisations and who can support programme implementation through a combination of technical expertise, field engagement, partner accompaniment and practical problem-solving.

**Main Responsibilities**

**Technical Leadership and Quality Assurance**

- Provide technical guidance and oversight for all WASH-related project activities.
- Ensure that WASH interventions are technically sound, context-appropriate and responsive to identified needs.
- Support the design, planning and adaptation of WASH activities throughout project implementation.
- Review technical approaches, tools, methodologies and project documentation and provide recommendations for improvement.
- Ensure alignment with relevant humanitarian standards, sector guidance and recognised good practice.
- Support the integration of accountability, community participation, protection and safeguarding considerations within WASH programming.
- Identify technical challenges and develop practical recommendations together with project partners.

**Partner Support and Accompaniment**

- Work closely with local partner organisations responsible for WASH implementation.
- Provide ongoing technical guidance, mentoring and accompaniment to partner teams.
- Review implementation plans, methodologies, monitoring information and technical reports.
- Support partners in addressing implementation challenges and adapting activities where necessary.
- Identify capacity-strengthening needs and support the development of practical solutions.
- Promote learning, exchange and continuous improvement among project teams.
- Ensure that technical decisions remain aligned with project objectives and community needs.

**Monitoring and Field Support**

- Conduct regular field visits to monitor implementation progress and programme quality.
- Verify the quality and appropriateness of completed and ongoing WASH activities.
- Assess technical risks and implementation challenges and propose corrective actions where required.
- Support the collection and interpretation of monitoring data and technical information.
- Provide technical recommendations for improving effectiveness, quality and sustainability.
- Document lessons learned, challenges and good practices.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Support Solidar Suisse's engagement with relevant WASH stakeholders and coordination mechanisms.
- Participate in relevant WASH-related meetings, technical working groups and consultations.
- Maintain constructive relationships with local authorities, humanitarian actors, civil society organisations and technical counterparts.
- Monitor developments relevant to the WASH sector and provide updates to Solidar Suisse Headquarters.
- Contribute to broader humanitarian coordination efforts where relevant.

**Risk Management, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Identify technical, operational and programme risks related to WASH implementation.
- Support the development and application of appropriate mitigation measures.
- Promote accountability to affected populations and the meaningful participation of communities.
- Ensure that WASH activities are implemented safely, inclusively and in accordance with safeguarding requirements.
- Escalate major concerns or risks through appropriate channels.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Contribute to organisational learning and continuous programme improvement.
- Support humanitarian assessments and response planning when required.
- Undertake other reasonable duties necessary for the successful implementation of Solidar Suisse's humanitarian programme in Venezuela.
- Respond flexibly to changing programme priorities and operational needs.

**Candidate Profile**

- University degree in water engineering, civil engineering, environmental engineering, public health, WASH, environmental sciences or another relevant field.
- At least five years of progressive professional experience in WASH programming within humanitarian and/or development settings.
- Demonstrated technical experience in the design, implementation or monitoring of WASH interventions.
- Experience working with national or local civil society organisations and implementing partners.
- Experience providing technical guidance, mentoring or capacity strengthening to programme teams.
- Good understanding of humanitarian principles, accountability commitments and community-centred programming approaches.
- Familiarity with humanitarian WASH standards and best practices.
- Experience participating in coordination mechanisms and working with multiple stakeholders.
- Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently while maintaining close collaboration with partners and colleagues.
- Willingness and ability to undertake regular field travel.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken.
- Good command of Microsoft Office applications.
- Good knowledge of the Venezuelan humanitarian and institutional context.

Each partner will lead implementation in its core sector, while contributing complementary expertise to the overall response.
