jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

At country level, the UNV Field Unit (FU) and/or designated UNV personnel are responsible for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes in the areas of peace, development and humanitarian assistance.  UNV Field Units/designated UNV personnel represent and position UNV in the respective countries with a focus on the UN Country Team, bringing UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners within a client service approach and collaborating with other stakeholders from government, civil society and private sector. As UNDP represents UNV at country level, UNV personnel are usually hosted within a UNDP Office and are accountable to the Supervisor and UNV Executive Coordinator for compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations

Scope of Work

- Assist in mobilizing volunteers and developing and maintaining partnerships

- Support in the management of key accounts of assigned partnerships.

- Support and maintain relationships with assigned UN partner/s in the country/countries to ensure an understanding of UNV’s mandate, key offers and the added value that UN Volunteer assignments bring in support to the achievement of their respective mandates.

- Support in the identification of volunteer placement opportunities based on UN agency strategies and plans and present UNV value proposition and volunteer modalities with the objective of maximizing the relevance of volunteerism for impact.

- Support in the preparation of descriptions of assignment, with a focus on the assigned partners.

- Support in the development of offers and initiatives that respond to the evolving needs of partners for volunteer solutions.

- Contribute to the organization of advocacy campaigns, key events and other external communication efforts that raise awareness and foster engagement.

- Ensure knowledge is documented, systematized and fed back into volunteer mobilization, using UNV's Client Relationship Management (CRM) to track interactions and updates.

- In consultation with the Online Volunteering (OV) Programme Associate in the respective Regional Office, act as a focal point for online volunteers and accreditation of OV service organizations, focusing on supporting host entities with developing OV opportunities through advocacy engagements and promoting the concept of OV.

2. Contribute to business intelligence in support of strategic and sustained mobilization

- Support partnerships development by collecting and analyzing data of UN Cooperation Frameworks and agency programming frameworks to identify volunteer engagement areas.Record volunteer mobilization opportunities and business intelligence in CRM.

- Support in the engagement with potential partners by preparing presentations, mapping etc. on opportunities for volunteerism for internal use by UNV.

- Support the identification of opportunities for communicating on positive volunteer stories and strengthening visibility of the Agency partnership and the impact of volunteerism.

- Contribute to the development of key messages, talking points, and reports as needed.

3. Contribute to positive volunteer experience

- Provide support during the onboarding process, ensuring volunteers receive timely information, access to necessary resources, and a smooth start to their assignments.

- Provide support to UN Volunteers throughout the volunteer management cycle, ensuring timely assistance and guidance during key life events to foster a smooth, inclusive, and positive volunteer experience.

- Support volunteer engagement by responding to inquiries, sharing updates, and escalating concerns to relevant colleagues to ensure volunteers are supported throughout their service.

- Assist in gathering feedback from volunteers through surveys or informal check-ins and help compile and share insights to inform improvements in volunteer management practices.

- Support the organization of appreciation initiatives and local events to acknowledge volunteer contributions and foster a sense of belonging.

- Support the Country Coordinator in ensuring volunteers’ satisfaction with their assignment.

- Backstop other functions in the Field Unit/at country level during peak periods or personnel absences, ensuring continuity of service and contributing to a seamless and positive volunteer experience.

4. Support duty of care of UN Volunteers serving in the assigned area

- Liaise with the respective entities’ security focal points or heads of office, as applicable, and provide support to ensure a detailed and precise understanding among UN Volunteers on all security-related issues, including e.g. assistance with headcounts in emergency situations.

- Provide timely and accurate support to UN Volunteers undergoing medical evacuation, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV, while maintaining compliance with established procedures.

- Provide tailored support to UN Volunteers who do not speak the UN official language, to facilitate their understanding and providing key information, and navigate their assignment environment effectively throughout the volunteer management cycle.

- Provide host entities with comprehensive information on the enabling instruments available through UNV that support the health and wellbeing of UN Volunteers, such as insurance and related benefits.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the general guidance of the Regional Manager, with day-to-day reporting to the Country Coordinator, the Client Engagement Assistant supports the identification, development, and cultivation of select partnerships with UN Agencies / Host Entities at country level. This includes managing the relationship with priority partners, gathering and sharing data and information that influence mobilization opportunities, ensuring client satisfaction with volunteer services, and bridging the delivery of services from centralized functions of the volunteer management cycle. The critical purpose of this role is the sustained mobilization of volunteers to the designated partners (clients) and support to the duty of care for serving volunteers.

The role involves regular contact and liaison with counterpart UN personnel at all levels, including senior level staff. Within UNV, all personnel are expected to work across multiple units, functions, and teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Core

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests

- Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Event planning and execution

- Ability to plan, manage and execute public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNV's overall brand and mandate

Required Skills and Experience

- Secondary education is required.

- A university degree in Social Sciences or related area will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with high school diploma) or 2 years (with bachelor’s degree) of practical and relevant experience at national or international level in partnership engagement, advocacy, management, client service or related areas.

Required skills:

- Experience in preparing presentation materials, including PowerPoint slides and talking points, as well as minute-taking and report drafting.

- Experience in the use of computers, oﬃce software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities.

The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia for its current Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

(1) Human Development

(2) Nature, Decarbonisation and Resilience

(3) Economic and Digital Transformation

To support programme implementation, UNDP Indonesia requires a Talent and People Development Associate to strengthen workforce planning, employer branding and the employee value proposition (EVP), talent pipelines and onboarding, learning and career management, manager capability and personnel engagement, and strategic partnerships and outreach.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Talent pipelines and onboarding

• Support the development and implementation of talent-sourcing and outreach approaches for priority, specialized and recurring talent needs.

• Conduct talent mapping from relevant labour-market segments, universities, professional associations, networks and candidate communities to support targeted outreach.

• Establish and maintain talent-pipeline databases and trackers, monitor candidate engagement and recruitment-related follow-up, and prepare regular pipeline and outreach updates.

• Coordinate talent outreach activities with hiring units, communications colleagues and external partners, ensuring that activities promote access to diverse and qualified talent pools.

• Coordinate onboarding readiness with relevant HR, hiring-unit, operations and ICT colleagues, including the preparation and monitoring of onboarding plans, induction schedules, welcome information, checklists and manager guidance.

• Monitor completion of onboarding actions, identify delays or service gaps, and follow up with responsible stakeholders to support timely completion.

• Collect and analyses feedback on recruitment, onboarding experiences and exit interview identify recurring issues and propose practical improvements to strengthen consistency, timeliness and the employee experience.

2. Learning and career management support

• Support the identification and consolidation of organizational and individual learning needs, and maintain learning plans, participation records and implementation trackers.

• Coordinate learning activities, career-development events, briefings, mentoring or peer-learning initiatives, including participant communication, materials, logistics, evaluation and follow-up.

• Compile, organize and maintain career-management resources and practical guidance that help personnel reflect on career aspirations, development priorities and possible learning pathways.

• Analyse learning data and participant feedback and prepare reports, lessons learned and practical recommendations to improve the relevance, accessibility and effectiveness of learning and career-management programmes.

• Support the design and coordination of manager-capability initiatives, including practical guidance, briefings and peer-learning activities for managers. Support employee engagement activities, including surveys, focus groups and related action planning, and consolidate the results and recommendations for HR and management.

3. Partnership and outreach

• Build and maintain working relationships with various units in CO and relevant external partners, including universities, professional associations, talent networks, service providers and other UN entities, as applicable.

• Coordinate partnership and outreach activities that expand access to diverse talent, strengthen employer visibility and support learning or career-development opportunities.

• Maintain complete and accessible records of partnership activities, commitments, deliverables, contacts and follow-up actions.

• Support the implementation of UNDP's Employer Value Proposition (EVP) and employer-branding initiatives to strengthen UNDP's positioning as an employer of choice, attract and retain priority talent, and promote an inclusive and positive employment experience.

• Prepare audience-specific EVP and outreach content, campaign materials, briefing notes, presentations and digital communications, and monitor implementation and feedback in collaboration with communication team.

4. Workforce Planning, HR Analytics and Delivery Coordination

• Support workforce planning exercises by collecting, validating and organizing workforce data, staffing needs, skills requirements, vacancy information and planned organizational changes.

• Coordinate integrated workplans, dashboards and action trackers, risks, ensuring that key priorities, milestones and deadlines are regularly monitored and followed up with relevant stakeholders in coordination with HR Associate.

• Analyze HR data, workforce trends and delivery information to identify emerging issues, patterns, risks and areas requiring management attention, and provide practical recommendations to support HR planning and decision-making.

• Prepare accurate reports, presentations, standard operating tools, templates, checklists, guidance notes and knowledge products that support consistent delivery and continuity of work.

• Identify delivery risks, delays, process gaps and quality concerns early, recommend practical corrective action to ensure compliance with prevailing rules.

• Translate HR data and operational information into management insights and recommendations to support workforce planning, talent management and continuous improvement of HR services.

• Perform other duties within the functional profile as required for the efficient functioning of the Office and the assignment.

The Talent and People Development Associate will work under the direct supervision of the HR Analyst and will provide substantive coordination, analytical and implementation support for workforce planning, talent attraction, employee development and engagement initiatives. The incumbent will manage assigned activities and deliverables, coordinate with relevant stakeholders, analyze workforce and talent information, prepare practical tools and recommendations, monitor progress and risks, and ensure complete documentation and timely follow-up. Supporting UNDP's portfolio approach, the incumbent will collaborate with Country Office, project, and UN agency teams, and works across multidisciplinary networks to foster horizontal cooperation and ensure consistent, high-quality HR service delivery.

Tier 0: Funcionários IP do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações permanentes (PA) e por prazo determinado (FTA), cujos contratos serão rescindidos ou não renovados durante 2026

Tier 1: Outros funcionários do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações permanentes (PA) e por prazo determinado (FTA) (definidos como candidatos “internos”)

Tier 2: Funcionários do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações temporárias (TA), pessoal com contratos PSA regulares e Voluntários da ONU Expert e Specialist

Tier 3: Todos os demais tipos de contrato do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV e de outras agências, e outros candidatos externos”

Descrição do Escritório/Unidade/Projeto

O PNUD oferece soluções integradas de programas, políticas e financiamento para alcançar os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). Nesse contexto, o PNUD criou a Rede Global de Políticas (Global Policy Network – GPN), uma rede de especialização técnica, de campo e global, em uma ampla gama de áreas de conhecimento e em apoio às soluções-chave (signature solutions) e às capacidades organizacionais previstas no Plano Estratégico. O Birô de Políticas e Apoio a Programas (BPPS) e o Birô de Crises (CB) são os dois birôs âncora da GPN. Nesse contexto, o Hub de Governança, Estado de Direito e Construção da Paz (GRP), um esforço conjunto com o BPPS, oferece liderança e serviços de assessoria para ampliar o impacto do PNUD em governança e construção da paz, assegurando a integração da governança democrática e dos direitos humanos na resposta e na recuperação em situações de crise.

Os governos locais e regionais já são responsáveis por mais de 65% das metas dos ODS, a maioria delas ligada à prestação de serviços básicos, como água, saneamento, mobilidade, ação climática, saúde ou educação. Cidades e territórios têm um papel central na implementação dos ODS, que estão se tornando um novo instrumento de planejamento estratégico e orçamentação no médio e longo prazo. Desde 2015, os governos locais e suas associações têm atuado de forma cada vez mais ativa na promoção dos ODS, por meio de advocacy e do trabalho com a população local e com parceiros para transpor o espírito da Agenda 2030 para cidades e territórios. Os governos locais também passaram a usar os ODS como marco estratégico para oferecer serviços públicos melhores e mais inovadores, vinculados às metas e aos indicadores dos ODS. No âmbito do projeto SDG Local Action, o PNUD é um dos parceiros implementadores do Mayors Challenge, uma iniciativa global para repensar os serviços mais essenciais que as cidades prestam aos seus moradores.

Nesse contexto, o projeto SDG Local Action busca contratar um(a) Cientista de Dados para apoiar a implementação do projeto Mayors Challenge 2025 no Rio de Janeiro, Brasil. O projeto implementa uma metodologia de política pública orientada por dados para antecipar as necessidades dos cidadãos e oferecer serviços de forma proativa, com potencial de replicação em diferentes públicos-alvo. Sua aplicação inicial se dá por meio da Plataforma Pequenos Cariocas, iniciativa prioritária da Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro voltada à primeira infância. O projeto utiliza o Registro Municipal Integrado (RMI), base de dados consolidada no data lake municipal que integra informações de Saúde, Educação e Assistência Social, possibilitando análises avançadas e uma visão mais integrada dos cidadãos. Com base nessa infraestrutura, o projeto combina modelos analíticos e comunicação proativa, especialmente via WhatsApp, para ampliar o acesso aos serviços e gerar dados que apoiem políticas públicas mais efetivas.

O(A) Cientista de Dados será responsável por liderar iniciativas analíticas e garantir a qualidade e a confiabilidade dos dados que orientam as decisões de políticas públicas, atuando principalmente com o RMI (Registro Municipal Integrado) – data warehouse estratégico que consolida informações de saúde, educação, assistência social e dezenas de outros sistemas municipais – no desenvolvimento de análises, métricas estratégicas e visualizações que apoiem a tomada de decisão baseada em evidências.

Escopo de trabalho

A. Garantir análises exploratórias e estatísticas para apoiar decisões

- Liderar análises exploratórias para identificar padrões, anomalias e oportunidades de melhoria nas bases municipais (saúde, educação e assistência social).

- Criar queries analíticas complexas em SQL (BigQuery) para extrair insights e validar hipóteses.

- Realizar análises estatísticas para apoiar a alocação de recursos e a identificação de vulnerabilidades.

B. Garantir métricas, indicadores e visualizações estratégicas

- Desenvolver e manter métricas estratégicas, KPIs e dashboards que monitorem a efetividade de programas e políticas públicas.

- Criar visualizações e narrativas baseadas em dados para públicos técnicos e executivos.

C. Garantir a qualidade, a confiabilidade e a governança dos dados

- Identificar inconsistências nos dados e propor melhorias sistêmicas.

- Estabelecer e documentar padrões de qualidade de dados, metodologias analíticas e boas práticas para o time.

D. Garantir a articulação com as equipes e os gestores públicos

- Colaborar com as equipes de engenharia de dados, produto e gestores públicos para traduzir requisitos em soluções analíticas robustas.

E. Apoiar a construção e o compartilhamento de conhecimento

- Realizar análises que identifiquem lacunas, oportunidades de integração e necessidades de dados do RMI.

O(A) ocupante da posição desempenha outras atividades compatíveis com seu perfil funcional, conforme necessário para o bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo institucional

Esta posição reporta ao Gerente de Projeto, Rio Mayors Challenge. O(A) ocupante trabalhará em estreita colaboração com a IplanRio, as secretarias municipais relevantes, as equipes técnicas e as contrapartes do PNUD para apoiar a implementação, a coordenação e a elaboração de relatórios do projeto.

Competências

Essenciais (Core)

Alcançar resultados: NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora o próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes, entrega trabalho de qualidade no prazo

Pensar de forma inovadora: NÍVEL 1: Aberto(a) a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, resolve problemas de forma pragmática, promove melhorias

Aprender continuamente: NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar-se com agilidade: NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se a mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Agir com determinação: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra iniciativa e motivação, consegue entregar com calma diante de adversidades, tem confiança

Engajar e construir parcerias: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão em relação aos outros, constrói relações positivas

Promover diversidade e inclusão: NÍVEL 1: Valoriza/respeita as diferenças, tem consciência de vieses inconscientes, enfrenta a discriminação

Competências transversais e técnicas

DATA Data analysis

Capacidade de extrair, analisar e visualizar dados (incluindo dados em tempo real) para gerar insights relevantes e apoiar a tomada de decisão eficaz.

DIGITAL Data governance

Conhecimento de ciência de dados, habilidade para desenvolver ferramentas de gestão de dados, organizar e manter bancos de dados e operar tecnologias de visualização de dados.

DIGITAL Data storytelling and communications

Habilidade para construir uma narrativa em torno de um conjunto de dados e de suas visualizações, de modo a transmitir o significado desses dados de forma poderosa e convincente.

DIGITAL Data strategy and management

Conhecimento para elaborar ou executar uma estratégia de dados ou um marco de gestão de dados.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Working with Evidence and Data

Capacidade de examinar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, embasar conclusões e apoiar a tomada de decisão.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Communication

· Comunicar-se de forma clara, concisa e inequívoca, tanto por escrito quanto oralmente; adaptar as mensagens e escolher os métodos de comunicação conforme o público;

· Capacidade de gerir a comunicação interna e externa, por meio da mídia, das redes sociais e de outros canais apropriados.

Qualificações mínimas do(a) NPSA selecionado(a)

Requisitos mínimos de formação

Diploma universitário de nível avançado (mestrado ou equivalente) em Ciência de Dados, Estatística, Ciência da Computação, Matemática, Economia, Políticas Públicas ou área afim é requisito. Ou

Diploma universitário de primeiro nível (graduação/bacharelado) nas áreas mencionadas acima, combinado com dois anos adicionais de experiência qualificada, será considerado em substituição ao diploma de nível avançado.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante

Candidatos com mestrado (ou equivalente) em uma área de estudo relevante não são obrigados a ter experiência profissional. Candidatos com bacharelado (ou equivalente) são obrigados a ter um mínimo de dois (2) anos de experiência profissional relevante em análise e ciência de dados.

Habilidades desejáveis, além das competências previstas na seção Competências

- Experiência em SQL para queries analíticas complexas, otimização de performance e modelagem de dados (BigQuery).

- Sólida experiência com Python para análise de dados (Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn).

- Experiência em Base estatística forte: análise exploratória de dados (EDA), estatística descritiva e inferencial e testes de hipóteses.

- Experiência comprovada com qualidade de dados, validação, governança e boas práticas de documentação.

- Experiência em ferramentas de visualização e BI (Looker, Metabase, Power BI ou similar) para a criação de dashboards estratégicos.

- Experiência em traduzir perguntas de negócio complexas em análises técnicas e comunicar resultados para diferentes públicos.

- Experiência com versionamento (Git), reprodutibilidade de análises e boas práticas de desenvolvimento analítico.

- Experiência com dbt para transformação, modelagem e documentação de dados.

- Experiência em Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Looker Studio, Cloud Functions).

- Experiência com dados governamentais, políticas públicas ou projetos de impacto social.

- Experiência em ferramentas de qualidade e observabilidade de dados (Great Expectations, dbt tests ou similar).

- Experiência com análise de séries temporais, análise de coorte ou análise geoespacial.

- Experiência com orquestração de pipelines (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster).

- Experiência prévia em definição de padrões, documentação técnica ou mentoria de analistas.

Idioma(s) exigido(s)

Fluência em português é requisito.

Conhecimento funcional de inglês é um diferencial.

Igualdade de oportunidades

Como empregador que oferece igualdade de oportunidades, o UNDP valoriza a diversidade como uma expressão da multiplicidade de nações e culturas onde operamos e, como tal, incentivamos candidatos qualificados de todas as origens a se candidatarem a funções na organização. Nossas decisões de emprego são baseadas no mérito e na adequação à função, sem discriminação.

O UNDP também está comprometido em criar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, onde todo o pessoal seja capacitado a contribuir para nossa missão, seja valorizado, possa prosperar e se beneficiar de oportunidades de carreira abertas a todos.

Assédio sexual, exploração e abuso de autoridade

O UNDP não tolera assédio, assédio sexual, exploração, discriminação e abuso de autoridade. Todos os candidatos selecionados, portanto, passam por verificações relevantes e espera-se que cumpram os respectivos padrões e princípios.

Direito de selecionar múltiplos candidatos

O UNDP reserva-se o direito de selecionar um ou mais candidatos a partir deste anúncio de vaga. Também podemos reter candidaturas e considerar candidatos que se candidatem a este posto para outras posições semelhantes no UNDP, no mesmo nível de classificação e com descrição de funções, experiência e requisitos educacionais semelhantes.

Alerta de fraude

O UNDP não cobra nenhuma taxa em nenhuma etapa do seu processo de recrutamento. Para mais informações, consulte www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Chief, HR Services [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the United Nations’ lead agency for international development. It works with countries and partners to address interconnected development challenges, strengthen institutions and resilience, and advance sustainable development. UNDP operates through a global network of headquarters, regional and country offices, and delivers programmes across development, humanitarian, crisis and post-crisis contexts.

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is one of the key UNDP corporate Bureaus that provides the corporate management architecture, policies, systems, advisory support and operational services that enable UNDP to deliver results with accountability and effective stewardship of resources.

Within BMS, the Office of Human Resources (OHR) is responsible for UNDP’s people management function, with a focus on enabling UNDP to have the right capacity and organizational culture to deliver on its mandate and enable people who work for the organization to perform at their best in the environment of inclusion and respect.

UNDP is currently operating in a period of significant institutional transformation, requiring OHR to strengthen strategic people leadership, modernize HR service delivery and enable the organization to adapt with agility while sustaining performance and accountability. In this context, OHR is seeking a high-caliber leader with a strong HR management background and the capacity, commitment and mindset to foster a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship and transformative results in the role of Chief, HR Services.

Duties and Responsibilities

As a member of OHR’s leadership team, working under the direct supervision of the Director, OHR and in close partnership with the Deputy Director, OHR and Director, BMS/Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC), the Chief, HR Services, provides strategic leadership for the design and delivery of integrated, client-focused HR services to UNDP offices, teams and personnel globally, including policy advice, business partnering, HR (re-)alignment, career transition, people analytics, special people and early-career programmes and insurance services.

The Chief, HR Services fosters innovation across the strategic HR services portfolio by using workforce data, artificial intelligence, automation and other digital solutions responsibly to improve decision quality, user experience, operational efficiency and organizational agility.

The Chief, HR Services champions organizational excellence and professionalism and models inclusive and supportive people leadership and management by fostering accountability, collaboration, innovation and high performance and creating an environment in which personnel can perform, develop and thrive.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks and crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1. Provide Leadership to Strategic Business Partnering

- Provide strategic leadership and technical oversight of HR business partnering, ensuring high-quality advisory support, capacity building and effective backstopping to headquarters units, regional bureaux and country offices.

- Spearhead the redesign and implementation of an integrated HR Business Partnering model to strengthen organizational effectiveness and enable the delivery of UNDP’s strategic priorities.

- Provide HR advice to ensure people decisions are consistent, fair, transparent and compliant with the UN Staff Regulations and Rules, applicable legal frameworks and UNDP policies, while effectively managing institutional and people-related risks.

- Work with the Management Consulting Team and other relevant partners in the design and implementation of Organizational Unit Restructuring Plans (OURP), establishing effective governance, monitoring progress and organizational impact, managing workforce and institutional risks, and ensuring consistent application and alignment with UNDP’s strategic priorities.

- Foster cross-functional collaboration across OHR and maintain strategic engagement with BMS/Office of Legal Services and Global Shared Services Centre to ensure coordinated, consistent and effective delivery of people-management initiatives and services across UNDP.

- Make a strategic contribution to the development of a solid HR policy portfolio, ensuring HR policies are responsive to evolving organizational needs and informed by operational experience, workforce data, legal considerations and consultations with key stakeholders.

- Foster collaboration with the global UNDP HR community to ensure effective capacity building and support.

2. Provide Strategic Leadership for Partner Personnel Service Agreement (PPSA) Services and Other Agency Services

- Provide strategic leadership and executive oversight of the development and delivery of a comprehensive portfolio of OHR services to UNDP business units and external partners; ensure effective service delivery models and financial sustainability.

- Strengthen client relationship management to ensure responsive, high-quality delivery.

- Lead the identification and implementation of technology solutions supporting effective service delivery.

- Oversee the delivery of Partner Personnel Service Agreement services to partner agencies, ensuring effective governance, responsible financial management, appropriate risk controls, service quality, and compliance with UNDP policies and partnership agreements.

- Provide strategic leadership to and effective management of the insurance portfolio.

3. Oversee Career Transition and Separation Services

- Provide strategic oversight of HR programmes supporting career transitions, including terminations, separations and inter-agency mobility, ensuring consistent, timely and people-centered delivery.

- Strengthen strategic partnerships with UN entities and other stakeholders to facilitate seamless inter-agency mobility and coordinated transition support.

- Ensure that career transition services are governed by robust standards and delivered in compliance with applicable legal, regulatory and UNDP policy frameworks, while proactively managing institutional and people-related risks.

4. Provide Strategic Leadership and Oversight of People Analytics

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the people analytics function, ensuring the delivery of timely, high-quality workforce and talent insights that inform executive decision-making, strategic workforce planning and organizational priorities.

- Champion the enterprise-wide use of workforce data, predictive analytics and responsible artificial intelligence to anticipate workforce trends, strengthen evidence-based people strategies and drive organizational performance and continuous improvement.

- Strengthen the governance, quality and accessibility of workforce data and analytics, ensuring appropriate standards, safeguards and capabilities are in place to support reliable and responsible organizational decision-making.

5. Oversee Special People Programmes, e.g. JPOSC and Medical Insurance Services

- Undertake senior-level engagement with UN entities, donor governments, and external partners to strengthen strategic partnerships, mobilize resources, and enhance UNDP's position as an employer of choice.

- Oversee pipeline programmes for early career talent, including Junior Professional Officers, Young Professionals, and Internships/fellowships;

- Exercise oversight and monitoring of the medical insurance portfolio managed by UNDP, including annual meetings, complaint handling, and regular reporting.

- Provide expert advice to senior management and stakeholders on medical insurance-related issues, medevac, and liaise with third-party administrators and providers

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent directly oversees three HR Advisors (P5) and two HR Specialists (P4).

Competencies

Core:

- Achieve Results: ​​LEVEL 4: Prioritize team workflow, mobilize resources, drive scalable results/strategic impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 4: Easily navigate complexity, encourage/enable radical innovation, has foresight

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 4: Create systems and processes that enable learning and development for all

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 4: Proactively initiate/lead organizational change, champion new systems/processes

- Act with Determination: ​​LEVEL 4: Able to make difficult decisions in challenging situations, inspire confidence

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 4: Construct strategic multi-partner alliances in high stake situations, foster co-creation

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 4: Create ethical culture, identify/address barriers to inclusion ​

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical:

- Business Direction and Strategy - Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management Change Management: Initiate, design and ensure successful implementation of organizational change; prepare and support individuals and teams in implementing change Partnership Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

- HR People Strategy & Planning - People Analytics: Ability to generate and align people data with business intelligence data to inform strategic decision-making; knowledge of databases, their architecture, integration and landscape; ability to create and use data models; knowledge of visualization techniques. Gathering and using data and information to provide insights into people issues and guide decision-making Business Partnering: Strategic thinking and development of long-term plans for the organization’s human resources needs while analyzing the current environment and developing strategies to achieve long-term objectives

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or other relevant field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 15 years (with master’s degree) or 17 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in human resources management or related fields at senior levels is required.

- At least five (5) years of experience managing teams in a diverse workplace in private or public international organizations is required.

- Professional certification in human resources management is desired.

- Experience working in the UN system or other international organizations is desired.

- Experience working across headquarters, shared service centres and/or field office environments is desired.

- Experience delivering HR business partnering and/or designing HR business partnering models is an advantage.

- Experience providing authoritative advice on complex, sensitive or high-risk HR matters to senior executives is an advantage.

- Experience leading organizational restructuring, workforce realignment or change-management initiatives is desired.

- Experience interpreting and implementing HR policies and ensuring consistent application across multiple organizational entities is desired.

- Experience leveraging workforce analytics, predictive analytics or business intelligence to support executive decision-making is desired.

- Experience developing and managing services, cost-recovery mechanisms or service delivery funding models is desired.

- Experience establishing and managing strategic partnerships with UN entities, governments, international organizations or other external stakeholders is desired.

- Experience supporting inter-agency mobility, career transition, or workforce transition programmes is desired.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the United Nations’ lead agency for international development. It works with countries and partners to address interconnected development challenges, strengthen institutions and resilience, and advance sustainable development. UNDP operates through a global network of headquarters, regional and country offices and delivers programmes across development, humanitarian, crisis and post-crisis contexts.

Within BMS, the Office of Human Resources (OHR) is responsible for UNDP’s people management function, with a focus on enabling UNDP to have the right capacity and organizational culture to deliver on its mandate and enable people who work for the organization to perform at their best in the environment of inclusion and respect.

In this context, OHR is seeking a high-caliber leader with a strong HR management background and the capacity, commitment and mindset to foster a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship and transformative results in the role of Deputy Director, OHR.

Duties and Responsibilities

As a member of OHR’s leadership team, working under the direct supervision of the Director, OHR and in close partnership with the Chief, HR Services, the Deputy Director, OHR provides substantive leadership for the continued development and implementation of an integrated talent management system that connects strategic workforce planning, organizational and job design, talent acquisition and deployment, succession management, career and leadership development, performance management, workplace experience, organizational culture, health and wellbeing. The Deputy Director fosters innovation across this system by using workforce data, artificial intelligence, automation and other digital solutions responsibly to improve decision quality, user experience, operational efficiency and organizational agility.

The Deputy Director ensures that integrated talent management strategies, policies, capabilities and service delivery arrangements are aligned with UNDP’s strategy and priorities and evolving business, operating and funding models. This includes shaping talent solutions that respond to changing programme and operational requirements, resource trends and the needs of different organizational contexts, while safeguarding fairness, inclusion, accountability and the effective management of institutional risk. The Deputy Director is accountable for strategic coherence and operational excellence across the talent lifecycle and for enabling a high-performing, adaptable and healthy workforce capable of delivering sustainable development results.

The Deputy Director serves as the Director’s principal strategic partner and deputizes for the Director, including representing OHR in senior management and inter-agency and staff-management forums.

The Deputy Director champions organizational excellence and professionalism and models inclusive and supportive people leadership by promoting accountability, collaboration, innovation and high performance and creating an environment in which personnel can perform, develop and thrive.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks and crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to strengthen horizontal collaboration.

1. Provide Strategic Leadership, Portfolio Oversight and Deputy Direction for OHR

- Provide strategic direction and oversight for the teams in the Deputy Director’s portfolio, ensuring integrated, client-focused delivery aligned with UNDP’s People Strategy and organizational priorities.

- Build and sustain strategic partnerships with UN entities, Member States, donors and external institutions, and mobilize resources to advance UNDP’s people priorities, programmes and services.

- Lead the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies across the portfolio to improve decision-making, service quality and operational efficiency.

- Ensure the quality, coherence and consistent delivery of corporate integrated talent management programmes across headquarters, regional and country offices.

- Represent OHR and deputize for the Director as assigned, including supporting the Director and UNDP in negotiations with staff representatives.

- As required, represent UNDP in senior-level HR forums, inter-agency bodies and strategic working groups, shaping system-wide dialogue, policies and practices.

2. Oversee Strategic Workforce Planning and Workforce Architecture

- Shape and lead the corporate workforce planning function, ensuring alignment with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, People Strategy, business and funding models and evolving business priorities.

- Lead the governance and continued evolution of UNDP’s workforce architecture, including job design, ensuring coherent job families, role profiles, position titles, career pathways and job design standards across the organization.

- Provide advice on complex workforce and organizational design matters, including reorganization, workforce optimization, as well as functional and HR alignment processes.

3. Provide Leadership to Talent Acquisition and Deployment

- Provide strategic oversight of UNDP’s talent acquisition and recruitment strategies, ensuring timely, transparent and effective outcomes of related processes.

- Ensure development and continuous improvement of talent acquisition, recruitment and deployment policies, procedures and practices across UNDP, and compliance with these across UNDP.

- Oversee senior-level recruitment and selection processes, ensuring sound governance, institutional rigor and the identification of high-caliber and diverse leadership talent.

- Provide strategic direction for talent deployment and mobility, including the Internal Talent Marketplace.

- Engage relevant stakeholders to anticipate talent needs and continuously improve talent acquisition and deployment strategies, policies and practices.

- Ensure UNDP leverages workforce analytics, digital platforms and innovative sourcing approaches to strengthen talent pipelines.

4. Oversee Succession Management and Talent Development

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the succession management function, ensuring leadership continuity, robust pipelines for critical and senior-level roles, and effective management of succession risks.

- Oversee the design and implementation of people and leadership development strategies that build a skilled, diverse and adaptable workforce aligned with UNDP’s evolving priorities.

- Ensure succession and talent development strategies are integrated with strategic workforce planning, career development, mobility, performance management and other functions in the integrated talent management cycle.

5. Oversee Performance Management, Workplace Experience and Culture

- Provide strategic leadership for UNDP’s organizational culture, ensuring that organizational values, leadership practices, people systems and ways of working reinforce inclusion, collaboration, accountability and high performance.

- Shape UNDP’s performance management, workplace experience and employee engagement approach.

- Lead organizational efforts to promote gender parity, diversity, equity and inclusion and to sustain a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, sexual harassment and abuse of authority, in coordination with relevant policy, ethics, oversight and support functions.

- Ensure that evidence from employee engagement, workplace experience and performance management informs leadership action, workforce planning, talent development, succession management, recognition and the continuous improvement of people policies and programmes.

- Oversee organizational approaches to mental health, psychosocial support, wellbeing and workforce resilience.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent directly oversees five HR Advisors (P5) and one HR Specialist (P4).

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management Change Management: Initiate, design and ensure successful implementation of organizational change; prepare and support individuals and teams in implementing change Partnership Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

- HR People Strategy & Planning - Organizational Design and Development: Knowledge of the organizational design and development theory (i.e. enabling organization's performance through the design of structures, frameworks, systems, policies and metrics, as well as building and developing its culture, capability, values, behaviours, and relationships); understanding of macro trends that impact the design of organizations (e.g. sustainability, geopolitical, demographic, technology); knowledge of organisational design and development diagnostic tools; ability to 'scenario plan' for longer-term organization design and development; ability to manage the development of capability/competency frameworks and maps

jobs.description:
Please note the appropriate Tier indicated in the vacancy title and ensure that you are holding the applicable contract as defined below:

• Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026

• Tier 1: UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed term (FTA) appointments (defined as “internal” candidates)

• Tier 2: UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA) and personnel on regular PSA contracts

• Tier 3: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is the central operations Bureau in UNDP that supports the Organization in the provision of management services. BMS provides policy, oversight, advisory and transactional services, and solutions for UNDP to deliver fully integrated development solutions, including procurement. In line with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, BMS aims to provide effective, sustainable and customer-focused procurement services to clients both internal and external to UNDP. UNDP’s corporate procurement functions lie within the BMS Office of Procurement (OP).

OP is responsible for development of procurement policy, corporate procurement services, procurement advisory services, as well as strategic procurement services to Country Offices and Central Bureaus. In addition, OP provides capacity building to the UNDP global procurement function. OP supports UNDP’s programme delivery in line with UNDP's Strategic Plan 2022-2025 and follows best practices in public sustainable procurement and the rules and regulations of UNDP, the accountability framework, while ensuring appropriate risk management for UNDP. We are a global team based in New York (USA), Copenhagen (Denmark) and in Cyberjaya (Malaysia), with additional Regional Procurement Specialists located in each Bureau Hub (Panama, Addis Ababa, Amman, Istanbul and Bangkok).

The Office of Procurement, through its Governance Team in Copenhagen (OPGT), provides direct procurement services and advisory support to UNDP Country Offices and Programmes globally for the supply of a) Electoral materials and equipment, incl. biometric registration hardware and software, back-end solutions, data centers, etc; b) Civil Registry, Identity digital systems, Digital Transformation solutions; and c) overall technology-intensive solutions and risky/large ICT deliveries.

Scope of Work

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Procurement Team Lead, the Procurement Specialist is responsible for effective delivery of procurement services in order to obtain the best value for money. He/she analyzes and interprets the financial rules and regulations, as well as technical requirements and needs from beneficiaries, and provides solutions to a wide spectrum of complex/urgent/sensitive procurement processes.

The Procurement Specialist promotes a collaborative, client-focused, quality and results-oriented approach in the Unit and works in close collaboration with OP staff for resolving complex procurement-related issues and information exchange.

He/she will also work collaboratively with operations and program staff in UNDP COs and HQ business units.

- Ensures elaboration and implementation of operational strategies focusing on achievement of the following results: Full compliance of procurement activities with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies and strategies. ensures effective internal control, and proper functioning of a client-oriented procurement management system. Provide assessment, elaborate and implement sourcing strategies, especially under situations of urgency and/or high risk outlining corresponding risk mitigation measures, quality management, cost savings, legal considerations, payment conditions and customer relations. Elaboration/review of internal Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) in Procurement, guidance documents, templates and tools. Elaboration and implementation of cost saving and reduction strategies, promote and contribute to sustainable solutions and effective achievement of best value for money principle. Review elaboration and implementation of contract strategy in the Team including tendering processes and evaluation, contractor appraisal, evaluation and negotiation of offers, management of the contract and contractor, legal considerations and payment conditions, quality assurance, performance measurement, customer relationship, risk assessment and management. Participate in periodic meetings of the office and of the Unit in order to provide prompt and timely advice in the planning of resources and activities.

- Monitors and ensures efficient management of procurement processes in Electoral/ID environment and provision of advisory support. Advise and implement OPGT’s procurement methodology and strategy in relation to Electoral and Identity procurement requests. Conduct as relevant assessment of requirements and solutions, markets, constraints, and propose strategy in observance of best practices and UNDP regulations. Provision of technical and analytical support in planning and budgeting, including analysis of options available, implications and cost/risks considerations. Execution and monitoring of electoral/ID procurement processes. Establishment and implementation of proper monitoring system and control of procurement processes including organization of RFQ, ITB or RFP, evaluation of offers, negotiation conditions of contracts in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations. Act where standards or regulations are not met. Implementation of effective internal control and risk management ensuring timely corrective actions and problem shooting during procurement processes and contract implementation. Review the solicitation documents, criteria for evaluation, specifications and evaluation reports, and participate in contractual negotiations for contracts of high value and complexity when required. Promote and supervise compliance with the regulations established by the Contracts, Assets and Procurement Committee (“CAP”) and the Advisory Committee on Procurement (“ACP”). Acts as audit focal point for the Unit and ensure the implementation of recommendations from internal and external audits assuring that corrective measures are placed in practice, when necessary. Harmonize procurement services where relevant in relation to joint procurement with other UN agencies in line with the UN reform. Draft and issue contracts, Terms and Conditions and Schedules and ensure effective management of contracts to secure beneficial contractual arrangements for UNDP. Provide consultation on ad hoc procurement processes to support business units as required.

- Ensures elaboration, introduction and implementation of sourcing strategy and e-procurement tools focusing on achievement of the following results: Development and management of the rosters of suppliers, elaboration of supplier selection and evaluation, quality and performance measurement mechanisms. Support and use of the e-procurement system, and upcoming corporate ERP system.

4. Provides advice and ensures facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the Team focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Organization of training for the team, and CO operations/ projects staff on Procurement.

- Synthesis of lessons learned and best practices in Procurement.

- Participation as required in Business Seminars, Knowledge events related to elections and Identity Management or Technology, contribute to presentations and Team’s visibilit

- Organization of trainings for Govt. staff on Procurement as required

5. Sustainable Procurement: Supports the development and adoption of sustainability related innovative practices (i.e. reduced packaging, transition towards sea freighted consignments, biodegradable packaging, etc.) and develop and apply a methodology to capture impact and effect of these initiatives.

The key results have an impact on the efficiency of the unit. Accurate analysis and presentation of information strengthens the capacity and accountability of the office and facilitates subsequent action by the supervisor. Timely compilation and presentation of data and information allows proactive decision making leading to implementation of most suitable sourcing and procurement strategies and tools.

InstitutionalArrangement

Supervisor: Procurement TeamLead, UNDP OP/Governance Team

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Como agencia líder de las Naciones Unidas en desarrollo, el PNUD trabaja en 170 países y territorios para erradicar la pobreza y reducir la desigualdad. Ayudamos a los países a desarrollar políticas, habilidades de liderazgo, habilidades de asociación, capacidades institucionales y a desarrollar resiliencia para lograr los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS). Nuestro trabajo se concentra en tres áreas de enfoque; desarrollo sostenible, gobernanza democrática y consolidación de la paz, y resiliencia climática y ante desastres.

El mandato global del PNUD es poner fin a la pobreza, construir una gobernanza democrática, un estado de derecho e instituciones inclusivas. Abogamos por el cambio y conectamos a los países con el conocimiento, la experiencia y los recursos para ayudar a las personas a construir una vida mejor.

Sobre la base de ese mandato global, las funciones del PNUD en Venezuela se focalizan en apoyar al país para acelerar el logro de los ODS, contribuyendo a la construcción de una sociedad resiliente, justa y equitativa, con una vida digna, mediante la promoción de un desarrollo económico socialmente inclusivo y sostenible desde el punto de vista ambiental, que contribuya al desarrollo humano integral.

Para ello, el PNUD promueve políticas sociales centradas en la reducción de la pobreza, la optimización de los sistemas de servicios sociales esenciales, la mitigación de los efectos del cambio climático y la adaptación a ellos y la gestión integral del riesgo de desastres, junto con la aplicación de medidas para la conservación de la biodiversidad y la mejora de la gestión ambiental urbana y rural con un enfoque territorial, con el fin de reducir la vulnerabilidad de la población a fenómenos socioeconómicos y socioambientales.

El PNUD en Venezuela es el Receptor Principal (RP) de la subvención aprobada por el Fondo Global de Lucha contra el VIH, la Tuberculosis y la Malaria (FG) para ejecutar la implementación de esta iniciativa, siguiendo los lineamientos establecidos en la propuesta formulada por los Programas Nacionales del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS), en conjunto con la Organización Panamericana de la Salud/ Organización Mundial de la Salud (OPS/OMS), Organizaciones No Gubernamentales (ONG) nacionales e internacionales y demás Organizaciones de la Sociedad Civil.

El PNUD adopta un enfoque de cartera para dar cabida a las cambiantes necesidades de negocio y aprovechar los vínculos entre las intervenciones para lograr sus objetivos estratégicos. Por lo tanto, se espera que el personal del PNUD trabaje a través de unidades, funciones, equipos y proyectos en equipos multidisciplinarios con el fin de mejorar y permitir la colaboración horizontal, y con los lineamientos generales de la subvención aprobada por el Fondo Global de Lucha contra el VIH, la Tuberculosis y la Malaria, para apoyar las acciones en el país, con el acompañamiento permanente del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud.

En línea con la política corporativa en la materia, el objetivo del programa de pasantía es proporcionar a estudiantes y recién licenciados de diversas formaciones académicas una exposición a las cuestiones de desarrollo y una experiencia de primera mano con el entorno de trabajo cotidiano del PNUD, ya sea en persona o a distancia.

Se prevé dos (2) puestos de pasantías, para integrarse al equipo de PSM (Procurement and Supply Management) de la unidad de Salud y Desarrollo del PNUD Venezuela:

- Adquisiciones y Cadena de Suministro , donde el/la pasante trabajará bajo la supervisión directa de la Analista de PSM, e interactuará de forma cotidiana con el Equipo de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo del PNUD Venezuela (Gerencia de la Unidad, finanzas, Programas, Monitoreo y Evaluación).

- Farmacia, donde el/la pasante trabajará bajo la supervisión directa de la Analista de PSM, e interactuará de forma cotidiana con el Equipo de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo del PNUD Venezuela (Gerencia de la Unidad, finanzas, Programas, Monitoreo y Evaluación).

Duties and Responsibilities

Los/as pasantes deberán realizar las siguientes actividades con fines de aprendizaje y fortalecimiento de capacidades, bajo la orientación y supervisión del equipo de PSM de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo:

Adquisiciones y Cadena de Suministro:

- Apoyar la organización y seguimiento administrativo de procesos de adquisiciones, colaborando en la recopilación, registro y archivo de información y documentación relacionada con compras, contrataciones y gestión de proveedores.

- Brindar apoyo en el seguimiento de embarques nacionales e internacionales, procesos de importación, trámites documentales, recepción y distribución de suministros de salud, con fines de aprendizaje sobre los procesos logísticos y de cadena de suministro.

- Colaborar en actividades de monitoreo de inventarios y almacenamiento, participando en la actualización de registros, inventarios físicos y revisión de información relacionada con existencias, vencimientos y movimientos de productos.

- Apoyar la consolidación y organización de datos e información relacionada con adquisiciones, logística e inventarios, contribuyendo a la elaboración de herramientas de seguimiento y análisis bajo supervisión.

- Colaborar en la preparación de informes, presentaciones, bases de datos, minutas y otros documentos de apoyo relacionados con las actividades de la cadena de suministro.

- Participar en reuniones, sesiones de trabajo y actividades de capacitación que contribuyan al fortalecimiento de sus conocimientos en adquisiciones, logística, abastecimiento y gestión de la cadena de suministro.

- Apoyar la redacción, actualización y organización de correspondencia, comunicaciones y documentos informativos de la Unidad.

- Colaborar en la preparación y edición de presentaciones, materiales visuales, informes y otros productos documentales requeridos por la Unidad.

- Brindar apoyo en otras actividades formativas y de apoyo operativo que contribuyan a su desarrollo profesional y al fortalecimiento de las iniciativas de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo.

Farmacia:

- Apoyar la revisión y organización de información técnica y documental relacionada con medicamentos, insumos de salud y actividades de aseguramiento de la calidad, fortaleciendo sus conocimientos sobre normativas y estándares aplicables.

- Colaborar en el seguimiento administrativo y documental de procesos relacionados con adquisiciones, logística, recepción y distribución de productos de salud, con fines de aprendizaje sobre la gestión de la cadena de suministro farmacéutica.

- Participar en actividades de monitoreo de inventarios y almacenamiento, apoyando la actualización de registros y la recopilación de información relacionada con existencias y fechas de vencimiento.

- Apoyar la consolidación y organización de información utilizada en ejercicios de cuantificación, abastecimiento, consumo e indicadores de gestión, contribuyendo a la elaboración de herramientas de seguimiento bajo supervisión.

- Colaborar en la organización de expedientes técnicos, documentación regulatoria, permisos y archivos relacionados con la gestión farmacéutica y los programas de salud.

- Participar en reuniones técnicas, actividades de monitoreo, capacitaciones y otras iniciativas orientadas al fortalecimiento de conocimientos en gestión farmacéutica, calidad y cadena de suministro.

- Apoyar en la elaboración y actualización de reportes, bases de datos, presentaciones, materiales visuales, informes y demás documentos relacionados con los procesos de abastecimiento, inventarios, distribución y otras actividades de apoyo a los programas de salud.

- Apoyar la redacción, actualización y organización de correspondencia, comunicaciones y documentos informativos de la Unidad.

- Brindar apoyo en otras actividades formativas y de apoyo operativo que contribuyan a su desarrollo profesional y al fortalecimiento de las iniciativas de la Unidad de Salud y Desarrollo.

Competencies

Gestión y liderazgo:

• Enfoque de gestión orientado a resultados.

• Condiciones para establecer buenas relaciones interpersonales y transmitir lineamientos institucionales.

• Respeto por la diversidad y género.

• Altos niveles de responsabilidad, ética y transparencia.

• Alta capacidad de aprendizaje e iniciativa, sensibilidad humana, responsabilidad y ética.

• Planificación y organización.

• Habilidad y vocación de servicio para trabajar con poblaciones en heterogeneidad social y situación de vulnerabilidad.

• Responsabilidad y creatividad.

• Iniciativa para la solución de problemas.

Trabajo en equipo y coordinación:

• Capacidad para trabajar en equipo y bajo presión.

• Capacidad y facilidad para adaptarse a ambientes de trabajo multiculturales.

Capacidad Técnica y Gestión de Conocimiento:

Pasante de Adquisiciones y Cadena de Suministro

• Conocimiento básico de adquisiciones, logística, comercio internacional, administración, cadena de suministro o áreas afines.

• Comprensión básica de procesos de abastecimiento, compras, inventarios, almacenamiento y distribución.

• Interés en la gestión de productos de salud, logística humanitaria y fortalecimiento de sistemas de salud.

• Capacidad para recopilar, analizar e interpretar información relacionada con adquisiciones, inventarios, consumos y desempeño logístico, no limitativo.

• Manejo de Microsoft Office, especialmente Excel, Word y PowerPoint.

• Capacidad para trabajar con bases de datos, herramientas de seguimiento y análisis de información, no limitativo.

• Habilidad para elaborar informes, presentaciones y documentos técnicos, no limitativo.
