Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

Moldova is part of the EU’s European Neighborhood Policy (ENP) and in the Eastern Partnership framework, which aims at strengthening individual and regional relationships between the EU and countries in its neighborhood. Moldova is also part of the Energy Community Treaty since 2010 and has signed the Association Agreement with EU in June 2014, including the DCFTA which entered into force in 2016. As a follow-up, Moldova is required to ensure transposition of the EU acquis Communautaire, which underpins the EU energy legislation on electricity, gas, oil, renewables, energy efficiency and environment. The country has synchronized its electricity network with the ENTSO-E to connect to European electricity market.

Considering the ongoing energy crisis, the energy sector is one of the top priorities for the Government and it is addressed in Government’s Plans and a number of policy documents, laws and regulations which outlined the need to undertake more actions towards a green and just energy transition of the Republic of Moldova.

In accordance to the existing strategic planning documents, one of main priorities of the Government is to diversify the energy mix with more renewable energy, which is also fully in line with commitments under the EU Clean Energy for all Europeans package. Achieving this goal will require significant investment in the medium and long term, but also the country’s ability to attract and absorb the funds. The development of renewables, such as wind and solar, will also depend on improving the balancing capabilities of the Moldovan power system and its integration with neighboring countries.

In this regard the EU and Moldova stressed the importance of resilience against any potential efforts by third parties to use energy as a geopolitical level. The EU has urged Moldova to ensure that the energy sector reform demonstrates full respect of the Energy Community acquis and is in line with the EU Third Energy Package. The EU side confirmed its support to the objective of Moldova for integration into the EU energy system and market, an important step being the recent synchronization of its electricity network with the Continental European Network (CEN).

Recognizing the importance of a just and green energy transition in addressing the root causes of the ongoing crisis, the "Accelerating a Just Energy Transition in the Republic of Moldova" portfolio of interventions has emerged - co-designed with the Government and other representatives of the energy system to ensure its relevance and effectiveness.

Through this Portfolio of interventions, the Government of Moldova will be further assisted to tackle the current energy crisis and energy poverty, and addressing prioritized systemic elements in the energy sector to cope with potential future energy crisis.

The Accelerating a Just Energy Transition in Republic of Moldova has the following five key areas of intervention:

- Accelerate Energy Diversification and Efficiency: By supporting the modernization of infrastructure, buildings, and the grid, the Project aims to increase access to renewable energy sources, promote energy efficiency, and encourage investment in renewable energy and innovative technologies.

- Decarbonizing Industries and Economic Sectors: The Project seeks to drive the decarbonization of various economic sectors such as construction, transportation, agriculture, and the private sector. It aims to promote sustainable practices, share green business models, and develop vocational skills for the green energy sector to create equitable employment opportunities and support the transition to a low-carbon economy.

- Foster Sustainable Consumption Patterns: Through comprehensive public awareness campaigns and educational materials, the Project aims to deepen understanding of energy efficiency and renewable energy among community members, business leaders, and government agencies. It strives to promote behaviour change towards sustainable energy practices, particularly among vulnerable populations.

- Strengthen Inclusive Energy Governance: The Project recognizes the importance of inclusive energy governance at both the national and local levels. It aims to strengthen the capacity of relevant institutions and stakeholders to effectively govern and manage the energy sector. By promoting transparency, accountability, and participation, the Project seeks to ensure that decision-making processes related to energy transition are inclusive, empowering all segments of society, including marginalized groups.

- Addressing Energy Vulnerability and Promoting Resilience: One of the Project 's primary focus is to address energy vulnerability and promote resilience among households and businesses. It will provide further support to the Government in improving and implementing compensation mechanisms, including the established an on-bill compensation mechanism targeting the households by level of vulnerability. This intervention aims to provide immediate relief to energy-poor households and the private sector, while also fostering long-term energy resilience and efficiency. The Project places a strong emphasis on meeting the energy needs of vulnerable groups, prioritizing affordability, reliability, and sustainability. To this end, it will explore conceptualisation of decentralized energy solutions, off-grid options, and harness the role of energy access in conflict and disaster recovery efforts, livelihoods, and social inclusion.

Implementation period: 2023-2027.

Duties and Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Project Associate during the assignment will include, but not be limited to, the following:

Assist in efficient delivery of the projects, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Undertake administrative, logistical, travel, procurement, financial and asset management tasks in full compliance with UNDP rules, regulations and policies;

- Provide support to procure goods and services required by the projects, in liaison with the relevant staff and units of UNDP Country Office;

- Provide administrative support in arranging Projects related meetings when needed.

- Participate in the preparation of work plans, operation plans and procurement plans and periodical reviews thereof;

- Provide support in quality control of Projects activities, including assessing impact and effectiveness, tracking outputs and results, and ensure timely and efficient delivery;

- Maintain an appropriate filing system and documenting the implementation to enable further operational and financial closure of the projects;

- Provide support in regular monitoring and data collection of Projects activities in accordance with work plan and procurement plan;

- Provide general secretarial and administrative assistance to the projects in close liaison with UNDP teams, other UN agencies.

Ensure administration and implementation of operational strategies, adapt processes and procedures focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance with respective UNDP and donor rules, regulations, and policies of financial activities, financial recording/reporting system and follow-up on audit recommendations;

- Implementation of effective internal controls, proper functioning of a client-oriented financial resources management system.

- Personal initiative to perform daily work timely, efficiently, and in compliance with established rules and plans;

Provide financial support to the Projects, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Assist Projects team in drafting Project progress reports with financial data;

- Assist projects management in performing budget cycle: planning, preparation, revisions, and budget execution;

- Provide assistance to partner agencies involved in Projects activities, performing and monitoring financial aspects to ensure compliance with budgeted costs in line with established policies and procedures;

- Monitor Projects expenditures, ensuring that no expenditure is incurred before it has been authorized;

- Perform preparatory work for mandatory and general budget revisions, annual physical inventory, auditing; and assist external evaluators in fulfilling their mission;

- Ensure that all Projects financial activities are carried out on schedule and within budget to achieve the project outputs;

- Ensure timely submission of financial reports to the UNDP Country Office to verify the accuracy of such reports for the national partner or donor;

jobs.title: Strategic Learning, Knowledge and Evaluation Specialist, P3, Bangkok, Thailand, UNCDF [Open to Tier 1 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

Duties and Responsibilities

Working under the guidance and supervision of the Head of the Impact Measurement, Verification, and Learning (IMVL) Unit, the Strategic Learning, Knowledge, and Evaluation Specialist leads the design, development, and implementation of UNCDF’s organizational learning and knowledge workstream, as well as coordinating UNCDF’s portfolio of evaluations.

The Strategic Learning, Knowledge, and Evaluation Specialist will drive initiatives that systematically capture, synthesize, and disseminate lessons learned, knowledge, and evaluation findings from across UNCDF’s portfolio, fostering a culture of continuous organizational learning that strengthens the design, delivery and impact of UNCDF’s work.

To support these objectives, the Specialist will lead UNCDF’s portfolio of thematic, programme, and project learning, knowledge, and evaluations activities, ensuring they are strategically designed, developed, and implemented to generate actionable insights that strengthen relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability of UNCDF’s interventions. The Strategic Learning, Knowledge, and Evaluation Specialist will translate these insights into learning loops, knowledge products, strategic recommendations, and innovative tools and approaches.

The Strategic Learning, Knowledge, and Evaluation Specialist will work closely with all UNCDF divisions to implement the organization’s learning and knowledge agenda, while overseeing the evaluation cycle. The Strategic Learning, Knowledge, and Evaluation Specialist will be based in Bangkok, Thailand, and may be required to travel occasionally.

UNCDF adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNCDF personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1.) Design and manage thematic, programme, and project learning, knowledge management, and evaluations in line with UNCDF’s learning and evaluation plan and priorities

• Liaise with all UNCDF divisions in the scoping, design, and execution of UNCDF’s learning and knowledge strategy, internal and external evaluations, and other learning exercises commissioned by UNCDF, including overseeing the work of external evaluation firms and consultants.

• Oversee the management cycle of UNCDF’s learning and knowledge strategy, including evaluations – preparing templates, finalizing Terms of References (TORs), sourcing, vetting and assessing evaluation firms/consultants, supervising inception periods, overseeing country visits of the evaluators, and reviewing draft and final reports.

• Ensure that UNDF’s learning, knowledge management, and evaluation work is aligned with relevant international standards and best practices across International Financial Institutions (IFIs) and Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs), as well as UNDP’s Evaluation Policy and UN Evaluation Group guidance and gender-responsive evaluation standards

• Provide technical guidance and quality assurance throughout the learning, knowledge strategy, and evaluation process, collaborating across the IMVL team and ensuring that objectives, questions, methodology, evidence, and deliverables are credible, useful, and fit for purpose.

2.) Strengthen UNCDF’s organizational framework, standards, and quality assurance for learning, knowledge, and evaluation

• Develop a learning, knowledge, and evaluation plan for UNCDF’s evolving portfolio of development finance instruments, to be used in all relevant organizational learning initiatives supporting UNCDF’s blended finance programming.

• Develop learning, knowledge and evaluation guidance notes, tools, templates, and training materials to support consistent application of learning, knowledge, and evaluation approaches across UNCDF’s development finance instruments and programmes, in line with applicable policies, norms, and standards.

• Participate in UNCDF Programme Appraisal Committee meetings to ensure that new projects/programmes meet relevant learning, knowledge, and evaluability standards.

• Lead, or participate in, as appropriate, internal reviews of UNCDF’s organizational or programmatic performance to identify opportunities for learning, knowledge, innovation, and greater operational impact.

3.) Guide and support knowledge building and management within and outside UNCDF

• Identify and formulate insights, lessons learned, and recommendations to be integrated into UNCDF knowledge management efforts both internally and externally with its key stakeholders,

• Use databases, tracking tools, knowledge management systems, and innovative technologies and approaches to support the use of learning, knowledge, and evaluation findings across UNCDF.

• Contribute to UNCDF’s participation in external learning, knowledge, and evaluation networks and communities of practice, including United Nations Evaluation Group task forces and other forums focused on the learning, knowledge, and evaluation of international development finance instruments.

• Participate in meetings, workshops, and other fora to establish a dialogue on learning, knowledge, and evaluation insights taking into account the information needs of various audiences for evaluation.

4.) Drive the application of organizational learning and knowledge through innovative and user-friendly approaches

• Develop innovative learning and knowledge management approaches, tools, and digital solutions to systematically capture, synthesize, and disseminate project insights and learnings from across UNCDF’s investment and programme portfolio.

• Design and manage feedback mechanisms that integrate strategic insights, lessons learned, and evaluation findings into project design, adaptive management, results monitoring, and strategic decision-making, enabling project teams to continuously strengthen implementation efforts and sharpen impact.

• Leverage AI, knowledge management platforms, and other emerging technologies to enhance learnings by identifying trends across the investment and programme portfolio and supporting insights-driven programme management and innovation.

• Establish and manage partnerships with learning institutions to advance UNCDF’s learning and knowledge contributions to the development finance community focused on early-stage, last mile financing of development solutions.

5.) Manage efficiently UNCDF resources for learning, knowledge, and evaluations

• Support the planning and budgeting of learning, knowledge and evaluation activities in coordination with programme/project teams, ensuring realistic scope, timelines, resourcing, and value for money.

• Manage UNCDF’s learning, knowledge, and evaluation resources effectively and efficiently, monitoring budgets, workplans, deliverables, risks, and timelines.

• Lead the sourcing, selection, and onboarding of learning, knowledge, and evaluation firms, consultants, and technical specialists based on requirements, technical quality, and organizational procedures.

• Coordinate and supervise learning, knowledge, and evaluation consultants and technical specialists, ensuring timely delivery, quality of outputs, and alignment with requirements, organizational standards, and contractual obligations.

• Manage UNDCF’s relationship with UNDP’s Independent Evaluation Office in line with provisions of the UNDP Evaluation Policy.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities:

• The position will supervise one Programme Associate

• The Position will also supervise evaluation teams including consultants, IPSA and TA in the data collection, analysis, and reporting on UNCDF performance, using established evaluation criteria and methods.

Competencies

Core competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

Within the Global Policy Network (GPN), the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for SDGs. As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

Through SFH, UNDP’s Istanbul Center for Private Sector in Development (ICPSD), one of the five Global Thematic Policy Centers of UNDP, acts as an enabler for the private sector and foundations to become more active partners in development, encouraging them through policy advice and technical services on how to contribute towards the achievement of the 2030 Agenda. ICPSD was established in 2011 in partnership with the Government of Turkey. The Center’s work to engage foundations and the private sector focuses on delivering policy advice and technical services in four thematic areas:

- Private sector engagement through South-South cooperation for the SDGs

- Digital transformation and private sector engagement in skills development

- SDG Financing and Private Sector Development

- Resilience and crisis response

Under its “SDG Financing and Private Sector Development” thematic area, the Center offers research, advocacy and multi-stakeholder partnership services to diversify sources of financing for the sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with a focus on attracting private impact capital. Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will support UNDP ICPSD’s SDG Financing and Private Sector Development portfolio Country Offices and in advancing strategic knowledge management objectives, leading research, content development, partnership building and project management for the design and implementation of projects and activities in coordination and collaboration with the COs, RBx and SFH teams. Under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Lead, SDG Finance and Private Sector Development, the Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will provide technical support to the design and implementation of technical assistance products across the portfolio's multi-country pipeline, including credit guarantee mechanisms, and energy-sector investment facilitation, drawing on engineering experience in the energy sector and private sector engagement experience in post-conflict and crisis-affected settings.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the guidance of and reporting directly to the SDG Financing and Private Sector Development Portfolio Lead, the Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will be responsible for performing and contributing to the following:

Research, Partnership Intelligence and Knowledge Generation:

- Lead qualitative and quantitative background analysis and technical due diligence on energy infrastructure and energy transition investments to inform new project design and partnership development across ICPSD's portfolio.

- Conduct desk research and analytical work on energy markets, tariff structures, and generation/grid technologies to inform the design and operationalization of new private sector engagement initiatives.

- Develop and quality-assure evidence-based briefs, concept notes, strategy papers, partnership proposals, and programme documents on energy and private sector engagement in support of new project pipelines, including partnership agreements/MOUs and monitoring and evaluation frameworks, ensuring readiness for management approval and external engagement.

- Contribute to the implementation of ICPSD's knowledge management activities in the energy and private sector development area, including maintaining an updated repository of technical data, research, and partner intelligence to support ongoing partnership identification and pipeline development.

- Lead qualitative and quantitative background analysis on energy-sector investment opportunities, private sector engagement modalities, and blended finance mechanisms as they relate to the identification of new partnership and co-financing opportunities across ICPSD's portfolio.

- Conduct other research and information collection tasks related to energy and private sector engagement as required by ICPSD.

Programme, Partnership and Event Management:

- Lead end-to-end coordination of ICPSD programme and partnership-related activities on energy and private sector engagement, including identifying and securing venues, speakers, and guests; drafting and distributing outreach and invitations; managing event registration; and performing other related event management tasks.

- Develop and quality-assure the full suite of event documentation including press kits, logistics notes, briefing materials, and background papers on energy investment and private sector engagement, for stakeholder workshops and partner engagements.

- Design and deliver substantive research inputs for events, trainings, and workshops, including speaker briefings and evidence syntheses on energy investment, private sector development, blended finance, and partnership and resource mobilization opportunities.

- Support the content development and organization of national and international conferences, workshops, retreats, partner and donor engagement events, and other events organized by ICPSD in support of new energy and private sector engagement project and partnership development.

Management Coordination, Partnership Development, facilitate knowledge management and Strategic Support:

- Prepare and quality-review notes, presentations, and strategic summaries on energy and private sector engagement for senior management and external advisory functions, exercising independent judgment on framing, accuracy, and positioning.

- Identify and escalate emerging issues, risks, or opportunities relevant to ICPSD's energy and private sector engagement project and partnership pipeline, providing management with timely, evidence-based situational assessments.

- Lead the development of knowledge management products including methodologies, reports, and thematic briefs on energy and private sector engagement, ensuring outputs meet ICPSD quality standards and are fit for external dissemination.

- Participate in events and organizations related to energy and private sector engagement, actively identifying and cultivating new partnership and project development opportunities.

- Participate in project and partner/donor coordination meetings on energy and private sector engagement, as required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will work under the guidance of and reporting directly to the UNDP ICPSD SDG Financing and Private Sector Development Portfolio Lead.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

jobs.description:

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

At country level, the UNV Field Unit (FU) and/or designated UNV personnel are responsible for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes in the areas of peace, development and humanitarian assistance.  UNV Field Units/designated UNV personnel represent and position UNV in the respective countries with a focus on the UN Country Team, bringing UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners within a client service approach and collaborating with other stakeholders from government, civil society and private sector. As UNDP represents UNV at country level, UNV personnel are usually hosted within a UNDP Office and are accountable to the Supervisor and UNV Executive Coordinator for compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations

Scope of Work

1.Assist in mobilizing volunteers and developing and maintaining partnerships

- Support in the management of key accounts of assigned partnerships.

- Support and maintain relationships with assigned UN partner/s in the country/countries to ensure an understanding of UNV’s mandate, key offers and the added value that UN Volunteer assignments bring in support to the achievement of their respective mandates.

- Support in the identification of volunteer placement opportunities based on UN agency strategies and plans and present UNV value proposition and volunteer modalities with the objective of maximizing the relevance of volunteerism for impact.

- Support in the preparation of descriptions of assignment, with a focus on the assigned partners.

- Support in the development of offers and initiatives that respond to the evolving needs of partners for volunteer solutions.

- Contribute to the organization of advocacy campaigns, key events and other external communication efforts that raise awareness and foster engagement.

- Ensure knowledge is documented, systematized and fed back into volunteer mobilization, using UNV's Client Relationship Management (CRM) to track interactions and updates.

- In consultation with the Online Volunteering (OV) Programme Associate in the respective Regional Office, act as a focal point for online volunteers and accreditation of OV service organizations, focusing on supporting host entities with developing OV opportunities through advocacy engagements and promoting the concept of OV.

2. Contribute to business intelligence in support of strategic and sustained mobilization

- Support partnerships development by collecting and analyzing data of UN Cooperation Frameworks and agency programming frameworks to identify volunteer engagement areas.Record volunteer mobilization opportunities and business intelligence in CRM.

- Support in the engagement with potential partners by preparing presentations, mapping etc. on opportunities for volunteerism for internal use by UNV.

- Support the identification of opportunities for communicating on positive volunteer stories and strengthening visibility of the Agency partnership and the impact of volunteerism.

- Contribute to the development of key messages, talking points, and reports as needed.

3. Contribute to positive volunteer experience

- Provide support during the onboarding process, ensuring volunteers receive timely information, access to necessary resources, and a smooth start to their assignments.

- Provide support to UN Volunteers throughout the volunteer management cycle, ensuring timely assistance and guidance during key life events to foster a smooth, inclusive, and positive volunteer experience.

- Support volunteer engagement by responding to inquiries, sharing updates, and escalating concerns to relevant colleagues to ensure volunteers are supported throughout their service.

- Assist in gathering feedback from volunteers through surveys or informal check-ins and help compile and share insights to inform improvements in volunteer management practices.

- Support the organization of appreciation initiatives and local events to acknowledge volunteer contributions and foster a sense of belonging.

- Support the Country Coordinator in ensuring volunteers’ satisfaction with their assignment.

- Backstop other functions in the Field Unit/at country level during peak periods or personnel absences, ensuring continuity of service and contributing to a seamless and positive volunteer experience.

4. Support duty of care of UN Volunteers serving in the assigned area

- Liaise with the respective entities’ security focal points or heads of office, as applicable, and provide support to ensure a detailed and precise understanding among UN Volunteers on all security-related issues, including e.g. assistance with headcounts in emergency situations.

- Provide timely and accurate support to UN Volunteers undergoing medical evacuation, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV, while maintaining compliance with established procedures.

- Provide tailored support to UN Volunteers who do not speak the UN official language, to facilitate their understanding and providing key information, and navigate their assignment environment effectively throughout the volunteer management cycle.

- Provide host entities with comprehensive information on the enabling instruments available through UNV that support the health and wellbeing of UN Volunteers, such as insurance and related benefits.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the general guidance of the Regional Manager, with day-to-day reporting to the Country Coordinator, the Client Engagement Assistant supports the identification, development, and cultivation of select partnerships with UN Agencies / Host Entities at country level. This includes managing the relationship with priority partners, gathering and sharing data and information that influence mobilization opportunities, ensuring client satisfaction with volunteer services, and bridging the delivery of services from centralized functions of the volunteer management cycle. The critical purpose of this role is the sustained mobilization of volunteers to the designated partners (clients) and support to the duty of care for serving volunteers.

The role involves regular contact and liaison with counterpart UN personnel at all levels, including senior level staff. Within UNV, all personnel are expected to work across multiple units, functions, and teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

- Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Event planning and execution

- Ability to plan, manage and execute public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNV's overall brand and mandate

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education is required.

- A university degree in Social Sciences or related area will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with high school diploma) or 2 years (with bachelor’s degree) of practical and relevant experience at national or international level in partnership engagement, advocacy, management, client service or related areas.

Required skills:

- Experience in preparing presentation materials, including PowerPoint slides and talking points, as well as minute-taking and report drafting.

- Experience in the use of computers, oﬃce software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Previous experience with international or development organizations is considered an asset.

- Knowledge and experience of ticket-based service management systems (e.g. Salesforce/UNALL, or equivalent) is considered an asset.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and Arabic.

jobs.title: Monitoring & Evaluation Specialist [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria was created to significantly increase resources to fight three of the world’s most devastating diseases, and to direct those resources to areas of greatest need. The Global Fund attracts, manages and disburses resources in a public-private partnership that makes a sustainable and significant contribution to the reduction of mortality and morbidity caused by the three diseases and to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

UNDP is a key partner to the Global Fund to Fight HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (GFATM) and is the UN agency assuming the role of Principal Recipient of GFATM grants in South Sudan for TB and HIV/AIDS. In its role as Principal Recipient, UNDP ensures quality financial management, timely procurement of supplies, and efficient monitoring and delivery service. UNDP’s management role consists of implementing grants, ensuring financial accountability, and training of national and international counterparts on program management, financial accountability and timely programmatic reporting to the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) and Global Fund (GF) Secretariat.

Position Purpose

The Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will report to the Program Manager (Global Fund) and will work within the Program & M&E unit to support the Finance & QA unit, the PSM & Procurement unit and the Warehouse/Supply Chain Management team. The Specialist will liaise with the GF Country Team, the Local Fund Agent (LFA), the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), the Ministry of Health (MOH), the South Sudan AIDS Commission (SSAC), the National TB Program, the technical working groups responsible for HIV and TB, and various other partners and stakeholders. The incumbent will be required to travel to service delivery sites for the purpose of monitoring and supporting project activities.

Scope of Work

Under the overall guidance of the Program Manager (Global Fund), the Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will be responsible for the following key tasks:

Lead the GC8 monitoring and evaluation framework and plans:

- Lead the development and updating of M&E frameworks and plans for the HIV, TB and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) portfolio in coordination with MOH, SSAC and the National TB Program;

- Conduct regular analysis of grant performance against GC8 targets, identify implementation gaps and emerging risks, and recommend concrete corrective actions in coordination with program teams and sub-recipients;

- Develop M&E tools, indicator reference sheets and training materials for the PMU, SRs and implementing partners;

- Support SRs to strengthen their M&E systems for timely and accurate reporting;

- Supervise and monitor the work of any M&E consultants assigned to support the team;

- Conduct M&E capacity assessments of SRs and national partners and implement a capacity development plan;

- Review progress reports against targets and propose remedial actions for under-performing indicators;

- Monitor implementation bottlenecks and provide analytical inputs to program decision-making.

Deliver grant performance reporting to the Global Fund:

- Coordinate the preparation of Program Update, Discontinuation and Progress Reports (PUDRs), bi-annual and annual updates to the Global Fund;

- Consolidate quarterly programmatic information and ensure timely submission through corporate systems and the Global Fund transparency portal;

- Organize and document program review meetings, including preparation of background data and follow-up action points.

Assure data quality across the HIV and TB portfolios:

- Review data from HMIS/DHIS2 and program sources for completeness, accuracy and consistency;

- Plan and conduct routine data quality assessments (RDQA/DQA) and support sub-recipient site quality assurance (RSQA);

- Supervise, mentor and support the M&E Analyst (TB/HIV);

- Strengthen the use of routine program data, including DHIS2 and community-level reporting, to identify service delivery gaps, monitor coverage among key and vulnerable populations, and inform program adjustments.

Manage surveys, evaluations and learning:

- Coordinate baseline, mid-term and end-line surveys and evaluations, including drafting Terms of Reference and providing technical direction;

- Facilitate dissemination of evaluation findings and the preparation of management responses;

- Document lessons learned and promote their use in program design and grant revisions.

Build M&E capacity and support nationalization and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Deliver M&E and health information systems (HIS) training to MOH, SSAC, National TB Program staff and SRs, including NEPWU-NASOSS;

- Support the Country Dialogue Transition Plan (CDTP) and capacity transfer for progressive nationalization of the PR role;

- Develop and monitor measurable milestones for transferring M&E responsibilities to national institutions, including strengthened national ownership of data quality assurance, analysis and Global Fund reporting;

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the PMU, Country Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

The key impact of the post will be high-quality, timely monitoring, evaluation and reporting of the GC8 portfolio, sustaining the grant’s high-rating performance and enabling UNDP, the LFA and the Global Fund to verify results. The post also builds national M&E capacity, supporting data quality for HIV and TB services and the sustainability of interventions under the Country Dialogue Transition Plan. The position will be supervising M&E Analyst.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact;

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems;

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences;

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands;

jobs.title: Auxiliar en Relaciones Interinstitucionales de la Cooperación Sur – Sur
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

La implementación de los proyectos de “Sembrando Vida” y “Juntos por el Bienestar” en Centroamérica y el Caribe, forma parte de los compromisos adquiridos por la Presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo en el marco de la IX Cumbre de la Comunidad de Estados Latinoamericanos y Caribeños (CELAC) celebrada el 08 y 09 de abril del 2025 en Tegucigalpa, República de Honduras.

En ese marco, México reafirmó su voluntad de profundizar la cooperación regional a través de programas y/o proyectos de desarrollo inclusivo, priorizando el bienestar de las comunidades rurales y la promoción de la autosuficiencia alimentaria como motores de una prosperidad compartida.

Estos proyectos se apegan al principio de Prosperidad Compartida instruido por la Presidenta de México. La prosperidad compartida, que México proyecta en materia de cooperación internacional se refiere al beneficio mutuo de los países a nivel bilateral, regional y triangular, a través de la cooperación y el intercambio de experiencias, buenas prácticas y recursos. Este principio implica que los países colaboren entre sí para contribuir a erradicar el hambre y la pobreza, así como potenciar la sostenibilidad a través de acciones específicas para combatir el cambio climático y salvaguardar el medio ambiente.

Además, la ejecución de estos proyectos en Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Belice y Cuba, es parte de los compromisos que la Presidenta de México ha asumido con sus homólogos de esos países, a fin de promover las condiciones necesarias para el bienestar y desarrollo integral de la población, de manera inclusiva y participativa.

El objetivo de “Sembrando Vida” es contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria y al incremento de productividad de productores agrícolas que se encuentran en situación de retorno, o que sean residentes en departamentos y distritos con altos índices de migración, fomentando la implementación de sistemas de producción agrícola que incentiven el autoconsumo y la comercialización de excedentes mediante el acompañamiento y capacitación y reducir sus intenciones de migrar.

El objetivo de “Juntos por el Bienestar” es brindar oportunidades de capacitación laboral a personas de entre 18 y 55 años de edad, que no estudian y no trabajan, que se encuentren en situación de retorno, o que sean residentes de municipios con altos índices de migración, vulnerabilidad y desempleo. Las personas podrán realizar su capacitación en el sector privado, gubernamental o con Organizaciones de la Sociedad Civil.

La posición Auxiliar en Relaciones Interinstitucionales de la Cooperación Sur - Sur tiene como objetivo general apoyar a la Dirección General de Ejecución de Proyectos Especiales de Cooperación Internacional en la realización de actividades fortalecimiento de alianzas en Centroamérica.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1.Apoyar en el diseño e implementación de la estrategia regional de articulación multiactor.

- Apoyar en la interlocución estratégica y articulación entre la AMEXCID, gobiernos receptores, agencias de cooperación internacional y Organizaciones de la Sociedad Civil en el marco de la Cooperación Sur-Sur.

- Auxiliar en la Formulación y articulación de propuestas técnicas y hojas de ruta para el fortalecimiento de alianzas que aseguren la pertinencia territorial y sostenibilidad institucional de las acciones en Centroamérica.

- Ayudar a promover espacios de diálogo multiactor e intercambio de buenas prácticas entre las instituciones mexicanas y las contrapartes internacionales en materia de desarrollo inclusivo y prosperidad compartida.

2. Ayudar al equipo coordinador del proyecto para garantizar mesas técnicas de dialogo interinstitucional.

- Apoyar a posicionar los resultados del programa en foros regionales, agencias internacionales y redes académicas o de desarrollo.

- Ayudar en la logística de mesas técnicas e instancias de concertación periódicas entre autoridades nacionales de los países receptores, la AMEXCID y actores locales para asegurar la viabilidad política, pertinencia territorial y apropiación institucional del programa.

- Auxiliar en la elaboración del reporte, dictámenes de viabilidad de alianzas y memorándums de negociación multiactor para la Dirección General de Ejecución de Proyectos Especiales de Cooperación Internacional.

3. Apoyar en la transversalización de Género, Derechos Humanos e Inclusión en la Agenda Multiactor, y apoyar en la gestión de conocimiento.

- Apoyar en la promoción de la transversalización de la perspectiva de género y los diagnósticos interseccionales en todos los acuerdos interinstitucionales, protocolos de atención y planes de trabajo con las contrapartes de la Cooperación Sur-Sur.

- Ayudar en los módulos de capacitación y metodologías participativas orientadas a servidores públicos y equipos técnicos de los países socios sobre corresponsabilidad, equidad y transversalización del enfoque de derechos.

- Auxiliar para adaptar e incorporar estándares internacionales de derechos humanos, prevención del acoso/violencia laboral.

- Fomentar la creación y el intercambio de conocimientos pertinentes para el proyecto.

Desempeñar otras funciones relacionadas con su perfil que sean necesarias para el cumplimiento de los objetivos del proyecto.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: NIVEL 1: Planifica y supervisa su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajos de calidad dentro del plazo establecido.

Pensar de Forma Innovadora: NIVEL 1: Abierto a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, es pragmático en la resolución de problemas, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: NIVEL 1: Mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: NIVEL 1: Se adapta a los cambios, gestiona de forma constructiva la ambigüedad y la incertidumbre, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: NIVEL 1: Muestra empuje y motivación, capaz de actuar con calma ante la adversidad, seguro de sí mismo.

Participar y Asociarse: NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: NIVEL 1: Apreciar/respetar las diferencias, ser consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, enfrentarse a la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Educación secundaria (certificado de preparatoria) es requisito.

- Estudios universitarios de primer nivel (Licenciatura) en Ciencias de la Comunicación, Relaciones Internacionales, Negocios Internacionales o afín, se le dará debida consideración, pero no es requisito.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Mínimo 4 años (con educación secundaria (preparatoria)) o 1 año (con licenciatura) en la gestión y articulación de alianzas estratégicas.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en formulación de propuestas e iniciativas estratégicas para la movilización de recursos o alianzas técnicas.

- Experiencia de trabajo con equipos multidisciplinares.

Habildiades Deseadas:

- Experiencia gestionando fondos o proyectos con organismos multilaterales.

- Experiencia en la elaboración de iniciativas, reportes finales para la toma de decisiones con contrapartes.

- Experiencia en la integración de enfoques de género y derechos humanos en iniciativas de la cooperación internacional

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

2.Office/Unit/Project Description

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD) est l’organisation de référence du système des Nations Unies en matière de développement durable. Présent dans plus de 170 pays et territoires, il accompagne les États dans la mise en œuvre de solutions intégrées pour lutter contre la pauvreté, réduire les inégalités, renforcer la résilience des communautés et promouvoir une gouvernance démocratique, inclusive et efficace.

Au Sénégal, le cycle de coopération 2024-2028 du PNUD est aligné sur les priorités nationales de développement et contribue à l’accélération de l’atteinte des Objectifs de développement durable (ODD). Il vise notamment à renforcer la gouvernance démocratique, l’État de droit, l’accès à la justice, la participation citoyenne, la cohésion sociale, la redevabilité des institutions publiques ainsi que la prévention et la gestion des risques de conflits.

Le portefeuille Gouvernance du PNUD regroupe un ensemble de programmes et projets stratégiques mis en œuvre en partenariat avec les institutions nationales, les collectivités territoriales, les organisations de la société civile, le secteur privé et les partenaires techniques et financiers. Ces interventions visent à consolider les institutions démocratiques, promouvoir les droits humains, renforcer les mécanismes de transparence et de redevabilité, favoriser la participation inclusive aux processus décisionnels et soutenir les réformes institutionnelles nécessaires à un développement durable et équitable.

Dans un contexte marqué par l’expansion du portefeuille, la diversification des partenaires de mise en œuvre et le renforcement des exigences en matière de gestion axée sur les résultats, de suivi financier et de conformité opérationnelle, le PNUD souhaite renforcer son équipe Gouvernance à travers le recrutement d’un(e) Associé(e) en Administration et Support aux Projets. Sous la supervision du Team Leader Gouvernance, le/la titulaire du poste apportera un appui essentiel à la gestion administrative et financière des projets, au suivi budgétaire, à la conformité des opérations ainsi qu’à la coordination des processus de reporting et de mise en œuvre, contribuant ainsi à l’atteinte des résultats stratégiques du portefeuille.

3. Fonctions / Résultats attendus

Sous la supervision du Responsable du portefeuille Gouvernance et en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Programme, Opérations et les partenaires de mise en œuvre, l’Associé(e) en Administration et Support aux Projets contribue à la gestion efficace, transparente et conforme des ressources du portefeuille Gouvernance. Il/elle assure un appui administratif, financier et opérationnel à la mise en œuvre des projets, au suivi budgétaire, au reporting ainsi qu’au respect des règles et procédures du PNUD.

Ses fonctions et responsabilités sont les suivantes :

a. Appui à la gestion financière et budgétaire des projets

- Assurer le suivi de l’exécution budgétaire des projets du portefeuille Gouvernance et veiller à l’utilisation efficiente des ressources.

- Participer à la préparation, à la révision et à la mise à jour des budgets et plans de travail annuels (PTA).

- Effectuer le suivi des engagements, des dépenses et des disponibilités budgétaires.

- Produire des analyses financières périodiques et signaler les écarts ou risques éventuels afin de faciliter la prise de décision.

- Contribuer à la préparation des clôtures financières et des exercices de révision budgétaire.

b. Appui à la gestion administrative et opérationnelle

- Assurer le traitement et le suivi des réquisitions, contrats, paiements, avances et autres transactions administratives liées aux projets.

- Veiller à la conformité des dossiers administratifs et financiers conformément aux règles, procédures et politiques du PNUD.

- Appuyer l’organisation logistique des ateliers, missions, réunions, et autres activités du portefeuille.

- Appuyer les formations et le partage des connaissances

- Assurer l’archivage physique et électronique des documents administratifs et financiers des projets.

c. Suivi des partenaires de mise en œuvre et conformité

- Appuyer le suivi financier et administratif des partenaires de mise en œuvre conformément aux modalités de gestion du PNUD.

- Vérifier la complétude et la conformité des rapports financiers et pièces justificatives produits par les partenaires.

- Contribuer au suivi des recommandations issues des audits, micro évaluations, contrôles de qualité et exercices d’assurance.

- Participer à l’identification et à la gestion des risques financiers et opérationnels des projets.

d. Reporting, suivi financier et assurance qualité

- Préparer des tableaux de bord et rapports périodiques sur la situation financière et l’exécution des projets.

- Contribuer à la production des rapports destinés aux partenaires techniques et financiers, au management du PNUD et aux mécanismes de gouvernance des projets.

- Assurer la qualité, la fiabilité et la disponibilité des données administratives et financières.

- Soutenir le suivi des indicateurs de performance liés à la gestion financière et opérationnelle des projets.

e. Appui à la planification et à la coordination du portefeuille

- Contribuer à la planification des activités et au suivi de la mise en œuvre des plans de travail.

- Appuyer la coordination entre les équipes programme, opérations, finances et les partenaires de mise en œuvre.

- Participer à la préparation des réunions de revue des projets, des comités de pilotage et des missions de supervision.

- Assurer le suivi des actions convenues et des échéances administratives et financières.

- f. Gestion des connaissances et renforcement des capacités

- Contribuer à la capitalisation des bonnes pratiques et des leçons apprises en matière de gestion administrative et financière des projets.

- Participer à l’élaboration et à la mise à jour de procédures, guides, outils et modèles de gestion.

- Appuyer les activités de sensibilisation et de renforcement des capacités des partenaires et membres de l’équipe sur les procédures administratives et financières du PNUD.

- Promouvoir les principes de transparence, de redevabilité et de gestion axée sur les résultats dans la mise en œuvre des projets.

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.4. Arrangement institutionnel :

L’Associé(e) en Administration et Support aux Projets travaillera sous la supervision directe du Responsable du portefeuille Gouvernance du PNUD Sénégal. Il/elle apportera un appui administratif, financier et opérationnel à la mise en œuvre des projets du portefeuille, en veillant à la conformité des opérations, au suivi budgétaire, à la qualité du reporting et à l’application des procédures du PNUD, afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des résultats programmatiques du portefeuille Gouvernance.

5. Compétences

Core

Obtenir des résultats :

NIVEAU 1 : Planifie et supervise son propre travail, prête attention aux détails, fournit un travail de qualité dans les délais impartis.

Penser de manière innovante :

NIVEAU 1 : S'adapte au changement, gère de manière constructive l'ambiguïté/l'incertitude, fait preuve de souplesse.

Agir avec détermination :

NIVEAU 1 : Fait preuve d'enthousiasme et de motivation, capable de rester calme face à l'adversité, confiant.

NIVEAU 1 : Fait preuve de compassion/compréhension envers les autres, établit des relations positives.

- Être en mesure de gérer la mise en oeuvre de stratégies, de programmes et de projets en mettant l’accent sur l’amélioration des performances et l’obtention de résultats démontrables. Connaître et comprendre les théories, les concepts, les méthodologies, les instruments et les outils pertinents.

- Au moins 6 ans (avec un diplôme d'études secondaires) ou 3 ans (avec la licence) d'expérience progressive pertinente dans le soutien à la gestion administrative et financière de projet et/ou de la coordination est requis

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the leading development organization in Montenegro. UNDP has been part of the country’s success in many fields, including inclusive growth, environment, crisis management, governance, gender equality and the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Our United Nations identity ensures neutrality and respect of the country’s choices for the future. UNDP is committed to development as an advocate and enabler of change. Transparency and accountability in operation makes us a trusted partner for national and international development stakeholders. And the wide, international presence keeps UNDP close to development issues, resources and thinking in the countries we operate.

The United Nations Development Programme in Montenegro is contributing to the country’s development through the following programmatic priorities outlined in the Country Programme Document (CPD) 2023-2027: 1) Inclusive and Green Growth and Stewardship of Natural Resources, 2) Human Development and Social Inclusion and 3) Trusted, accountable, people-centered and gender-responsive institutions.

Furthermore, the UNDP commitment to gender equality is integral to all efforts to expand people’s choices, realize a just and sustainable world, and achieve the vision of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. UNDP will work through its six ‘signature solutions’, on poverty and inequality; governance; resilience; environment; energy; and gender equality.

UNDP Montenegro’s gender equality portfolio cuts across all programme pillars and combines a strong national policy and programming function with implementation of regional initiatives. The portfolio covers gender-based violence, social protection, governance and public administration, rule of law, women’s political participation and women’s economic empowerment. The regional women’s economic empowerment programme provides an additional platform for bringing regional evidence, approaches, partnerships and learning into the Montenegro country programme, while ensuring that national experience and results inform regional implementation and knowledge exchange.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under direct supervision of the Project Analyst for Economic Empowerment of Women and overall guidance of the Gender Equality Analyst, the incumbent will support the women’s economic empowerment component of the regional EU4Gender Equality Programme for the Western Balkans and national gender equality initiatives and programming by carrying out the following main tasks:

• Provide support to implementation of day-to-day activities under the regional EU4Gender Equality Programme and national gender equality programming

• Provide relevant administrative and logistical assistance in implementation of activities under the regional EU4Gender Equality Programme and national gender equality programming

• Perform regular financial tasks necessary for the successful and timely implementation of activities under the regional EU4Gender Equality Programme and national gender equality programming

I Provide support to implementation of day-to-day activities under the regional EU4Gender Equality Programme and national gender equality programming

• Draft routine correspondence and reports from oral instructions, previous correspondence or other available information sources, in accordance with the standard office procedures, and ensure appropriate follow-up; write minutes from the meetings; provide translation/interpretation services into English and vice versa, when needed

• Ensure all documentation (progress reports, consulting and other technical reports, minutes of meetings, etc.) are properly maintained in hard and electronic copies in an efficient and readily accessible filing system, for when required

• Assist the CO M&E officer in matters related to M&E and knowledge resources management and in the preparation of progress reports to donors, governance structures, corporate reports and CO management by continuously keeping track of implemented activities.

II Provide relevant administrative and logistical assistance in implementation of activities under the regional EU4Gender Equality Programme and national gender equality programming
