Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Central Africa is home to the second largest tropical rainforest in the world. Forest loss is accelerating despite ongoing efforts, as government action alone has not been sufficient to establish an effective balance between the interests of the forest and of economic development.

On this basis, a coalition of willing donors – Norway, European Union, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Netherlands, and South Korea – together with Central African partner countries – Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Cameroon, the Republic of Congo, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, and the Republic of Gabon – have entered in 2015 into a collaborative partnership to establish in partnership with the United Nations, the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI). The objective of this initiative is to recognize and preserve the value of the forests in the region to mitigate climate change, reduce poverty, and contribute to sustainable development. This objective will be attained through the implementation of country-led, national scale REDD+ and Low Emissions Development (LED) investment frameworks that include policy reforms and measures to address the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation and promote sustainable development.

The CAFI Trust Fund is the principal means to implement the Central African Forest Initiative. It is administered by the MPTF-Office (http://mptf.undp.org/factsheet/fund/AFI00). As per the updated Fund Terms of Reference and the direct cost Secretariat project document, the UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) is hosting the CAFI Secretariat providing the secretariat administrative services under the oversight of the CAFI Executive Board and other participating UN organizations (UNDP, UNCDF, FAO, UN-Habitat, UNFPA, and UNEP).

Established by the Executive Board, the CAFI Secretariat was created to support the fund management coupled with policy and programmatic dialogue and portfolio administration, strongly based on result-based management and solid reporting methods. With the intensification of CAFI presence in countries and solid increase in investment programmes and related digital innovations, including but not limited to the introduction of Payment for Environmental Services, a Technical Assistance Facility, Private Sector projects, it is fundamental that the Secretariat provides high-efficiency M&E services to support the Trust Fund objectives. This requires an M&E Unit led by an expert Head of M&E that can efficiently work across all CAFI partner countries and portfolio accordingly namely DRC, Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Gabon, embracing and helping to expand CAFI’s digital ecosystem in support of M&E in general and performance-based programming in particular.

Position Purpose

Under the strategic guidance of the Head of Secretariat, the Team Lead f the Monitoring and Evaluation and Risk Management Unit promotes results-based management and a programme effectiveness approach, by leading the design and implementation of innovative and effective monitoring, evaluation and learning frameworks, systems and tools, and implements a robust approach to risk management across the investment portfolio of the Trust Fund, serving the Executive Board in risk-based decision making approach. Where relevant, the Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management will also support programme quality assurance and developing relevant systems. The Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management provides technical support on M&E and reporting practices to the business unit`s senior management as well as programme and project teams. The Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management promotes a collaborative, efficient, client-focused, evidence-based, and portfolio management approach.

The Team Lead of M&E and risk leads a team of personnel working on M&E and RBM, and as applicable, quality assurance work; collaborates closely with Programme, Operations and project teams in other branches and across partners and donors, programme staff in other UN agencies, and Government officials, technical advisers and experts, NGOs, and other organizations on programme implementation and monitoring and evaluation issues and practices.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Lead in designing and implementing the monitoring and evaluation frameworks, systems, and tools at Fund level and conduct quality assurance of the overall Fund’s portfolio.

• Develop integrated monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and results-based management (RBM) policies, frameworks, systems/tools and plans at Fund level, in line with CAFI’s Terms of Reference and CAFI’s Manual of Operations and its related policies towards programmes, projects and initiatives, to inform on their adequate implementation, and ensure their effectiveness and compliance with the Fund programming and reporting requirements.

• Development, continued improvement and implementation of CAFI M&E and Learning policy and strategies/Plans (e.g. the Fund’s evaluation strategy/plan), as well as related guidelines, minimum standards, procedures and templates.

• Develop SOPs and guidelines for CAFI Secretariat staff, partner countries and implement organizations.

• Coordinate partner countries in adapting, if and as required, CAFI’s M&E framework, procedures and tools to their context, while ensuring full alignment with CAFI’s.

• Participate in CAFI’s annual planning processes, defining targets and harmonized indicators to ensure consistency with CAFI’s policies across CAFI’s portfolio of programmes and projects.

• Contribute to the elaboration and mapping of business processes and procedures in programme and project oversight that includes providing input to establishment of quality assurance processes, guidance notes, protocols, tools, checklists, and sharing best practices.

• Provide technical, innovative and policy advice on M&E and RBM requirements and activities to programme and project managers, staff concerned with monitoring and evaluation, and consultants and/or members of the evaluation team. Collaborate with Programme and project teams on developing integrated development approaches.

• Ensure gender equality, disability inclusion, and Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principles are an integral part of programmes and operations and that these considerations are fully mainstreamed into programming and reflected in project design, monitoring, reporting, and evaluations in line with the UNDP Gender Equality and Disability Inclusion Strategies, UNSDG Operational Guide for Country Teams on LNOB, and available regional guidance.

• Develop the evaluation plan and ensure its timely implementation in line with CAFI standards for the CAFI funded programs/projects, Letters of Intent and the Trust Fund (such as independent evaluations, mid-term reviews, tranche releases).

• Ensure monitoring of data collection by projects, analyze and exploit data combining layers of maps, photo and satellite images, text and statistics.

• Facilitate the development and implementation of spatial monitoring through a dedicated structured geographic information system integrating data acquisition, administration, processing, analysis and dissemination, with support from specialized personnel.

• Support the implementation and growth of CAFI’s ecosystem of digital tools in support of efficiency and transparency, in synergy with colleagues from the programming and PES teams (specifically CAFI Connect and CAFI PES).

2.) Lead coordination of monitoring, reporting, evaluation and results-based management of CAFI programmes and projects.

• Oversee implementation and application of efficient and evidence-based results monitoring, and as applicable, quality assurance work for programme and project development and delivery using integrated portfolio management approach as well as the CAFI Connect tool and the CAFI PES dashboard

• Ensure timely identification of potential implementation problems and bottlenecks and advise the management and programme/project teams on strategies/corrective measures to address them.

• Lead the cross-cutting reviews, studies and evaluations of the M&E unit.

• Manage and coordinate third-party monitoring and/or any other data collection intervention.

• Review and approve all plans and Terms of Reference (TOR) for project and programme mid-term reviews, evaluations, and assessments. Participate in consultant and evaluation team recruitment and selection. Review and provide input on evaluation inception reports, evaluation methodology, and draft evaluation reports for quality assurance and compliance purposes.

• Ensure the optimal use of evaluation findings and recommendations. Provide guidance and input in the preparation of timely management responses and key actions to all evaluations; consolidate evaluation findings to assess effectiveness and impact of programmes/projects; and develop a communication/dissemination plan to incorporate into recommendations for improvement by projects and partners. Follow up on implementation of evaluation recommendations by project teams.

• Facilitate collation of monitoring and evaluation of impact results and/or data/information in a format that is relevant for evidence-based policy, communications and/or development interventions.

• Drive the application of CAFI’s social and environmental safeguards as applicable as part of the reporting exercises and the programme evaluation strategy.

• Lead the development of funded evaluation plans that accompany the development of programme documents and oversee the timely implementation of evaluations in the plan.

• Provide support, as applicable, in ensuring projects are designed, implemented, and completed in line with RBM and quality standards and programme and project management policies and procedures.

• Provide input into the independent verification of land use projects as per relevant EB decisions.

3.) Provide substantive contributions to capacity building and facilitate knowledge building and sharing on monitoring, evaluation, and results-based management

• Contribute to the assessment of capacity needs and elaboration of capacity development plans, tools, and methodologies. Design, organize and lead training activities; and participate in preparing knowledge packages on RBM, monitoring and evaluation, data collection/survey methods, gender mainstreaming and portfolio approach programme and project teams as well as national partners and key stakeholders.

• Lead the identification, synthesis, documentation, and dissemination of key lessons learned and good practices derived from monitoring and evaluation activities on what works, what does not work, and/or revised theories of change to identify innovative ideas for their scaling or replication.

• Provide sound contributions to local and global networks, communities of practice, and other knowledge management mechanisms. Proactively participate in regional and international fora on relevant thematic areas (including engaging in thematic discussions, contributing with analytical papers, etc.).

4.) Lead solid and efficient Reporting

• Ensure donor reports are timely prepared in line with established requirements. Prepare Results Reports, analysis of results of projects, and other periodic information and reports for the Executive Board, government partners, donor community and other key stakeholders. Advise on data use and interpretation to assess country programme results, improve programme quality, identify trends, and inform future decision-making processes.

• With direct support from CAFI’s Reporting Specialist, facilitate the reporting exercises across CAFI`s portfolio of funded projects, incorporation of lessons learned from previous exercises and semi-annual reporting to the Executive Board on the compliance of the reporting function. Provide regular update to the Executive Board on project and portfolio performance based on the information in the CAFI Connect and CAFI PES dashboard and narrative reports.

• Lead the organization and execution of accountability sessions with implementing partners to drive performance and reinforce a results culture

5.) Lead Implementation of Risk Management Framework across CAFI Portfolio

• Develop and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework for the Trust Fund, maintaining updated all related Policies and SOPs.

• Identify and assess risks across key categories, taking due diligence and reporting as per Risk Policies in place.

• Conduct risk assessments at portfolio, program, and country levels.

• Lead and guide funded projects in conducting risk due diligence.

• Maintain and regularly update a risk register.

• Design and implement risk mitigation strategies and internal controls.

• Advise program teams and implementing partners on risk reduction measures, compliance requirements and preventive controls such as procurement safeguards and financial oversight

• Ensure integration of risk management into program design and approval processes.

• Drive the development and oversee the implementation of contingency and risk response plans.

• Co-lead fiduciary risk oversight by working in collaboration with Management Specialist to monitor financial management reports from implementing organizations.

• Proactively track risk indicators and early warning signals to identify emerging threats; escalate critical risks to accordingly and propose corrective actions

• Contribute to the preparation of annual reports and portfolio reviews with a risk perspective.

• In collaboration with the Policy Dialogue Unit, conduct due diligence assessments of implementing partners in regard to their Institutional capacity, Governance systems and financial management capabilities

• Lead the risk due diligence for all prospective partners and new program designs to ensure risk is integrated into all approval processes

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervises M&E Specialist (IPSA) and MRV and Compliance Manager (IPSA)

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction and Strategy-System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management-Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment

Business Management & Monitoring & Evaluation:

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks.

- Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Business Management & Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

Partnership Management & Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

2030 Agenda: Engagement & Effectiveness: Programmatic Risk Management and Analysis.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Development/Development Studies, Economics, Statistics, Business Management, Social Policy, or related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, programme and/or team management working with quality assurance instruments, results-based management models, and multiple stakeholders is required.

- Proven experience in the Monitoring & Evaluation of a large Fund is required.

- Experience and proven technical knowledge of the results-based management cycle and monitoring and evaluation is required.

- Proven experience in designing monitoring and evaluation systems and designing development projects or integrated portfolios is required.

- Proven ability to work with quantitative and qualitative data and appropriately use qualitative data /information collection tools in innovative ways is required.

- Demonstrated experience in using GIS tools (e.g. QGIS, ArcGis), mobile data collection tools (e.g. Kobo toolbox, ODK), remote sensing applications and data treatment software (e.g. SPSS) is an asset.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), and web-based management systems, and up-to-date, advanced knowledge of data management tools and database packages is required.

- Experience in designing, implementing and/or managing assessments and/or data collection exercises/processes is desired.

- Experience in using project management or project portfolio management softwares (e.g. TECPRO, MSPRO) is an advantage.

- Certification in Enterprise Risk Management or related is desired.

- Expertise in fiduciary oversight and financial controls is desired.

- Experience conducting applied research projects and reporting on findings is desired.

Languages:

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required

- Fluency in written and spoken French is required

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.description:
Aproximación por Niveles (Tiered Approach)

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organización, la mayoría de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicación por niveles (tiers) en donde:

- Nivel 0: personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos sáran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

- Nivel 1: otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

- Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas

- Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor tenga en cuenta del nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si lo hay, y asegúrese de que cumple con la elegibilidad para aplicar.

Descripción del proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

El PNUD trabaja en más de 170 países y territorios, dando asistencia para desarrollar políticas, habilidades de liderazgo y asociación, capacidades institucionales y construcción de resiliencia, fomentando el desarrollo humano sostenible. En Panamá trabaja a nivel nacional, nivel municipal y comarcal. El PNUD hace parte de las Agencias, Fondos y Programas de las Naciones Unidas en Panamá aportando al logro del Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible (UNSDCF en inglés).

Por más de 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

- Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

- Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

- Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

Dentro del Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental, se brinda asistencia al Gobierno de Panamá en alineamiento con el Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible en Panamá 2026-2030 y el Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2030, los cuales destacan la necesidad de fortalecer el capital humano, reducir las desigualdades y apoyar la innovación y el crecimiento sostenible.

El proyecto “Latidos del Barrio: Cultura que Transforma Comunidades” es una iniciativa impulsada por el Ministerio de Cultura con apoyo del PNUD, orientada a fortalecer la inclusión social, la cohesión comunitaria, la participación ciudadana, el acceso a servicios culturales y formativos, la activación deportiva y la economía creativa en territorios priorizados. El proyecto operará mediante una Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto, con enfoque territorial, gestión basada en resultados, articulación interinstitucional, acompañamiento comunitario y cumplimiento de los procedimientos aplicables del PNUD.

Alcance del trabajo

El/La Asociado/a de Adquisiciones deberá conducir y ejecutar los procesos de adquisiciones de bienes, contrataciones de servicios, contratos de obras y logística detallados en el Plan de Adquisiciones para el proyecto 1005658: “Latidos del barrio: Cultura que transforma comunidades” utilizando el método de contratación requerido de acuerdo con cada adquisición.

El objetivo de esta posición es asegurar que las adquisiciones de bienes, obras y servicios se realicen conforme a las normas, políticas y procedimientos de PNUD.

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

1. Planificación:

- Apoyar en la elaboración, actualización y seguimiento del Plan de Adquisiciones, en conjunto con el Proyecto, con el fin de determinar los procedimientos y la metodología requerida para cada proceso de adquisición.

- Desarrollar términos de referencia para las adquisiciones que sean requeridos por el proyecto según el plan de adquisiciones, y revisar y proponer los ajustes que sean necesarios a dichos términos de referencia elaborados por la respectiva unidad solicitante.

- Realizar investigación de mercado, buscar y pre-calificar a proveedores potenciales según las necesidades establecidas en el plan de adquisiciones, y así tenerlos identificados oportunamente para lograr llevar a cabo procesos más competitivos.

2. Ejecutar Procesos de Adquisiciones:

- Efectuar el proceso de solicitud de cotizaciones (RFQ), solicitud de propuesta (SDP), invitación a licitación (ITB), consultorías, contrataciones directas u otros procesos competitivos de acuerdo con la normativa vigente según cada renglón del Plan de Adquisiciones, para compra de bienes y servicios.

- Gestionar y dar seguimiento a las actividades correspondientes a cada caso, de acuerdo con el proceso de adquisiciones que se llevará a cabo, a saber: Revisar, en caso de no haberse realizado en la fase de planificación, los términos de referencia del proceso de adquisiciones que se va a desarrollar. Solicitar cotizaciones, enviar invitaciones, hacer publicaciones a través de los canales de comunicación establecidos. Coordinar y organizar las conferencias previas de los procesos de adquisiciones que así lo requieran. Recibir ofertas de los proveedores y atender sus consultas oportunamente. Organizar el panel para la evaluación de las propuestas recibidas, velando por el cumplimiento de las normas en cuanto a imparcialidad, conflicto de interés, confidencialidad para cada proceso. Levantar las actas y hacer recomendación según resultado de matriz de evaluación. Comunicar a los proponentes, formular órdenes de compra y/o contrato con el PNUD según sea el caso.

3. Coordinación:

- Revisar periódicamente listado de procesos asignados para ejecutar las tareas que correspondan según el flujo establecido y cumplir con los tiempos de ejecución acordados.

- Notificar oportunamente a la Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto sobre los avances o cualquier situación que pueda producir atrasos. Asimismo, deberá entregar a la Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto informes semanales de progreso de los procesos de adquisición pendientes.

- Apoyar a la Unidad Coordinadora de Proyecto en el seguimiento de los contratos adjudicados.

4. Gestión Documental y Aprendizaje:

- Recopilar las lecciones aprendidas durante la ejecución del proyecto.

5. Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes para el proyecto.

- Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción.

- Brindar apoyo en la difusión e intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas dentro de la oficina de país y a nivel regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes a nivel nacional, regional e internacional relacionadas con el trabajo del proyecto asignado.

- Realizar contribuciones valiosas a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia distribución a los socios.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la Asociado/a de Adquisiciones estará asignado al proyecto 1005658: “Latidos del barrio: Cultura que transforma comunidades” bajo la supervisión del/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto.

Movilización: Esta posición estará basada en las Oficinas de PNUD Panamá, Costa del Este, P.H. Dream Plaza, Piso 12, Avenida Centenario. En caso de requerirse desplazamientos a los territorios priorizados (Centros Latidos del Barrio), los gastos de movilización, hospedaje y alimentación serán cubiertos por el proyecto conforme a los procedimientos aplicables.

Competencias

Competencias esenciales

- LOGRO DE RESULTADOS - NIVEL 1: Planifica y supervisa su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles, entrega un trabajo de calidad antes de la fecha límite.

- PIENSA DE MANERA INNOVADORA - NIVEL 1: Abierto a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, es pragmático solucionador de problemas, hace mejoras.

- APRENDE CONTINUAMENTE - NIVEL 1: De mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

- SE ADAPTA CON AGILIDAD - NIVEL 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja constructivamente la ambiguedad/incertidumbre, es flexible.

- ACTÚA CON DETERMINACIÓN - NIVEL 1: Muestra impulso y motivación, capaz de rendir con calma frente a la adversidad confiado.

- COMPROMISO Y ASOCIACIÓN - NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión, comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

- DIVERSIDAD E INCLUSIÓN - NIVEL 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Competencias transversales

- DIRECCIÓN Y ESTRATEGIA INSTITUCIONAL PENSAMIENTO ESTRATÉGICO : Elaborar estrategias eficaces y planes prioritarios en consonancia con la misión y los objetivos del PNUD, fundamentados en el análisis sistémico de las dificultades, las oportunidades y los riesgos potenciales; conectar la visión general con la situación real para crear soluciones específicas tangibles; incorporar aprendizajes de diversas fuentes para anticiparse a las tendencias actuales y futuras, y responder a ellas con eficacia; demostrar capacidad de previsión. TOMA DE DECISIONES EFICAZ : Tomar decisiones de forma oportuna y eficaz, en consonancia con la autoridad, el ámbito de especialización y los recursos que se tengan, y tener en cuenta el potencial de las implicaciones generales.

- DESARROLLO INSTITUCIONAL GENERACIÓN DE CONOCIMIENTOS : Capacidad para buscar información y convertirla en conocimiento útil, pertinente para el contexto o que responda a una necesidad planteada. Capacidad para aplicar los conceptos existentes a nuevas situaciones y desarrollar nuevos conceptos para generar soluciones viables y nuevos enfoques. Conocimiento de conceptos, modelos conceptuales y teorías relevantes que puedan resultar útiles para abordar situaciones nuevas. INTEGRACIÓN DENTRO DE LAS NACIONES UNIDAS : Capacidad de identificar e integrar la capacidad y los activos del sistema de las Naciones Unidas, y de participar en las labores conjuntas. Conocimiento del sistema de las Naciones Unidas y capacidad para aplicar dicho conocimiento a situaciones estratégicas o prácticas.

Competencias técnicas

- ADQUISICIONES GESTIÓN DE ADQUISICIONES : Capacidad de adquirir bienes, servicios y obras de una fuente externa. PROCURE-TO-PAY : Conocimiento de los ciclos de compras y pagos, así como de sus conceptos, principios y políticas y capacidad para aplicarlos a situaciones estratégicas o prácticas.

Habilidades y experiencia requeridas

Educación

- Se requiere educación secundaria completa. O bien,

- Experiencia en la implementación de procesos de adquisiciones conforme a las metodologías establecidas por organismos internacionales y PNUD.

Idiomas

- Deseable nivel básico de lectura y escritura en inglés (no es un requisito excluyente).

Información importante para las/os postulantes

Todos los puestos en las categorías NPSA están sujetos a contratación local.

Igualdad de Oportunidades

El PNUD, como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que opera. En este sentido, se alienta a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postularse a las vacantes de la organización. Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

jobs.title: Asociado/a Adquisiciones
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

La Unidad de Operaciones del PNUD, específicamente el área de Adquisiciones requiere los servicios profesionales de personal que se integre al equipo del área con el fin de contribuir al desarrollo de diferentes procesos de los distintos programas y proyectos del PNUD.

El PNUD en Honduras facilita el acceso a asesorías en políticas, finanzas y programas para crear soluciones innovadoras y audaces que aceleren los esfuerzos nacionales para abordar los complejos desafíos del desarrollo. Emplea un enfoque integrador, involucrando activamente y forjando alianzas con diversos actores en la sociedad comprometidos con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y el bienestar del país. El PNUD está presente en unos 170 países y territorios, ofrece una perspectiva global y un conocimiento local.

A través de sus programas, el PNUD en Honduras trabaja para promover la participación ciudadana y el goce de derechos al desarrollo trabajando en pilares esenciales para el fortalecimiento de un Estado de Derecho. En ese sentido, su trabajo en el área de gobernabilidad democrática se centra en apoyar reformas, mecanismos y veedurías a favor de la representatividad y la participación ciudadana. Se promueve mejoras en el ejercicio de los derechos humanos con enfoque en el derecho al desarrollo y los derechos de las mujeres, pueblos indígenas y afro-hondureños, y el fortalecimiento de la transparencia y la eficacia en la prestación de servicios públicos.

El rol del PNUD en la ejecución general de proyectos se realiza a través de dos funciones principales: (i) apoyo especializado, supervisión y control de calidad, que incluye actividades de apoyo técnico para la planificación, implementación, seguimiento y evaluación del proyecto; y (ii) apoyo técnico operativo, a solicitud del Gobierno y/o socios, tales como adquisición de bienes y servicios, emisión de boletos, tarifas diarias, pagos, organización de eventos, gestión de recursos humanos, entre otros.

El Objetivo principal de esta posición es realizar procesos de adquisición de bienes, servicios y/u obras relacionados y la selección de consultores individuales para el/los proyecto(s), empleando para ello la normativa correspondiente.

Duties and Responsibilities

Funciones:

- Apoyar el seguimiento integral a los procesos de adquisición y contratación, incluida la adjudicación y negociación de contratos, de conformidad con las normas y los procedimientos establecidos.

- Asesorar a la UP en las estrategias de adquisición de bienes, obras y servicios que mejor respondan a los objetivos planteados. Asesorar y acompañar en el proceso de construcción de lo términos de referencia y especificaciones técnicas cuando se requiera. Apoyar en elaborar, actualizar y dar seguimiento a los planes de adquisiciones y contratos (PAC) de proyectos, en coordinación con la Unidad de Programa(UP) y con base en los Planes Operativos Anuales (POA). Apoyar en la elaboracion oportunamente de documentos estándar y específicos para todas las modalidades de adquisición y contratación contempladas en el PAC, según aplique.

- Contribuir al fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal de oficina y proyectos en temas referentes a procedimientos y políticas de adquisiciones.

- Fungir como secretario/a , en comisiones evaluadoras, orientar a los miembros y realizar las gestiones necesarias para el buen funcionamiento de las mismas.

- Garantizar el mantenimiento actualizado de los expedientes documentales y electrónicos de los procesos de adquisiciones incluyendo, pero no limitándose a: proceso de selección, contrato y enmiendas y evaluaciones de desempeño.

- Garantizar el pleno cumplimiento de las operaciones con las normas, reglamentos, políticas y el Marco de Control Interno (ICF) del PNUD.

- Apoyar otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que considere necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y de la Organización.

Competencies

Esenciales

Lograr Resultados:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión:

NIVEL : Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación

Competencias Transversales y Técnicas

Área Temática

Nombre

Capacidad para investigar información y convertirla en conocimiento útil, relevante para el contexto o que responda a una necesidad planteada. Capacidad para aplicar conceptos existentes a nuevas situaciones y desarrollar nuevos conceptos para generar soluciones viables y nuevos enfoques. Conocimiento de conceptos, modelos conceptuales y teorías relevantes que puedan ser útiles para abordar nuevas situaciones.

Comunicar de manera clara, concisa, sin ambigüedades, tanto de manera verbal como escrita; adaptar mensajes y elegir métodos de comunicación según audiencia.

Background

The Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC) serving as the implementing partner and UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the project supports national and local governments in accelerating the transition toward sustainable, resilient, low-carbon, and people-centered urban development. The project promotes integrated urban planning, climate-smart infrastructure, sustainable mobility systems, resource-efficient urban services, enhanced urban biodiversity, and accessible green public spaces. It also strengthens institutional capacities and inclusive governance mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of citizens, communities, civil society organizations, the private sector, and vulnerable groups in urban development and decision-making processes. Through these interventions, the project contributes to creating greener, more resilient, and more inclusive cities that improve quality of life while advancing Mongolia's climate and sustainable development objectives.

The Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry (MOFALI) serving as the implementing partner and the UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by GEF, the project supports national efforts to reduce the use and release of hazardous chemicals across key economic sectors and supply chains.

The project seeks to strengthen the policy and regulatory framework for chemicals management, enhance institutional and technical capacities, improve industry practices, promote the adoption of safer and more sustainable alternatives, and increase transparency and accountability among public and private sector stakeholders. It also supports knowledge generation, awareness raising, and multi-stakeholder engagement to facilitate informed decision-making and responsible chemicals management throughout product life cycles. Through these interventions, the project contributes to reducing environmental pollution and health risks, advancing circular economy principles, and accelerating Mongolia's transition toward greener production systems and sustainable consumption patterns.

The Admin and Finance Associate will provide administrative, financial, and logistical support for the effective implementation of the GEF Funded projects of UNDP Mongolia. Under the direct supervision of the respective Project Managers and in close coordination with the UNDP Country Office operations team, the incumbent will support project budgeting, financial planning and reporting, travel and event logistics, asset and inventory management, records management, and compliance with UNDP, GEF, and national implementation modality (NIM) requirements. The Associate will ensure timely processing of financial transactions, maintain accurate project documentation, monitor expenditures against approved budgets, support project audits and reviews, and facilitate administrative coordination among implementing partners, government institutions, service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure efficient and accountable project delivery and achievement of project results.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administrative and Finance Associate provides integrated operational, financial, and administrative support to the Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project and the Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project, ensuring efficient implementation, compliance, and coordination across both GEF-funded initiatives. Working closely with Project Managers, implementing partners, and the UNDP Country Office, the Associate supports financial management, administrative processes, logistics, and reporting to facilitate the timely and accountable delivery of project results.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Project Managers, the Admin and Finance Associate is responsible for project implementation support services, ensuring effective operational management of the project and transparent utilization of financial resources. The Admin and Finance Associate promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. The Admin and Finance Associate works in close collaboration with the Project Implementing Unit (PIU) and the Country Office.

Summary of key functions:

- Financial Management and Budget Administration

- Assets Management

- Administrative Travel support

- Actively contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, operational plans, and procurement plans to support effective project implementation

- Maintain project financial records and supporting documentation in accordance with UNDP, GEF, and Government requirements

- Process budgets, fund allocations, payments, advances, and financial transactions through Quantum and other applicable systems

- Verify the accuracy and completeness of financial documents and ensure timely resolution of financial processing issues

- Maintain effective internal controls and ensure compliance with UNDP financial rules, regulations, and procedures

- Monitor budget utilization, expenditures, cash flow, and delivery rates, and advise the NPC on variances, risks, and corrective actions

- Prepare financial forecasts, analyses, and periodic financial reports to support project planning, decision-making, and reporting requirements.

Financial Management and Budget Administration

- Monitor project financial performance and expenditures against approved GEF budgets, work plans, and results frameworks;

- Track, verify, and report co-financing contributions in accordance with GEF requirements and reporting standards;

- Coordinate with UNDP, government counterparts, implementing partners to ensure timely submission Government of Mongolia, UNDP, and GEF financial reports and supporting documentation;

- Ensure compliance with UNDP POPP, GEF, NIM, and relevant Government regulations;

- Contribute to gender-responsive budgeting and tracking of expenditures related to gender equality and social inclusion.

Assets Management:

- Ensure effective inventory and asset management in compliance with applicable Government of Mongolia, UNDP policies and procedures;

- Participate in periodic physical verification of project assets and inventories, prepare and submit inventory verification reports, and process all required asset receiving and disposal documentation;

- Manage the transfer, reassignment, and disposal of project assets in accordance with Government of Mongolia and UNDP asset management rules, regulations, and established procedures.

Administrative and Travel Support:

- Support the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, operational plans, and procurement plans;

- Provide administrative, logistical, and travel support for project activities, including meetings, missions, training, workshops, conferences, and seminars;

- Maintain office supplies, inventory records, contract files, project documentation, and archives in accordance with established procedures;

- Prepare and monitor procurement and contractual documentation and maintain an up-to-date contract management system;

- Support the preparation of project reports and ensure proper filing, record management, and archiving of project documents;

- Facilitate coordination among projects, partners, and related initiatives to promote collaboration and synergies;

- Document, compile, and disseminate project knowledge, lessons learned, and good practices, and contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Monitor and share relevant national, regional, and international best practices to support project implementation and learning;

- Perform other administrative, operational, and financial tasks as assigned by the Project Manager to support effective project delivery.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Business Management

- Results-based Management - Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools

- Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Working with Evidence and Data -Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends

Provide inputs to the development of customer service stratege. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

jobs.title: SIDS Coalition for Nature Coordinator (Home Based)
jobs.description:
Background

The Blue & Green Islands Integrated Programme (BGI IP) is a transformative and comprehensive initiative designed to address pressing environmental challenges faced by Small Island Developing States (SIDS). These Countries, due to their small size, remote locations, and reliance on limited resources, are highly vulnerable to climate change impacts and other shocks. The programme will leverage significant innovation emerging from SIDS to turn their most pressing challenges into opportunities for prosperity, enabling them to build forward better, greener and bluer.

The overall objective of the BGI IP’s Global Coordination Project (GCP) is to enhance collaboration, capacity and partnerships among 15 BGI IP country projects in valuing nature, scaling up of nature-based solutions in the food, tourism, and urban sectors, and securing public and private finance to facilitate nature-positive development and reduce ecosystem degradation in SIDS. This will be achieved by demonstrating the transformational potential of incorporating the value of nature into decision-making and using innovative nature-based solutions to achieve development and MEA goals and address SIDS challenges related to food security, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and reduction of hazardous chemical pollution.

A Global Programme Coordination Unit (GPCU) has been established by the GCP for the overall BGI IP. The GPCU is responsible for the overarching management and coherence of the BGI-IP through workstreams including day-to-day programmatic coordination of the Policy and Practice Facility, Knowledge Management and Learning Cluster, and Nature Based Solutions Accelerator, capacity development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting, adaptive management, technical coherence and advice, compliance, knowledge management, cross-project collaboration and networking, and facilitation of joint learning, solutions sharing, and upscaling efforts. The GPCU works to optimize strategic engagement with key multi-stakeholder bodies and platforms for policy coherence and change at global, regional, and national levels. This is done through collective action and a clear agenda established in collaboration with the IP’s country and institutional partners, to assure a seat at the table on policy and related discussions relevant to SIDS and the IP context.

The GPCU is responsible for programme level support to the Country Projects and for receiving and collating information on the state of the Programme for the PSC, and for organizing the annual meeting of the GCP and all the 15 Country Projects, as well as quarterly meetings of the BGI IP PSC, and for collating and disseminating all programme M&E results. Effective participation from key BGI IP countries will be ensured through Regional Nodes and Thematic Working Groups, where country project managers come together to exchange best practices and learning around themes such as evidence-based nature-based solutions, public and private sector engagement and finance, monitoring and evaluation, safeguards, gender, etc.

The SIDS Coalition for Nature (SCN) was launched at the 15th Conference of the Parties of the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP15) in 2022. The Coalition aims to catalyze SIDS strategic partnerships and advocate as ‘one’ for SIDS priorities. Through the Coordinator, BGI will work with the Coalition to elevate SIDS leadership, strengthen regional and global policy alignment, mobilize partnerships, and scale integrated solutions emerging from the BGI-IP. The Coordinator will lead, operationalize, and manage the Coalition’s activities in close coordination with the Coalition and AOSIS, governments, and regional bodies including SPREP, CARICOM, and IOC.

Scope of Work

The SIDS Coalition for Nature Coordinator will be responsible for leading and coordinating the development, functioning, and strategic engagement of the SIDS Coalition for Nature. S/he will facilitate strengthened regional and global collaboration among SIDS, support the upscaling of country project results and ensure coherent representation of SIDS priorities in relevant multilateral processes and policy platforms, and ensure effective coordination with and integration of Nature and the BGI mission into the wider SIDS Agenda. The Coordinator will engage with the leadership and members of the SIDS Coalition for Nature, AOSIS, SIDS governments, regional bodies, and global partners to advance nature-positive development efforts across SIDS.

The role of the SIDS Coalition Coordinator is strictly technical, coordination-focused, and facilitative in nature. The incumbent does not represent SIDS Member States, AOSIS, or any intergovernmental body in political or negotiation processes. All political positions, joint statements, and advocacy stances remain the prerogative of SIDS governments and AOSIS. The Coordinator supports these processes by providing technical inputs, organizing consultations, synthesizing information, and facilitating communication among stakeholders, ensuring that all outputs are reviewed and approved by the appropriate SIDS authorities prior to external use. Specific duties include:

Duties and Responsibilities

Responsibilities supporting the wider mandate of the SIDS Coalition for Nature

- Coordinate implementation, monitoring, and follow-up of the Coalition’s work programme, including the annual update of a SIDS Nature-positive Development Roadmap, ensuring coherence with the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), 2018-2030 UNCCD Framework, Paris Agreement, the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS), and other relevant UN processes.

- Support partnership development, proposal drafting, and resource mobilization, engaging development partners, multilateral funds, and philanthropic initiatives to advance SIDS-led nature action.

- Lead coordination, operationalization, and strategic development of the SIDS Coalition for Nature as a global partnership platform.

- Serve as the primary liaison of the SIDS Coalition for Nature with AOSIS, SIDS governments, regional organizations (SPREP, CARICOM, IOC), and UN agencies, facilitating communication and ensuring timely information-sharing and coordinated action.

- Coordinate global/regional policy engagement to elevate SIDS priorities on Nature, climate, resilience, financing and sustainable development.

- Support SIDS-led advocacy in key multilateral processes (CBD, UNCCD, UNFCCC, UN Ocean Conference, SIDs relevant meetings etc.).

- Prepare analytical briefs, progress reports, position papers and policy inputs to inform intergovernmental negotiations, high-level dialogues, and advocacy regarding interconnected SIDS priorities in biodiversity and sustainable development fora on Nature, climate, resilience, financing and sustainable development.

- Ensure effective coordination with and integration of Nature and BGI into the global and regional SIDS Agenda.

- Strengthen partnerships with coalitions such as the High Ambition Coalition, Global Ocean Alliance, Ocean Panel, UNCCD-related SIDS collective action and relevant UN Decades and Initiatives.

- Organize regional/global dialogues, ministerial briefings, and technical working sessions for Coalition priorities.

- Provide technical and logistical support for planning and delivering Coalition meetings, activities, and capacity-building initiatives at national, regional, and global levels.

- Support SIDS champions in advancing integrated policy frameworks that embed NbS and nature-positive development.

Responsibilities supporting BGI-IP integration and contributions

These duties will ensure that the Coalition benefits from BGI data, lessons, partnerships, knowledge, and lessons for potential replication and scaling. Working in close coordination with the BGI Global Coordination Unit, the Coordinator will:

- Develop a multi-year Coalition Work Plan and detailed annual work plan in alignment with the BGI’s regional and global workstreams.

- Facilitate upscaling of BGI Child Project results through regional and global platforms, promoting south–south collaboration.

- Support structured SIDS–SIDS (South–South) cooperation by organizing exchanges, dialogues, and collaborative learning initiatives, in coordination with the BGI GCP and its regional partners.

- Enhance SIDS Coalition for Nature and AOSIS integration to strengthen Nature within the AOSIS agenda and leverage the AOSIS space and platform to leverage Nature and BGI.

- Represent the SIDS Coalition and BGI in global policy fora, technical panels, and donor partnership discussions.

- Engage with global SIDS knowledge networks to share BGI knowledge and lessons.

- Ensure gender equality and social inclusion considerations are embedded in all SIDS Coalition for Nature activities.

- Facilitate rapid sharing of lessons, models, and analytics across SIDS regions, in coordination with the BGI GCP and its regional partners.

- Produce and submit quarterly narrative reports to the BGI Global Programme Coordination Unit summarizing activities, results, and emerging priorities.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Partnership Management

Coalition Building

Ability to build, maintain, and mobilize multi-country coalitions and strategic alliances

Public Policy

Policy Advocacy

Ability to influence policy positions, draft statements, and support intergovernmental negotiation.

Nature, Climate & Energy

SIDS Technical Expertise

Understanding of SIDS development challenges, nature-positive strategies, and NbS policy frameworks.

Business Development

Resource Mobilization

Ability to identify and engage donors to attract financing for SIDS collective actions.

Knowledge Generation

Knowledge Synthesis

Ability to capture, package and disseminate lessons, evidence, and analytics for policy uptake.

Communications

Strategic Positioning

Ability to craft clear messaging, talking points, and briefs for high-level SIDS advocacy.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Advanced university degree (Master’s level or equivalent) in international relations, public policy, environmental policy, development studies, economics or related fields.

A Bachelor’s degree with two additional years of experience may be accepted.

Experience:

Minimum 5 years (with Master’s) or 7 years (with Bachelor’s) of progressively responsible experience in international policy coordination, SIDS/global negotiations, coalition management, environmental diplomacy, or nature/climate governance.

Required Skills:

- Demonstrated experience working with SIDS governments, AOSIS, regional organizations, or multilateral platforms/organizations.

- Experience coordinating coalitions, networks, or multi-country initiatives.

- Strong understanding of nature, climate, blue/green economy, and SIDS-related policy frameworks.

- Experience drafting policy briefs, joint communiqués, and technical advisories.

- Experience coordinating high-level events, dialogues, or multilateral negotiation spaces.

- Excellent communication, strategic advisory, and diplomacy skills.

Desired Skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Experience working with SIDS regional bodies (CARICOM, SPREP, IOC, others), global bodies (AOSIS, others), or UN Agencies (UNDP, UNDESA, others).

- Experience in intergovernmental negotiating processes (UNFCCC, CBD, UNGA, SIDS conferences).

- Knowledge of SIDS financing mechanisms and global environmental funds.

- Working knowledge of French or Spanish is an advantage.

Institutional Arrangement

The SIDS Coalition Coordinator will report administratively to the BGI Global Coordinator given the use of BGI funding to support this position. However, the Coordinator will closely collaborate and coordinate with the SCN Leadership who will set strategic and programmatic priorities for the position. The SCN co-Chairs, BGI Global Coordinator, the UNDESA SIDS Unit Chief and the Coalition Coordinator will periodically meet to align BGI and UNDESA support with Coalition priorities.

In addition, the position will work closely with SCN & AOSIS country representatives and focal points, regional and other partners. S/he will also maintain collaboration with BGI GEF Agencies and other partners relevant to global SIDS coordination processes and BGI implementation.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.
